candidates.ai_feasibility: medium — needs prose plus metrical notes; phonetic descriptions require a linguist's check
candidates.pilot_unit: Preface + De litteris (c. 280 verses, estimate)

candidates.title: Commenta Bernensia & Adnotationes super Lucanum — scholia on Lucan; Бернские комментарии и «Примечания к Лукану». Proposed unit: Commenta Bernensia on Book 1
candidates.author: Anonymous
candidates.date: Compiled 9th–10th c. from late antique material
candidates.size: Usener 1869; Endt 1909; est. 150k words combined (estimate)
candidates.edition: Usener, Teubner 1869; Endt, Teubner 1909 (both public domain); Cavajoni supplements 1979–90
candidates.ru_evidence: No translation found; not in the ancientrome.ru catalogue
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia lists no translations; none found in searches
candidates.other_translations: None found
candidates.value: Explain Lucan's history, geography, astronomy and Stoic ideas, partly from late antique sources. Important for Lucan studies and the medieval reception of the civil wars
candidates.ai_feasibility: high — short notes
candidates.pilot_unit: Commenta Bernensia on Book 1 (est. 10–12k words)

candidates.title: Calcidius, Commentarius in Platonis Timaeum — Commentary on Plato's Timaeus; Калкидий, «Комментарий к Тимею» (RU-gap). Proposed unit: chapters on fate
candidates.author: Calcidius
candidates.size: 355 chapters; est. 70–80k words (estimate)
candidates.edition: Wrobel 1876 (public domain); Waszink, Plato Latinus IV 1962 (copyright)
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Халкидий' lists no translation, only Petrova's encyclopedia article (2008)
candidates.en_evidence: J. Magee, On Plato's Timaeus, Dumbarton Oaks Medieval Library 41 (2016)
candidates.other_translations: French (Bakhouche), mentioned on en.wikipedia
candidates.value: Main channel of Platonism to the Latin West until the 12th c.: cosmology, matter, demons, fate. For historians of philosophy and science
candidates.ai_feasibility: high — technical but lucid prose
candidates.pilot_unit: Chapters on fate and providence (c. chs. 142–190; est. 12k words)

candidates.title: Fulgentius, Expositio Virgilianae continentiae — Exposition of the Content of Vergil; Фульгенций, «Изъяснение содержания Вергилия» (RU-gap)
candidates.author: Fabius Planciades Fulgentius
candidates.size: c. 20 Teubner pp.; est. 7–8k words (estimate)
candidates.edition: Helm, Teubner 1898 (public domain)
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia lists Russian only for the Mitologiae (Гусейнов 1988; Можелян 2012/2014; Болгов 2015–16); nothing for this work or the Expositio sermonum antiquorum
candidates.en_evidence: Whitbread, Fulgentius the Mythographer (1971); also McVeigh, Hardison (search results)
candidates.other_translations: French: É. Wolff, Virgile dévoilé (2009)
candidates.value: Reads the Aeneid as the stages of human life, with Vergil himself appearing as interpreter. A bridge to medieval allegory; short and vivid, so a good fast pilot
candidates.ai_feasibility: high — short; ornate, mannered Latin needs care
candidates.pilot_unit: Whole work (~7–8k words)

sweep:latin-scholia.ru_gap_notes: These texts exist in English but have no Russian translation, or only scraps. Varro's De lingua Latina V–VII (Kent, Loeb 1938; de Melo, OUP 2019) has only excerpts from VIII–X in Russian. Calcidius on the Timaeus (Magee, DOML 41) has none. Fulgentius' Expositio Virgilianae continentiae and Expositio sermonum antiquorum (Whitbread 1971) have none. Servius on Aeneid 4 (Bolchazy-Carducci 2002) has none; Russian covers only Aeneid 1 excerpts. Several works of Boethius are in English but missing from Russian bibliographies: In Ciceronis Topica and De topicis differentiis (Stump 1988/1978), De divisione (Magee 1998), and the De interpretatione commentary, chapters 1–6 and 9 (Ancient Commentators on Aristotle). The Bobbio scholia exist in English excerpts (attalus.org) with no Russian. Asconius is no longer a gap: a full Russian translation appeared in 2026 (Khrustalev).

sweep:greek-lexica.corpus_overview: I surveyed about 30 Greek lexica, grammars, metrical treatises, proverb collections and learned compilations. Russian is almost empty. Only Athenaeus has a complete Russian translation (Golinkevich, Наука 2003 and 2010), along with Aelian's Varia historia (Polyakova 1963). A Russian Photius Bibliotheca is under way (Vasilik, vol. 1, 2024; earlier fragments by Freiberg 1969). Everything else has no Russian at all or only small excerpts: Pollux (one 2022 article), Stephanus (letter E only, 2003), Stobaeus (IV.7, 2018), Aelian's De natura animalium (about 30 pp. of excerpts), and the Suda (more than 100 entries by Maxim the Greek, 16th c.). Complete English translations exist for the Suda (31,000+ entries, SOL 2014), Harpocration (1,247 entries, CC BY 4.0), Aelian NA (Loeb), Athenaeus, Hephaestion (1987) and Apollonius' Syntax (1981). English is partial for Photius' Bibliotheca, Stephanus (a few entries on ToposText), the Atticist lexica (selected entries on atticism.eu) and Stobaeus. I found no translation into any modern language of Pollux (confirmed by Bristol, 2024), Hesychius (about 51k glosses), Photius' Lexicon, the Etymologica, Ps.-Zonaras, Orion, Orus, Choeroboscus, Herodian, Ammonius or Erotian, nor of Stobaeus as a whole. The only complete non-English versions are Stephanus (German, Billerbeck 2006–17), Zenobius with Diogenianus (Italian, Lelli 2006) and Timaeus (French, Bonelli 2007). Pure glossaries (Hesychius, the Etymologica, Photius' Lexicon) are poor targets for continuous translation and suit thematic dossiers better. The best value for effort is in discursive compilations (Pollux, Zenobius, Stephanus, Stobaeus) and in RU-gap texts that have open English versions for cross-checking (Suda, Harpocration).

candidates.title: Ὀνομαστικόν / Onomasticon / «Ономастикон»; unit: Book 8 (law courts, laws, magistracies)
candidates.author: Julius Pollux (Ioulios Polydeukes) of Naucratis
candidates.genre: Thematic onomastic lexicon / thesaurus of realia
candidates.size: 10 books (epitomized). Bethe's edition is about 550 Teubner pp. Estimate: more than 100k Greek words.
candidates.edition: E. Bethe, Lexicographi Graeci IX (Teubner 1900–37; Bethe died 1940, so public domain in most jurisdictions). Bekker 1846 (PD). Both scanned on archive.org.
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Юлий Поллукс) lists no translation. Only tiny excerpts: Onom. 3.149–155 (Yanzina & Korneev, Индоевроп. языкознание и класс. филология 26, 2022, doi 10.30842/ielcp230690152678) and 9.83 in ФРГФ (1989).
candidates.en_evidence: Jean Golding Institute, Bristol (Aug 2024): 'not translated into any modern language'. Naomi Scott's crowdsourcing project is only at prototype stage. Only extracts on theatre and masks exist (1775; modern Book 4 excerpts).
candidates.other_translations: No complete translation in any modern language. Only articles on single passages (e.g. Polish, 2021, Book 4 medical terms). Latin 1502.
candidates.value: Unique thesaurus of Greek life: cult, theatre, music, law, money, crafts, the body, games. Quotes lost comedy and Attic prose. Cited constantly by historians of Athenian institutions, theatre and daily life, yet never translated. Absolute flagship for Neoscholia.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium-high: list-like Attic vocabulary suits LLMs. Synonym clusters, the epitomized and corrupt text and identifying quotations need expert review, which suits multi-model cross-critique.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book 8 (Athenian courts, laws, archons, the constitution). Estimate 10–12k Greek words. Alternatives: Book 9 (city, coins, games) or Book 4 (music, theatre).

candidates.title: Ἐπιτομὴ τῶν Ταρραίου καὶ Διδύμου παροιμιῶν / Zenobius' Epitome of Proverbs (vulgate, CPG I) / «Собрание пословиц» Зенобия
candidates.author: Zenobius, sophist (epitomizing Didymus and Lucillus of Tarrha)
candidates.genre: Paroemiography: proverbs with explanations and aitia
candidates.size: 552 proverbs in six 'centuries' (CPG I pp. 1–175). Estimate about 25k words. The Athos recension adds material.
candidates.edition: Leutsch & Schneidewin, Corpus Paroemiographorum Graecorum I (Göttingen 1839; PD, archive.org). W. Bühler, Zenobii Athoi proverbia (1982–99; partial, in copyright).
candidates.ru_evidence: No ru.wikipedia article on Zenobius and no translation listed. Searches find only isolated proverbs quoted in other articles (e.g. 'Спорить о тени осла').
candidates.en_evidence: No English translation found (en.wikipedia 'Zenobius', OpenAlex). Proverbs are treated only piecemeal in commentaries.
candidates.other_translations: Italian complete: E. Lelli, I proverbi greci. Le raccolte di Zenobio e Diogeniano (2006); also Lelli (ed.), Proverbi, sentenze e massime (Bompiani 2021). Portuguese partial (Revista Hypnos, 2025).
candidates.value: Proverbs explained through myth, local history, lost comedy and Didymus' scholarship. Rich in folklore, religion and ethnography; source of Erasmus' Adagia. Readable for a broad public and ideal to show off commentary. Could be extended to Diogenianus and Ps.-Plutarch.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: short self-contained prose entries. Commentary must trace sources (Didymus, comic fragments) and parallels in Diogenianus and the Suda. Lelli's Italian can serve for cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Centuries I–II (proverbs 1.1–2.100, 200 entries; estimate 8–9k words).

candidates.title: Ἐθνικά / Ethnica / «Этника»; unit: entries on Hellenistic city foundations (Alexandreiai, Antiocheiai, Seleukeiai…)
candidates.author: Stephanus of Byzantium (surviving in an epitome, traditionally Hermolaus')
candidates.genre: Geographical-grammatical lexicon of place names and ethnic adjectives
candidates.size: Epitome of 60 books. Meineke's edition is about 715 pp. Estimate: over 3,000 entries.
candidates.edition: A. Meineke 1849 (PD). M. Billerbeck et al., CFHB 43/1–5 (2006–2017, Greek with German translation; in copyright).
candidates.ru_evidence: Only letter E (M. M. Kholod, Клио 2(21), 2003; online at vostlit.info) and Pontic/Caucasian excerpts in Latyshev's collection. No complete Russian translation.
candidates.en_evidence: ToposText work 241: 'A few entries… have been translated by Brady Kiesling'; the rest is Greek only. No complete English translation found.
candidates.other_translations: German complete (Billerbeck, 2006–2017). Latin 1678.
candidates.value: Preserves thousands of fragments of lost historians and geographers (Hecataeus, Theopompus, Alexander Polyhistor). Key for historical geography, ethnography, epigraphy and Hellenistic foundations; the Alexander material fits the editor's expertise.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: formulaic entries are easy. Morphology of ethnic forms, corrupt quotations and source identification need an expert. Billerbeck's German is an ideal cross-check.
candidates.pilot_unit: About 40 entries on Alexandreia, Antiocheia, Seleukeia, Apameia, Laodikeia, etc. (estimate 5k words). Alternative: the whole of letter Δ.

candidates.title: Ἀνθολόγιον / Anthology (Eclogae and Florilegium) / «Антология» Стобея; unit: Book IV, chs. 22–25 (marriage, household, children)
candidates.author: Ioannes Stobaeus
candidates.language: Ancient Greek (prose and verse excerpts in many dialects)
candidates.size: 4 books; Wachsmuth–Hense 5 vols (about 2,500 pp.). Unit estimate 15–20k words.
candidates.edition: C. Wachsmuth & O. Hense, Berlin 1884–1912 (PD; archive.org).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Стобей): 'не переведена ни на один современный язык'. Only Anth. IV.7 (Наставления о царской власти, Исторический вестник 26, 2018, pp. 280–306) and scattered fragments in collections.
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia (Stobaeus): 'The entire work has not been translated into any modern language'. Only excerpted authors are translated (Hermetica, Arius Didymus, Pythagorean pseudepigrapha).
candidates.other_translations: No complete translation. Partial versions only within editions of the source authors.
candidates.value: Preserves hundreds of otherwise lost texts: tragedy, comedy, Presocratics, Stoics, Hierocles, Pythagorean treatises. Read as whole chapters, it shows late-antique thematic ethics. Valuable for history of philosophy, gender and the family.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium-high: many short excerpts. Verse fragments, Doric pseudepigrapha, attribution and textual problems need expert review.
candidates.pilot_unit: IV.22 Περὶ γάμου (On marriage). Estimate 8–10k words.

candidates.title: Σοῦδα / Suda / «Суда» (Свида); unit: biographical entries on Greek poets (from Hesychius' Onomatologos)
candidates.author: Anonymous Byzantine compilers
candidates.size: 31,000+ entries (Adler, 5 vols). Unit estimate several hundred entries, 15–40k words.
candidates.edition: A. Adler, Lexicographi Graeci I (1928–38; Adler died 1966, so likely in copyright in RU/EU). Bernhardy 1834–53 (PD).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Суда): only 'более ста статей' rendered by Maxim the Greek (16th c.). No modern Russian translation found; only scattered excerpts.
candidates.en_evidence: Suda On Line: the last of 31,000+ entries was translated on 21 July 2014 (SOL history page; en.wikipedia).
candidates.other_translations: Latin 1581. No other complete modern translation found.
candidates.value: Main ancient source for the lives and work lists of Greek authors, much of it now lost. Indispensable to every Hellenist. A Russian version of the bio-bibliographical entries would serve all Russian classicists and students. RU-gap flagship.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high for prose biographies; medium where entries quote fragments. SOL is available for cross-checking, not as a base.
candidates.pilot_unit: Lives of the lyric, tragic and comic poets (about 150 entries; estimate 15k words).

candidates.title: Περὶ ζῴων ἰδιότητος / De natura animalium (On the Characteristics of Animals) / «О природе животных»
candidates.author: Claudius Aelianus
candidates.size: 17 books, about 900+ short chapters (estimate). Loeb runs to 3 vols.
candidates.edition: R. Hercher (Teubner 1864–66; PD). García Valdés et al. (Teubner 2009; in copyright).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Клавдий Элиан) lists only excerpts: Polyakova 1961 (pp. 532–540), Gasparov 1964 (pp. 285–296), Taronyan 2007 (pp. 260–264), Aleksanyan (XI 10–11).
candidates.en_evidence: Loeb, A. F. Scholfield, LCL 446, 448, 449 (listed on ru.wikipedia).
candidates.other_translations: Reported but not re-verified here: Spanish (Gredos, 1984), Italian (BUR, Maspero 1998), French (Zucker, 2001–02).
candidates.value: The richest ancient collection of animal lore: zoology, Egyptian and Indian marvels, moral exempla; source for the Physiologus and bestiaries. Used in history of science, religion and animal studies. Very readable. RU-gap.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: simple narrative prose. Commentary needs zoological identification and source tracing (Aristotle, Ctesias, Megasthenes).
candidates.pilot_unit: Book 1 (60 chapters; estimate 7k words) or Book 16 (Indian and eastern animals).

candidates.title: Λέξεις τῶν δέκα ῥητόρων / Lexicon of the Ten Orators / «Лексикон десяти ораторов»
candidates.author: Valerius Harpocration
candidates.genre: Special lexicon on the Attic orators (law, institutions, prosopography)
candidates.size: 1,247 entries (Harpokration On Line count). Estimate 30–35k words.
candidates.edition: W. Dindorf 1853 (PD). J. J. Keaney 1991 (in copyright).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Валерий Гарпократион) lists no translation. Searches in Russian found none.
candidates.en_evidence: Harpokration On Line (Duke DC3, Sosin et al.): all 1,247 entries translated, licensed CC BY 4.0. The complete draft was announced in 2016.
candidates.other_translations: None found.
candidates.value: Key for Attic oratory, Athenian law and institutions, and prosopography. Preserves fragments of the Atthidographers and Aristotle's Ath. Pol. Essential for Russian historians of Athens and translators of the orators. RU-gap; the open English allows transparent cross-checking.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: short factual entries; the CC BY English is available for comparison. Commentary should link each entry to the orators' passages.
candidates.pilot_unit: Legal and institutional entries in letters Α–Δ (about 300 entries; estimate 8k words).

candidates.title: Περὶ ὁμοίων καὶ διαφόρων λέξεων / De adfinium vocabulorum differentia (On Differences of Similar Words) / «О различии близких слов»
candidates.author: 'Ammonius' (perhaps reworking Herennius Philo of Byblos)
candidates.size: About 500 entries (estimate). Nickau's text is about 136 pp. Estimate 15k words.
candidates.edition: K. Nickau (Teubner 1966; in copyright). Valckenaer 1739/1822 (PD).
candidates.ru_evidence: No ru.wikipedia article and no Russian translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia (Ammonius Grammaticus) lists none. OpenAlex returns only reviews of Nickau's edition. No English translation found.
candidates.other_translations: None found (search not exhaustive).
candidates.value: Ancient semantics through distinctions such as βίος/ζωή, famous via Agamben, and many others. Preserves Didymus and Tryphon. Useful for lexical semantics, NT and philosophy readers, and Greek teaching. Can be translated in full.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: compact, structured entries. Nuances between near-synonyms need careful bilingual rendering, and a reviewer must check each distinction.
candidates.pilot_unit: Entire text, or letters Α–Ε as the pilot (estimate 4k words).

candidates.title: Ἐκλογὴ ῥημάτων καὶ ὀνομάτων Ἀττικῶν / Ecloga (Selection of Attic Words) / «Эклога»; optional cluster with Moeris, Aelius Dionysius, Pausanias and the Antiatticist
candidates.author: Phrynichus Arabius of Bithynia
candidates.size: About 400+ entries (estimate); estimate 12k words.
candidates.edition: E. Fischer (de Gruyter 1974; in copyright). Lobeck 1820 and Rutherford, The New Phrynichus 1881 (PD).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Фриних' is only a disambiguation page (no grammarian). No Russian translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: The PURA Digital Encyclopedia of Atticism (atticism.eu) entries include English translations of selected glosses. Rutherford 1881 is a commentary. No complete translation found.
candidates.other_translations: None complete found.
candidates.value: Central document of ancient language purism (Attic versus Koine) and Second Sophistic identity. Used by linguists, Koine and NT scholars, and teachers of Greek prose. Pairs with current ERC research.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium-high: needs linguistic precision about forms; atticism.eu serves as a cross-check.
candidates.pilot_unit: Whole Ecloga, or the first 100 entries (estimate 3k words).

candidates.title: Ἐγχειρίδιον περὶ μέτρων / Enchiridion (Handbook on Metres), with Περὶ ποιήματος / «Энхиридион о метрах»
candidates.author: Hephaestion of Alexandria
candidates.size: Consbruch pp. 1–73 (estimate 10–12k words). Scholia and Choeroboscus' commentary add about 300 pp.
candidates.edition: M. Consbruch, Hephaestionis Enchiridion cum commentariis veteribus (Teubner 1906; PD).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Гефестион (грамматик)) lists only the English translation. No Russian translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: J. M. van Ophuijsen, Hephaestion on Metre (Mnemosyne Suppl. 100, 1987); cited on ru.wikipedia.
candidates.other_translations: None found.
candidates.value: The only complete ancient Greek metrical handbook. A source for Sappho, Alcaeus and Anacreon fragments and the basis of metrical terminology. Useful for Russian teaching of Greek verse. RU-gap.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: LLMs make scansion errors, so an expert metrician must review. Notation needs standardizing.
candidates.pilot_unit: Whole Enchiridion (estimate 10–12k words).

candidates.title: Περὶ συνδέσμων / On Conjunctions (alternative: Περὶ συντάξεως Book I) / «О союзах»
candidates.author: Apollonius Dyscolus
candidates.size: Conjunctions about 45 Teubner pp. (estimate 10k words). Syntax is 4 books, about 500 pp.
candidates.edition: R. Schneider, GG II.1 (1878; PD). G. Uhlig, GG II.2 (1910; PD).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Аполлоний Дискол) lists only studies (Dobiash 1882; Polikarpov 2007), no translation.
candidates.en_evidence: Syntax: Householder 1981 (standard bibliography). De pronomine pars generalis with English translation (Schmidhauser PhD 2007, per en.wikipedia). No English found for Conjunctions.
candidates.other_translations: From standard bibliography, not re-verified: French, Syntax (Lallot 1997) and Conjunctions (Dalimier 2001); Spanish, Syntax (Gredos 1987).
candidates.value: Founding work of Western syntax, behind Priscian and Byzantine grammar. Russian linguists and historians of linguistics lack direct access.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: dense technical argument, corrupt text, and terminology that must stay consistent. A strong test for multi-model review.
candidates.pilot_unit: De coniunctionibus, complete (estimate 10k words).

candidates.title: Τῶν παρ' Ἱπποκράτει λέξεων συναγωγή / Glossary of Hippocratic Words / «Собрание гиппократовских слов»
candidates.author: Erotian (Erotianus)
candidates.date: c. 60s CE (dedicated to Nero's physician Andromachus)
candidates.size: About 100 pp. in Nachmanson's edition (estimate 10–12k words).
candidates.edition: E. Nachmanson, Erotiani Vocum Hippocraticarum collectio (Uppsala 1918; PD).
candidates.ru_evidence: No ru.wikipedia article. Listed without any translation in the ru.wikipedia list of surviving Greek works. None found.
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia (Erotianus) lists none. OpenAlex search found none.
candidates.other_translations: None found (search not exhaustive).
candidates.value: The earliest list of Hippocratic works, plus Hellenistic medical lexicography (fragments of Bacchius and Glaucias). Important for history of medicine and of the Hippocratic text.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium-high: short glosses; identifying the Hippocratic passages needs expert checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Preface with the list of works, plus letters Α–Γ (estimate 3k words).

candidates.title: Λέξεις Πλατωνικαί / Lexicon Platonicum / «Платоновский лексикон»
candidates.author: Timaeus the Sophist
candidates.size: 468 entries (en.wikipedia); estimate 5–6k words.
candidates.edition: Ruhnken 1754/1789; Koch 1828 (PD). M. Bonelli 2007 (Brill; in copyright).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Тимей (греческий грамматик)) lists no translation. None found.
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia lists only Bonelli's French. No English found.
candidates.other_translations: French: M. Bonelli, Timée le Sophiste. Lexique platonicien (Brill 2007).
candidates.value: Ancient Platonic philology and Attic usage; the reception of Plato in the Imperial period. A natural fit for the Russian Platonic studies community. Small enough to finish quickly.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: brief glosses; Bonelli's French is available for cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Entire lexicon (468 entries).

candidates.title: Καινὴ ἱστορία / New History (for Polymaths) / «Новая история» (Photius, Bibliotheca cod. 190)
candidates.author: Ptolemy Chennus (Ptolemy Hephaestion)
candidates.size: Survives only in Photius' summary (Westermann 1843 pp. 182–192). Estimate 5–6k words.
candidates.edition: A. Westermann 1843 (PD). R. Henry, Photius Bibliothèque III (Budé 1962).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Птолемей Хенн): only excerpts (Latyshev, ВДИ 1947 №4, pp. 277–278) plus a content paraphrase. Vasilik's new Russian Photius (vol. 1, 2024) may later include it.
candidates.en_evidence: tertullian.org has only an English rendering of Henry's French (indirect), cited on en.wikipedia.
candidates.other_translations: French (Henry, Budé 1962).
candidates.value: A parody of Alexandrian scholarship and a showcase of invented sources and myths. Excellent for a commentary that exposes the fakery. Short and attractive to general readers.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: narrative summary. The commentary must check the alleged sources.
candidates.pilot_unit: Whole of cod. 190 (books 1–7 summary).

sweep:greek-lexica.ru_gap_notes: These texts have English (or other modern) translations but no Russian one. Suda: complete on Suda On Line (2014); in Russian only Maxim the Greek's 100+ entries. Harpocration: Harpokration On Line, all 1,247 entries, CC BY 4.0. Aelian, De natura animalium: Loeb; in Russian only about 30 pp. of excerpts. Hephaestion's Enchiridion: van Ophuijsen 1987. Apollonius Dyscolus' Syntax: Householder 1981. Lexicon Rhetoricum Cantabrigiense: English online by D. Avilés (SFU Nomoi). Stephanus: complete German (Billerbeck), but only letter E in Russian. Photius' Bibliotheca: partial English (Freese 1920, Wilson 1994) and a Russian translation in progress (Vasilik, vol. 1, 2024), so check its coverage before investing. The open-licensed English versions (Harpocration, SOL) can be cross-checked transparently.

sweep:greek-scholia.corpus_overview:
I surveyed about 25 corpora. Web-search budget ran out midway, so some checks rely on catalogue pages fetched directly (ancientrome.ru, ru/en-Wikipedia, BMCR, the Hellenistic Bibliography, ToposText, Canopos).

RUSSIAN: I found no translation of any major Greek scholia corpus (Homer, Hesiod, Pindar, the tragedians, Aristophanes, Apollonius, Aratus, Theocritus, Nicander, Lycophron) and no translation of Eustathius' commentaries. Ru-wiki 'Схолии' notes that scholia are usually left untranslated. Russian translations exist only for allegorical and mythographic treatises: Cornutus (Poznev 1999), Palaephatus (1791; Yarkho), Heraclitus Paradoxographus and the Vatican Anonymous (Yarkho), Proclus' essay on myths (Petrov). There are also the hypotheses of Aristophanes of Byzantium (Torshilov), 8 pp. of Tzetzes excerpts (1969), and a draft of Tzetzes' Carmina Iliaca (Smyka, online).

ENGLISH: Complete translations exist only for Tzetzes' Allegories (DOML 2015/2019) and Chiliades (online 2015). Partial: Iliad scholia (CUP vol. 1, Books 1–2, 2025); Eustathius on Odyssey 1–8 (Brill 2022–23); Eustathius on the Iliad (preface only, 2002); D-scholia mythological narratives (2023/2026, CC); Euripides' Orestes scholia (online); an unvetted ChatGPT draft of Tzetzes on Lycophron (ToposText).

OTHER LANGUAGES: French has Pindar O.1–2 (2013, 2020; 17 volumes projected), Apollonius (2010), and Aristophanes' Frogs/Plutus. Italian has the Aeschylus and Hesiod scholia (2009). A German edition and translation of the Pindar scholia is in progress (Fribourg).

ESTIMATE: well under 10% of the corpus exists in any modern language, and close to 0% in Russian.

candidates.title: Scholia vetera in Pindari carmina: Pythian odes / Old scholia on Pindar's Pythians / Схолии к Пифийским одам Пиндара
candidates.author: Anonymous; Alexandrian and Roman-era material (Aristarchus, Didymus etc.)
candidates.date: Sources 3rd c. BCE–2nd c. CE; transmitted in Byzantine MSS
candidates.size: Whole corpus: Drachmann's 3 vols (est. ~1,000 Teubner pp.). Pythian scholia: vol. II (1910), est. ~250 pp.
candidates.edition: Drachmann, Teubner 1903–27. Public domain (PD): Drachmann died 1935. Boeckh 1811–19 also PD, scan at archive.org/details/pindaroutasozome01pinduoft. A new Fribourg edition is in progress.
candidates.ru_evidence: Russian search ('схолии к Пиндару перевод') found only Starikovsky's translation of the odes themselves (HSE 2025); its commentary only cites scholia. Ancientrome.ru Pindar page: only Gasparov's translation of the odes.
candidates.en_evidence: BMCR 2010.08.39 and 2014.12.27: the Besançon French volume (2013) is the first translation of the O.1 scholia into any modern language. No English translation is mentioned.
candidates.other_translations: French: Daude et al., Scholies à Pindare I (Lives + O.1, 2013) and II (O.2, 2020). Italian: metrical scholia (Martino 1999). German: Fribourg edition with translation in progress (Isthmians/Nemeans first).
candidates.value: The main ancient source for Pindar's occasions, victors, chronology and myth variants. Preserves Aristarchus, Didymus and lost historians and poets. It pairs directly with the new Russian Pythians (HSE 2025), which gives an immediate Russian readership. An emblematic 'old scholia + new scholia' series for Neoscholia.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium-high. Terse lemmatised Greek with abbreviations, metrical and grammatical jargon, and embedded fragments. LLMs parse it well, but every quotation and source attribution needs checking against Drachmann's apparatus.
candidates.pilot_unit: Scholia to Pythian 1 (Hieron, Etna); est. ~30 Drachmann pp., ~10k words. Pythian 4 is an alternative.

candidates.title: Scholia in Homeri Iliadem (A, bT, D): unit Book 6 / Scholia to the Iliad / Схолии к «Илиаде», песнь VI
candidates.author: Anonymous compilers. Sources: Aristonicus, Didymus, Herodian and Nicanor (the 'four-man commentary' in the A scholia), the exegetical tradition, Porphyry, and the Mythographus Homericus (D)
candidates.date: Hellenistic to late antique sources; Venetus A is 10th c.
candidates.genre: Scholia (textual criticism, grammar, literary criticism, mythography)
candidates.size: Erbse: 5 text vols, plus the D-scholia (van Thiel). Book 6 (A+bT+D): est. 15–20k words.
candidates.edition: Erbse 1969–88 (de Gruyter, in copyright). PD: Dindorf 1875–77 and Maass 1887–88. D-scholia: van Thiel 2014, open access (kups.ub.uni-koeln.de/5586).
candidates.ru_evidence: Russian search for scholia translations to the Iliad found none. Ru-wiki 'Схолии' says scholia are generally not translated into modern languages.
candidates.en_evidence: Beck et al., The Ancient Scholia to Homer's Iliad: A Translation, vol. 1 (Books 1–2), CUP 2025; further volumes pending. The D-scholia's mythological narratives only: Smith et al. 2023, CC BY (ToposText 866).
candidates.other_translations: None found for the full corpus.
candidates.value: The richest body of ancient literary and textual criticism, carrying the Alexandrian editors' readings. Indispensable for Homeric studies and the history of philology. The most emblematic text for a 'Neoscholia' platform.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. Critical signs, Herodian's accentuation notes and Aristarchean terminology need a glossary, and source layers must stay labelled. The exegetical bT notes are easy. Base the work on the PD and open texts, since Erbse is in copyright.
candidates.pilot_unit: All scholia to Iliad 6 (Glaucus–Diomedes, Hector–Andromache); est. 15–20k words. Not yet covered by the CUP translation.

candidates.title: Scholia vetera in Apollonium Rhodium: unit Book 2 / Scholia to the Argonautica / Схолии к «Аргонавтике» Аполлония Родосского
candidates.author: Anonymous; per the subscription, derived from Lucillus of Tarrha, Sophocleus and Theon
candidates.date: 1st c. BCE–2nd c. CE sources; MSS 10th c.+
candidates.size: Wendel: xxvi + 401 pp. (est. ~140k words). Book 2: est. ~30k words.
candidates.edition: Wendel 1935 (Weidmann). Wendel died 1951, so PD in RU/EU; US status needs checking. Keil 1854 (in Merkel's edition) is PD.
candidates.ru_evidence: Ancientrome.ru catalogue has no Apollonius scholia. Ru-wiki 'Схолии' names them among important but untranslated corpora.
candidates.en_evidence: Cuypers' Hellenistic Bibliography lists only Lachenaud's French translation (2010), and BMCR 2014.12.27 likewise names only the French one. No English translation is listed.
candidates.other_translations: French: Lachenaud, Scholies à Apollonios de Rhodes (Belles Lettres, Fragments 9, 2010; xlv + 576 pp.).
candidates.value: A treasury of lost mythographers and historians (Pherecydes, Herodorus and others). Book 2 covers the Bosporus, the Pontic coast, the Amazons and Colchis: Black Sea ethnography of direct interest to Russian, Ukrainian and Georgian readers and archaeologists.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High-medium. Clear explanatory prose, but many toponyms and source citations, so outputs need a gazetteer (e.g., ToposText/Pleiades) and fragment cross-checks.
candidates.pilot_unit: Scholia to Book 2 (Amycus, Phineus, Symplegades, the Pontic periplus); est. ~30k words. Lines 2.1–647 (~12k words) would be a smaller pilot.

candidates.title: Ioannes Tzetzes, Commentary (scholia) on Lycophron's Alexandra / Иоанн Цец, Комментарий к «Александре» Ликофрона
candidates.author: John Tzetzes (formerly attributed to his brother Isaac), with older scholia
candidates.size: Scheer vol. II (1908): lxiv + 398 pp. (est. ~150k words).
candidates.edition: Scheer 1881/1908 (Weidmann), PD. Leone 2002 (Congedo) for the old scholia and paraphrases.
candidates.ru_evidence: Ancientrome.ru Lycophron page has Surikov's Alexandra translation and Kaukhchishvili's article on Lycophron's scholiasts, but no translation of the commentary. Ru-wiki 'Иоанн Цец' lists none.
candidates.en_evidence: ToposText work 860 carries a ChatGPT-4 machine translation of Scheer, self-described as done 'with more speed than accuracy'. There is no scholarly English translation.
candidates.other_translations: No modern translation listed in Cuypers' Hellenistic Bibliography; only Canter's Latin edition of 1601.
candidates.value: The key to the most obscure Hellenistic poem and a huge mythographic thesaurus with lost authors. It complements Surikov's Russian Alexandra. Setting a vetted multi-model translation beside the raw ChatGPT draft would showcase Neoscholia's method.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. Tzetzes' allusive Byzantine prose, polemics and dense quotations are hard. The existing machine draft offers a baseline for measurable gains from cross-model review.
candidates.pilot_unit: Tzetzes' prolegomena plus commentary on Alexandra 1–100; est. ~12k words.

candidates.title: Scholia Graeca in Odysseam: unit Book 1 / Scholia to the Odyssey / Схолии к «Одиссее», песнь I
candidates.author: Anonymous; Alexandrian, Porphyrian and Byzantine layers, plus the D-scholia
candidates.size: Dindorf: 2 vols (est. ~800 pp.). Book 1: est. 12–15k words.
candidates.edition: Pontani 2007– (Edizioni di Storia e Letteratura, in copyright). Dindorf 1855 is PD. D-scholia: Ernst 2006, open at KUPS.
candidates.ru_evidence: No Russian translation found in search or on ancientrome.ru, whose Homer page lists only translations of the poems.
candidates.en_evidence: The search found no English translation of the Pontani or Dindorf scholia. Only the D-scholia's mythological narratives are translated (Roy and Smith 2026, Canopos/ToposText 921).
candidates.other_translations: None found.
candidates.value: Far less studied than the Iliad scholia. Pontani's new edition revealed much unpublished exegesis, including Porphyry fragments. Essential for the reception of the Odyssey.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. Same technical idiom as the Iliad scholia. Pontani's text is in copyright, so either translate from Dindorf and flag divergences or ask the publisher for permission.
candidates.pilot_unit: All scholia to Odyssey 1 (Telemachy opening); est. 12–15k words.

candidates.title: Eustathius of Thessalonica, Parekbolai on the Iliad: unit Proem + Book 1 / Евстафий Солунский, Комментарий к «Илиаде»
candidates.author: Eustathius of Thessalonica
candidates.size: Van der Valk: 4 vols (est. ~3,000 pp.; ~0.8–1M words). Pilot: est. ~20k words.
candidates.edition: Van der Valk 1971–87 (Brill, in copyright). Stallbaum 1827–30 (Leipzig) is PD.
candidates.ru_evidence: Ru-wiki 'Евстафий Солунский' lists only the editions and studies (Kazhdan; Pravoslavnaya Entsiklopediya), with no translation of the commentaries.
candidates.en_evidence: English Wikipedia and the search: only the preface has been translated (Jenkins, Bachrach and Hayton, Notre Dame 2002). The Odyssey commentary, books 1–8, is in English (Cullhed and Olson, Brill 2022–23; BMCR 2023.11.38).
candidates.other_translations: Latin: Politi 1730 (Il. 1–5). No modern full translation found.
candidates.value: The summa of Byzantine Homeric learning. Preserves lost scholia, Atticist lexica and historians, and documents 12th-c. pedagogy and the reception of antiquity. A major gap in both Russian and English.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium-low. Long periods, dense intertext and etymological play. Needs aggressive source-tracing agents and expert review.
candidates.pilot_unit: Prooimion plus commentary on Iliad 1.1–100; est. ~20k words.

candidates.title: Eustathius, Commentary on Dionysius Periegetes / Евстафий Солунский, Комментарий к Дионисию Периэгету
candidates.author: Eustathius of Thessalonica
candidates.size: Est. ~200 GGM pp. (~70k words).
candidates.edition: Müller, Geographi Graeci Minores II (1861), PD. Bernhardy 1828, PD.
candidates.ru_evidence: Ru-wiki lists only Ilyushechkina's Russian translation of Dionysius himself (VDI 2005–06). Latyshev's Scythica may contain small excerpts (not verified).
candidates.en_evidence: English Wikipedia ('Eustathius of Thessalonica') lists only old editions of this commentary and no translation. Searches found none.
candidates.other_translations: None found.
candidates.value: Byzantine geography with extracts from lost geographers and historians. The Pontic and Scythian material is of direct interest to Russian readers, and the commentary pairs with the existing Russian Dionysius.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. Toponym-heavy and digressive, but syntactically easier than the Homer commentaries. Needs place-name linking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Commentary on Dionysius' Pontus and Scythia sections; est. 10–12k words.

candidates.title: Proclus' scholia (and Byzantine scholia) on Hesiod's Works and Days / Схолии Прокла к «Трудам и дням» Гесиода
candidates.author: Proclus Diadochus, with Tzetzes and Moschopoulos layers
candidates.size: Pertusi 1955: est. ~300 pp. Proclus layer: est. ~40k words.
candidates.edition: Pertusi 1955 (Vita e Pensiero, in copyright). Gaisford, Poetae Minores Graeci, is PD.
candidates.ru_evidence: Ancientrome.ru Hesiod page lists only the poems (Veresaev, Tsybenko). No Russian translation of the scholia found.
candidates.en_evidence: None found; exhaustive search was not possible. BMCR 2014.12.27 names only an Italian translation of the Hesiod scholia.
candidates.other_translations: Italian: Cassanmagnago 2009, all Hesiod scholia (Bompiani; per BMCR 2014). German: Marzillo 2010, Proclus' fragments (from bibliographic knowledge, not re-verified).
candidates.value: A Neoplatonist's ethical and allegorical reading of Hesiod. Preserves Plutarch's lost Works and Days commentary and agrarian and calendar lore. Valuable for philosophers and for the reception of Hesiod.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High-medium. Clear expository prose; separating the Proclan, Plutarchan and Byzantine layers needs an expert.
candidates.pilot_unit: Prolegomena plus scholia on Works and Days 1–201 (Prometheus, Pandora, Ages); est. ~12k words.

candidates.title: Eustathius, Prooemium to the Pindar Commentary / Евстафий Солунский, Предисловие к комментарию на Пиндара
candidates.author: Eustathius of Thessalonica
candidates.size: 38 chapters, est. ~20 Teubner pp. (~8k words).
candidates.edition: Printed in Drachmann, Scholia vetera III (1927), pp. ~285ff., PD. Tafel 1832 PD. Kambylis 1991 (in copyright).
candidates.ru_evidence: No Russian translation listed in ru-wiki or ancientrome.ru, and Russian searches found none.
candidates.en_evidence: English Wikipedia lists only the Tafel 1832 and Schneidewin 1837 editions. No English translation found.
candidates.other_translations: German: Kambylis 1991. Italian: Negri 2000. Both from bibliographic knowledge, not re-verified online.
candidates.value: The only surviving part of Eustathius' Pindar commentary: a Byzantine theory of lyric, the life of Pindar and anecdotes (e.g., Pan singing Pindar's paean). A small, self-contained opener for a Pindar series.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Short and coherent, so the whole text can be multi-reviewed. The Atticizing style needs care.
candidates.pilot_unit: The whole text (~8k words).

candidates.title: Scholia vetera and Tzetzes on Aristophanes' Clouds / Схолии к «Облакам» Аристофана
candidates.author: Anonymous (Alexandrian sources, Symmachus); John Tzetzes
candidates.size: Clouds scholia (vetera + Tzetzes): est. ~60–80k words. Pilot: est. ~10k words.
candidates.edition: Holwerda 1977 and Koster 1960 (Groningen; in copyright). Dübner 1842 (Didot) is PD.
candidates.ru_evidence: Ancientrome.ru Aristophanes page has the comedies only. Torshilov's translation of the hypotheses of Aristophanes of Byzantium is not of the scholia.
candidates.en_evidence: Rutherford 1896–1905 covers the Ravenna scholia; English Wikipedia confirms the edition, while its English rendering comes from the title and was not re-verified. No modern English translation found.
candidates.other_translations: French: Chantry, scholia to Frogs and Plutus (2009–10; BMCR 2014.12.27).
candidates.value: Key evidence for Old Comedy staging, Athenian prosopography (komodoumenoi), lost comic fragments and the reception of Socrates. Tzetzes adds a Byzantine schoolroom voice.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. Puns, proper names and Attic legal and cultic terms need specialist review.
candidates.pilot_unit: Scholia to Clouds 1–262 (Strepsiades, the phrontisterion); est. ~10k words.

candidates.title: Scholia vetera in Aratum / Scholia to Aratus' Phaenomena / Схолии к «Явлениям» Арата
candidates.author: Anonymous (drawing on Eratosthenes, Hipparchus and Stoic sources)
candidates.size: Martin: xxxvii + 595 pp. (est. ~150k words).
candidates.edition: Martin 1974 (Teubner, in copyright). Maass, Commentariorum in Aratum reliquiae (1898), is PD.
candidates.ru_evidence: No entry on ancientrome.ru and nothing in the ru-wiki listings. No Russian translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: Cuypers' Hellenistic Bibliography, 'Aratus and Aratea', lists only Martin's edition and studies, with no translation of the scholia.
candidates.other_translations: None listed.
candidates.value: Ancient astronomy, constellation myths, meteorology and doxography (Mansfeld); a bridge to Eratosthenes' Catasterisms and the Latin Aratea. Appeals to historians of science and a wide readership.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. Technical astronomy needs diagrams and expert review; otherwise straightforward explanatory prose.
candidates.pilot_unit: Scholia on Phaenomena 1–136 (proem, the Dike myth); est. ~12k words.

candidates.title: Scholia on Euripides' Phoenissae / Схолии к «Финикиянкам» Еврипида
candidates.author: Anonymous; ancient and Byzantine (Moschopoulos, Thomas Magister) layers
candidates.size: Phoenissae 1–689 in Mastronarde: est. ~25k words.
candidates.edition: Mastronarde, EuripidesScholia.org, Release 4 (2026), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, which is compatible with Neoscholia's non-commercial licence. Schwartz 1887–91 is PD.
candidates.ru_evidence: No Russian translation found on ancientrome.ru or ru-wiki. Not specifically searched in Russian.
candidates.en_evidence: EuripidesScholia.org gives English translations for the Orestes scholia only; the Phoenissae scholia are untranslated.
candidates.other_translations: None found.
candidates.value: Phoenissae was a Byzantine triad play with a rich Theban mythography and ancient staging notes. The openly licensed critical text with apparatus is ideal for publishing source and translation side by side.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Open digital text with structured scholia types; Mastronarde's Orestes translations offer a style benchmark.
candidates.pilot_unit: Scholia to Phoenissae 1–260; est. ~10k words.

candidates.title: Ioannes Tzetzes, Exegesis of the Iliad / Иоанн Цец, Экзегеза к «Илиаде»
candidates.author: John Tzetzes
candidates.size: Long introduction plus commentary on Iliad 1; est. ~50k words.
candidates.edition: Papathomopoulos, Athens 2007 (in copyright). Hermann 1812 is PD; its completeness is unverified.
candidates.ru_evidence: Ru-wiki 'Иоанн Цец' lists the Exegesis among his works and gives no translation. The only Russian Tzetzes items are 1969 excerpts and Smyka's Carmina Iliaca.
candidates.en_evidence: Search found no English translation; only the Allegories (DOML 2015, 2019) are translated (BMCR 2015.09.45, 2020.03.07).
candidates.other_translations: None found.
candidates.value: Byzantine prolegomena on Homer's life, poetics and allegory; Tzetzes' early method. Complements his Allegories and Eustathius, and is important for the history of Homeric reception.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. Polemical, idiosyncratic prose. The PD text is uncertain, so editorial checks are needed.
candidates.pilot_unit: The introduction (Homer's life, genres, allegory); est. ~15k words.

candidates.title: Ioannes Tzetzes, Historiai (Chiliades) / Book of Histories / Иоанн Цец, «Книга историй» (Хилиады) [RU-gap]
candidates.author: John Tzetzes
candidates.genre: Verse encyclopedic commentary on his own letters
candidates.size: About 12,700 lines (12,674 per ru-wiki; 12,759 per ToposText); about 600–668 historiai.
candidates.edition: Leone 1968/2007 (in copyright). Kiessling 1826 is PD.
candidates.ru_evidence: Ru-wiki 'Иоанн Цец' lists only excerpts in Памятники византийской литературы IX–XIV вв. (1969), pp. 252–259. No full or substantial translation exists.
candidates.en_evidence: Untila, Berkowitz et al. 2015, online at theoi.com under CC BY-NC-ND 3.0, so usable only for cross-checking (ToposText 617).
candidates.other_translations: None found.
candidates.value: A vast mythographic and historical thesaurus with lost sources and Byzantine scholarly self-portraits, including anecdotes on Alexander. Heavily used but inaccessible to Russian readers.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium-high. Plain narrative verse that translates readily into prose; source attribution is unreliable, so the commentary must flag errors.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book I (est. ~1,000 lines), or a thematic cluster of the Alexander historiai.

sweep:greek-scholia.ru_gap_notes:
Translated into English but not into Russian:
- Tzetzes, Chiliades (full; online 2015, CC BY-NC-ND).
- Tzetzes, Allegories of the Iliad and of the Odyssey (DOML 2015 and 2019; only Smyka's Carmina Iliaca draft exists in Russian).
- Porphyry, Homeric Questions (Schlunk 1993; MacPhail 2011). Ru-wiki lists only De antro nympharum in Russian.
- Iliad scholia, Books 1–2 (CUP 2025).
- Eustathius on the Odyssey, books 1–8 (Brill 2022–23).
- D-scholia mythological narratives (CC BY 2023/2026).
- Euripides' Orestes scholia (EuripidesScholia.org).

Probably also gaps, but Russian status unverified: Heraclitus' Homeric Problems (Russell and Konstan 2005) and Ps.-Plutarch's De Homero (Keaney and Lamberton 1996).

Not gaps: Cornutus (Poznev 1999) and Palaephatus (Yarkho) are already in Russian.

sweep:alexander-fiction.corpus_overview:
I checked about 22 Alexander texts and 15 related fiction texts. The web-search budget ran out partway through, so some negative findings rest only on catalogue checks (ru-wiki, facetia.ru, ancientrome.ru, azbyka.ru, archive.org) and should be re-verified.

RUSSIAN. Modern translations exist only for these: the Old Russian/Serbian Alexandria (Литпамятники 1965); N. Gorelov's 2006 volume (Leo's Nativitas from the Bamberg MS, Collatio Alexandri et Dindimi, Epistola ad Aristotelem, Commonitorium Palladii); and Palladius' Greek De gentibus Indiae (Taronyan 2007). The Greek Romance itself has only A. N. Egunov's excerpt (α I.15–26, 30–41; 1960/61). I found no Russian translation for about 12 units: Julius Valerius, the Zacher and Metz Epitomes, Liber de morte, Itinerarium, recensions β/γ/ε/λ, Historia de preliis J1–J3, and the Byzantine verse and vernacular versions.

ENGLISH. Translated: α (Haight 1955; Dowden 1989), the β-based Stoneman 1991, Leo + J1 + Epistola + Iter ad Paradisum (Kratz 1991), J1 (Pritchard 1992), Itinerarium (Davies 1998), Armenian and Syriac. No full English translation for Julius Valerius (only the birth episode, DeAngeli 1982), ε, γ, J2/J3 or the 1388 poem. Julius Valerius does exist in French (Callu 2010) and partly in Italian (Valla vols I–II). ε appears untranslated in any language.

FICTION. Russian covers the Life of Aesop (Gasparov), Drosilla (1969), Hysmine (since 1769) and Dictys. I found no Russian for Rhodanthe, Aristandros, the papyrus novel fragments or the Ps.-Clementines.

candidates.title: Res gestae Alexandri Macedonis translatae ex Aesopo graeco / Julius Valerius, Deeds of Alexander of Macedon / Юлий Валерий, «Деяния Александра Македонского»
candidates.author: Julius Valerius Alexander Polemius
candidates.genre: Novel: Latin adaptation of the Greek Alexander Romance (α)
candidates.size: 3 books; c. 30–35k words (est.; Kübler text pp. 1–168)
candidates.edition: Rosellini, Teubner 1993/2004 (standard, copyright). Public domain: Kübler, Teubner 1888 (with Collatio): https://archive.org/details/iulivalerialexan00vale
candidates.ru_evidence: Russian web search ('Юлий Валерий … перевод') found nothing. The facetia.ru survey of Alexander literature names Julius Valerius but gives no translation. ru-wiki lists none.
candidates.en_evidence: Only the birth episode, Latin/English facing, E. S. DeAngeli 1982 (Gower sources; gower.lib.utsa.edu). No complete English translation found. The BMCR 2005.05.42 review mentions none.
candidates.other_translations: French: J.-P. Callu, Brepols 2010 (complete; publisher says 'never translated before'). Italian: Books I–II in Stoneman–Gargiulo, Fondazione Valla 2007, 2012; vol. III not yet published.
candidates.value: Earliest Latin Alexander Romance and the best witness to the lost α text. Gateway to the Western medieval tradition via the Zacher Epitome, and a showpiece of late-antique Latin prose. Textual critics of Ps.-Callisthenes need it, and no English or Russian version exists.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium-high. Mannered, archaizing late Latin with corrupt passages. The parallel Greek α (Kroll) allows line-by-line cross-checking by AI reviewers. The editor's own expertise is ideal for validation.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book I (Nectanebo, birth, youth, Bucephalus, Olympic victory; c. 10–12k words), with Greek α parallel

candidates.title: Βίος Ἀλεξάνδρου τοῦ Μακεδόνος, recension α / Greek Alexander Romance α / Псевдо-Каллисфен, «Жизнь Александра Македонского» (ред. α)
candidates.author: Pseudo-Callisthenes (anonymous)
candidates.size: 3 books; c. 30–35k words (est.; Kroll 1926, c. 145 pp.)
candidates.edition: W. Kroll, Historia Alexandri Magni I, 1926. Public domain (pre-1930; Kroll d. 1939): https://archive.org/details/historiaalexandr00pseu. Also Stoneman–Gargiulo, Valla 2007–12 (Books I–II).
candidates.ru_evidence: Only A. N. Egunov's excerpt (Book I.15–26, 30–41; rest summarized) in «Поздняя греческая проза», 1960/61, pp. 397–416 (facetia.ru; ru-wiki Псевдо-Каллисфен). No complete Russian translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: E. H. Haight 1955 (en-wiki). K. Dowden 1989 in Reardon, CAGN (not re-verified). Stoneman's Penguin 1991 is β-based (attalus.org).
candidates.other_translations: Italian: Valla I–II (2007/2012). Bulgarian: B. Bogdanov 2005 (recension unclear). French: Bounoure–Serret 1992 and Spanish: García Gual, Gredos 1977, both from memory, not re-verified.
candidates.value: Antiquity's most widely diffused novel and the root of dozens of versions. Russian readers and Slavists have no complete modern Russian text to set beside the Old Russian Alexandrias. A natural Russian flagship for an editor whose dissertation is on the Romance.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High: plain koine narrative, letters and oracles. Risks are the lacunae and Kroll's supplements (from Julius Valerius, the Armenian and β); reviewers must flag reconstructed passages.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book III (Porus, Brahmans, letter to Aristotle, Candace, death and testament; c. 11k words est.). Egunov did not touch this book.

candidates.title: Anonymi Byzantini Vita Alexandri regis Macedonum (recension ε) / ε-recension of the Alexander Romance / ε-редакция «Романа об Александре»
candidates.author: Anonymous Byzantine redactor
candidates.size: c. 25k words (est.; Trumpf ed. xxvi + 205 small pp.)
candidates.edition: J. Trumpf, Teubner 1974 (copyright; scan at archive.org/details/anonymibyzantini0000unse). Unique MS: Oxford, Bodl. Barocci 17. An open Greek text would need re-collation from the MS.
candidates.ru_evidence: ru-wiki and the facetia.ru surveys list only Egunov's α excerpt. A Russian search for any Pseudo-Callisthenes translation found no Greek-recension translations.
candidates.en_evidence: Targeted English search ('recension ε' Trumpf translation) returned only studies (e.g. Huelva/Arias Montano article on Achilles Tatius imitations). No translation located.
candidates.other_translations: None found. The Valla edition prints α, β, γ but not ε.
candidates.value: Byzantine Christian reshaping of Alexander: Jerusalem visit, monotheist hero, Gog and Magog enclosure, prophecy. Source for γ and later Byzantine and apocalyptic tradition. Apparently untranslated anywhere: a genuine first translation for Byzantinists and Slavists.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Straightforward Byzantine koine. Copyright on Trumpf limits reproducing the Greek: publish the translation keyed to Trumpf's chapters, or re-collate the MS.
candidates.pilot_unit: Jerusalem visit plus Gog and Magog enclosure episodes (c. 4–5k words est.)

candidates.title: Incerti auctoris Epitoma rerum gestarum Alexandri Magni cum Libro de morte testamentoque Alexandri / Metz Epitome and Liber de morte / «Мецская эпитома» и «Книга о смерти и завещании Александра»
candidates.author: Anonymous
candidates.date: 4th–5th c. CE (Liber = Latin version of a Hellenistic pamphlet)
candidates.size: c. 8–10k words total (est.)
candidates.edition: P. H. Thomas, Teubner 1960/1966 (standard, copyright). Public domain: Volkmann 1886 and Wagner 1901 (sole MS destroyed 1944). Digitized copies not verified.
candidates.ru_evidence: None found: not in ancientrome.ru's anonymous-Latin catalogue, no ru-wiki article, nothing in the facetia.ru survey. A dedicated Russian search could not be run (budget exhausted).
candidates.en_evidence: No complete English translation located. Excerpts are believed to appear in Heckel & Yardley 2004 (not verified).
candidates.other_translations: None verified
candidates.value: Vulgate (Cleitarchan) material found nowhere else, covering Hyrcania to India. The Liber preserves the Hellenistic 'last days and testament' pamphlet shared with Romance III.30–33, linking history and Romance. Core source for Alexander historians.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High: plain late Latin. Lacunae and transmission only through 19th-c. transcripts must be flagged in the apparatus.
candidates.pilot_unit: Liber de morte testamentumque Alexandri complete (c. 3k words est.), with Romance III.30–33 parallel

candidates.title: Pseudo-Callisthenes, recension β / Greek Alexander Romance β / «Роман об Александре», ред. β
candidates.author: Pseudo-Callisthenes (anonymous redactor)
candidates.size: 3 books; c. 35k words (est.; Bergson 1965, 210 pp.)
candidates.edition: L. Bergson 1965 (copyright). Public-domain composite text: C. Müller, Didot 1846 (MSS A, B, C): https://archive.org/details/arrianianabasis00dbgoog
candidates.ru_evidence: ru-wiki: the medieval Chronographic Alexandria derives from β, but no modern Russian translation of the Greek is listed. Egunov's excerpt is from α.
candidates.en_evidence: R. Stoneman, Penguin 1991, 'based mainly on β' with additions (attalus.org)
candidates.other_translations: Italian: Valla edition prints β beside α and γ (BMCR 2014.05.09). German: van Thiel 1974 (MS L), not re-verified.
candidates.value: The version read in Byzantium and the Greek source of the Old Russian Chronographic Alexandria. A modern Russian version lets Slavists compare directly. Contains the famous wonders letter (Land of the Blessed, Water of Life).
candidates.ai_feasibility: High: koine prose. Manuscript divergence (9 MSS) needs a clear base-text policy.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book II.32–44 (letter to Olympias on the wonders; c. 6k words est.)

candidates.title: Recension γ of the Greek Alexander Romance / ред. γ «Романа об Александре»
candidates.author: Anonymous Byzantine compiler
candidates.size: 3 books; 463 pp. in the 1962–69 edition; c. 60k words (est.)
candidates.edition: Lauenstein (I, 1962), Engelmann (II, 1963), Parthe (III, 1969), Beiträge zur klass. Philologie (copyright; scans at archive.org). Müller 1846 (public domain) used γ MS C.
candidates.ru_evidence: No modern Russian translation of any Greek recension other than Egunov's α excerpt (ru-wiki, facetia.ru)
candidates.en_evidence: No English translation found. Dedicated search not run. Stoneman 1991 (β) and Haight (α) do not cover γ.
candidates.other_translations: Italian partial: Valla vols I–II print γ with translation (BMCR 2014.05.09)
candidates.value: The largest Byzantine compilation, merging β and ε. Adds Jewish and Christian episodes, Palladius on the Brahmans, and catalogues of subject peoples. Key to the Byzantine reception and to Slavonic versions.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium-high: easy Greek but large. Synoptic alignment with β and ε can be automated.
candidates.pilot_unit: γ-specific episodes of Book II, e.g. the Jerusalem visit (c. 5k words est.)

candidates.title: Itinerarium Alexandri ad Constantium Augustum / Alexander's Itinerary / «Итинерарий Александра»
candidates.author: Anonymous (possibly Julius Valerius)
candidates.size: c. 8–10k words (est.)
candidates.edition: R. Tabacco, Florence 2000 (standard). Public domain: A. Mai 1817: https://archive.org/details/itinerariumalex00unkngoog
candidates.ru_evidence: None found: not in the ancientrome.ru anonymous-Latin list, no ru-wiki article. The facetia.ru survey cites the work without a translation.
candidates.en_evidence: I. Davies 1998 (Ancient History Bulletin), listed among translations in en-wiki
candidates.other_translations: Italian: R. Tabacco 2000 (text, translation, commentary)
candidates.value: Arrian-based compendium written for Constantius II's Persian war. Evidence for 4th-c. imitation of Alexander, Arrian's reception in Latin, and the circle of Julius Valerius. Natural companion volume.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium-high: terse, sometimes corrupt late Latin. Arrian parallels allow systematic AI cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Dedication to Constantius plus Granicus/Issus chapters (c. 3k words est.); the whole text is pilot-sized

candidates.title: Βίος Ἀλεξάνδρου, Byzantine Alexander Poem (1388) / Byzantine verse Alexander / Византийская стихотворная «Александрия» (1388)
candidates.author: Anonymous
candidates.size: c. 6,100 political verses (est.)
candidates.edition: S. Reichmann 1963 (Cod. Marc. gr. 408; copyright). Public domain: W. Wagner, Trois poèmes grecs du moyen-âge 1881: https://archive.org/details/troispomesgrecs00wagngoog
candidates.ru_evidence: The ru-wiki 'Византийский роман' list includes the verse 'Alexandreid' with no translation. Facetia.ru and ru-wiki Alexandria pages also cite none.

candidates.other_translations: None found
candidates.value: Major Palaiologan reworking of the Romance into verse. It links the learned Byzantine and vernacular Greek/Slavic Alexander traditions. The public-domain text allows a fully open bilingual edition.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium: semi-vernacular lexicon (Kriaras) is weaker in LLM training data. Needs cross-model lexical review.

candidates.title: Fragments of the Greek novels on papyrus: Ninus, Metiochus & Parthenope, Sesonchosis, Iolaus, Lollianus' Phoinikika / «Роман о Нине» и др.
candidates.author: Anonymous; Lollianus
candidates.size: c. 10–15k words total (est.); Ninus c. 1.5k
candidates.edition: Stephens & Winkler 1995 (text + English). Open texts in papyri.info DDbDP (CC BY): https://papyri.info

candidates.en_evidence: Stephens & Winkler, Ancient Greek Novels: The Fragments (1995); not re-verified this sweep
candidates.other_translations: Not checked
candidates.value: Earliest Greek fiction, including historical romances (Ninus/Semiramis, Sesonchosis) that parallel the Alexander Romance. Essential for the history of the genre. Short and openly licensed.

candidates.other_translations: Italian: F. Conca 1994 (not re-verified)

sweep:alexander-fiction.ru_gap_notes:
These texts have English translations but no Russian one:
- **Greek Romance α:** Haight 1955 and Dowden 1989; Russian has only Egunov's Book I excerpt.
- **Recension β:** Stoneman 1991.
- **Itinerarium Alexandri:** Davies 1998.
- **Historia de preliis J1 and Iter ad Paradisum:** Kratz 1991; J1 also Pritchard 1992.
- **Rhodanthe and Aristandros:** Jeffreys 2012.
- **Papyrus novel fragments:** Stephens & Winkler 1995 (Russian status unknown).
- **Ps.-Clementines:** Ante-Nicene Fathers, 1886 (Russian status unknown).

The Armenian and Syriac Romances (Wolohojian; Budge) are in English; their Russian status is unknown.

The most valuable gap: a complete Russian α with β supplements. The most influential ancient novel has no full Russian version, though Old Russian Alexandria scholarship depends on it.

sweep:greek-historiography.corpus_overview:
Russian coverage of Greek historiography from the Hellenistic period to the 7th century is broad but often dated or amateur.
(1) The late-antique classicizing historians are all in Russian. Destunis (1860) translated 9 of them: Dexippus, Eunapius, Olympiodorus, Malchus, Peter, Menander, Candidus, Nonnosus and Theophanes of Byzantium. Priscus followed in 1860/61 and again by Latyshev (1948); Skrzhinskaya retranslated Olympiodorus (1956).
(2) Fragmentary historians (FGrHist): simposium.ru holds an amateur Russian corpus of about 612 author entries (agnostik, 2017 onward). No scholarly Russian edition exists.
(3) These are already translated into Russian: Memnon, Agatharchides (Bukharin 2012/2019), Nicolaus (Smirnov), Phlegon's Mirabilia, Ps.-Plutarch De fluviis (Torshilov) and Hesychius' Patria (Surikov).
(4) Large gaps:
- Cassius Dio: professional Russian only for books 51–80 (2011, 2014), so books 1–50 are missing.
- Diodorus 21–40: only an amateur Russian translation.
- Malalas: Russian only for books XIV–XVIII plus excerpts.
- Chronicon Paschale: Russian covers only Adam to Terah (2004), English only 284–628. The Abraham–284 bulk has no modern translation in any language.
- Synkellos, Africanus, John of Antioch, Excerpta Barbari and Eusebius' Chronographia: English yes, Russian no.
- Lydus: Russian only for De magistratibus I–II and scraps of De mensibus and De ostentis.
(5) Byzantine chronicles that carry ancient material have no modern Russian: Zonaras 1–9, Georgios Monachos, the pre-Christian part of Kedrenos, Glykas. Georgios, Zonaras 1–6, Kedrenos and Glykas also lack English. Hippolytus' Chronicon has only an online English draft.
Net: at least 14 sizeable units lack Russian, and at least 5 lack any published modern translation.

candidates.title: Chronicon Paschale (Easter Chronicle; «Пасхальная хроника»). Proposed unit: the Epitome from Abraham to AD 284
candidates.author: Anonymous (cleric close to Patriarch Sergius I)
candidates.genre: Christian world chronicle / chronography with consular fasti and Olympiads
candidates.size: Whole work c. 730 Bonn pp. (Dindorf I). Proposed unit roughly 400+ Bonn pp. (Greek + Latin), est. 90–120k Greek words (rough)
candidates.edition: Dindorf, CSHB 1832, 2 vols: public domain, scanned. No modern critical edition of the pre-284 part
candidates.ru_evidence: Самуткина Л.А., «Пасхальная хроника», СПб.: Алетейя 2004 covers only the introduction and the Epitome from Adam to Terah. Kuzenkov's review (patriarchia.ru): «лишь первая, небольшая часть хроники». No Russian for Abraham–628
candidates.en_evidence: Only Whitby & Whitby, Chronicon Paschale 284–628 AD (TTH 7, Liverpool; 2nd imp. 2007). No English for Creation–284 found in en/ru Wikipedia bibliographies
candidates.other_translations: None found for the Abraham–284 portion (only the old Latin of Du Cange/Dindorf)
candidates.value: Transmits Africanus-based chronology, Olympiad and consular lists, synchronisms for Hellenistic and Roman history, and the Alexandrian Easter computus. A key witness to how Byzantium received ancient history. The bulk of a major chronicle exists in no modern language, which makes it an ideal Neoscholia flagship.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High: formulaic Koine, annalistic entries. Risks: numerals, consul names and era reckonings; check them programmatically against the fasti
candidates.pilot_unit: Olympiads c. 100–130 (Philip II to the Diadochi, including the Alexander entries) or the Republican consular-fasti block. c. 25–30 Bonn pp., est. 6–8k words

candidates.title: Hippolytus of Rome, Chronicon (Συναγωγὴ χρόνων καὶ ἐτῶν, including the Diamerismos; «Хроника» Ипполита Римского)
candidates.author: Hippolytus of Rome
candidates.language: Greek (Matritensis gr. 121), plus Latin versions (Liber generationis I–II)
candidates.genre: Christian world chronicle with an ethnographic-geographic catalogue of peoples, lands and islands
candidates.size: Greek text est. 15–20k words, not counting the Stadiasmus. GCS 46 c. 200 pp. including the Latin versions
candidates.edition: A. Bauer, TU 29.1 (1905): public domain. Bauer–Helm, GCS 46 (2nd ed. 1955): in copyright
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Ипполит Римский) lists about 20 Russian translations (Refutatio, Antichrist, Apostolic Tradition, etc.); none is of the Chronicon. No Russian found
candidates.en_evidence: Only an online 'rough draft' English translation by T. C. Schmidt & N. Nicholas (2010), per en.wikipedia. No published English found
candidates.other_translations: None found
candidates.value: The earliest surviving Christian world chronicle. Its Diamerismos (the division of the earth among Noah's sons) is a foundational text of late-antique ethnography and geography, used by the Paschale, Synkellos and Georgios Monachos. Matters to classicists, historians of geography and scholars of early Christianity.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High: plain Greek and lists. Needs gazetteer linking (Pleiades/ToposText) and collation with the Latin versions
candidates.pilot_unit: The Diamerismos with its catalogues of peoples, languages and islands, est. 4–6k words

candidates.title: Georgios Monachos (Hamartolos), Chronicon syntomon, Book I (Adam to Alexander); «Хроника Георгия Амартола», кн. I
candidates.author: Georgios Monachos (Hamartolos)
candidates.genre: Byzantine monastic world chronicle (ancient and biblical history)
candidates.size: Whole work: de Boor, 2 vols, c. 800 pp. Book I (Adam, Nimrod, Persians, Chaldaeans, Brahmans, Amazons, Alexander) est. 25–35k words
candidates.edition: C. de Boor, Teubner 1904 (public domain); corrected reprint by Wirth 1978
candidates.ru_evidence: No modern Russian. Only the medieval Old Slavonic translation (ed. Istrin) and Senina 2012 (Leo V reign excerpt), per ru.wikipedia
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia lists only editions (Muralt 1859, PG 110, de Boor 1904). No English translation found
candidates.other_translations: Medieval Slavonic and Georgian (Arsen of Iqalto) only. No modern translation found
candidates.value: The Slavonic 'Amartol' shaped Russian chronicle writing (the Primary Chronicle). Book I carries ancient lore: Brahmans (via Palladius), Alexander, Persian and Chaldaean material. A facing-text translation would serve Byzantinists, Slavists and Alexander-tradition scholars, and connects directly to the editor's expertise.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High: Koine with patristic quotations. Source identification (Palladius, Josephus, Theodoret) is needed
candidates.pilot_unit: The Book I sections on Alexander and the Brahmans, est. 5–7k words

candidates.title: Eusebius of Caesarea, Chronicon Book 1 (Chronographia; «Хроника» Евсевия, кн. 1)
candidates.author: Eusebius of Caesarea
candidates.language: Classical Armenian (version of the lost Greek), plus Greek fragments in Synkellos
candidates.genre: Chronography: an anthology of national histories and king-lists
candidates.size: Est. 40–50k words (Karst GCS 20, roughly pp. 1–143)
candidates.edition: Aucher 1818 (Armenian + Latin; public domain). Schoene–Petermann 1875 (public domain). Karst, GCS 20 (1911), German translation
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Хроника Евсевия): only partly in Russian, namely the Roman-era Canons in Jerome's Latin version (Kiev 1910). Book 1 not translated. ancientrome has only the Ptolemy king-list (from English)
candidates.en_evidence: Online only, not peer-reviewed: attalus.org translation of Book 1 (Schoene–Petermann pp. 1–295). Jerome's Canons in English on tertullian.org
candidates.other_translations: German (Karst 1911, from the Armenian). Latin (Aucher, Petermann)
candidates.value: Preserves excerpts of Berossus, Abydenus, Alexander Polyhistor, Manetho, Castor and Porphyry on the Ptolemies and Seleucids. A core source for Near Eastern and Hellenistic chronology, used by Assyriologists, Egyptologists and Hellenistic historians.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium: LLMs are weaker in Classical Armenian. Mitigate with Greek parallels (Synkellos) and Karst as cross-check; an Armenologist reviewer is required
candidates.pilot_unit: The Chaldaean section (Berossus/Abydenus/Polyhistor excerpts), est. 8–10k words

candidates.title: Cassius Dio, Roman History, Books 1–35 (fragments plus Zonaras' epitome 7–9); «Римская история», кн. I–XXXV
candidates.author: Cassius Dio (Zonaras for the epitome)
candidates.size: Boissevain vol. I fragments plus Zonaras 7–9, est. 70–90k words
candidates.edition: Boissevain 1895–1901 (public domain). Zonaras: Dindorf, Teubner 1868–75 (public domain)
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia lists professional Russian only for books 51–80 (Makhlayuk et al. 2011, 2014). Books 36, 37 and 48 exist only as amateur versions from English (ancientrome). Nothing for books 1–35
candidates.en_evidence: Loeb, E. Cary (1914–27); online at LacusCurtius
candidates.other_translations: French listed on ru.wikipedia. German (O. Veh) not re-verified
candidates.value: The main Greek narrative of regal and Republican Rome where Livy is lost: the Punic Wars, the Gracchi. Books 36–50 likewise lack a professional Russian translation, which makes this one of the largest Russian gaps in Roman historiography and useful for broad audiences and teaching.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High: Attic-style Greek. The provenance of each excerpt (Constantinian excerpts, Zonaras, Tzetzes) must be marked in the apparatus
candidates.pilot_unit: Regal period: Books 1–3 fragments plus Zonaras 7.1–12, est. 8–10k words

candidates.title: John Malalas, Chronographia, Books I–XIII; «Хронография» Иоанна Малалы, кн. I–XIII
candidates.author: John Malalas
candidates.size: Books I–XIII est. 60–70k words (about 60% of the work)
candidates.edition: Dindorf, CSHB 1831 (public domain). Thurn, CFHB 35 (2000; in copyright)
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia: Russian exists for books XIV–XVIII (Samutkina 2000/2003; Chekalova 2001). For I–XIII only excerpts of II and V (Averintsev 1987; Freiberg 1968) and VIII (Talakh 2013)
candidates.en_evidence: Jeffreys, Jeffreys, Scott et al., Byzantina Australiensia 4 (1986), listed on ru.wikipedia
candidates.other_translations: Old Slavonic (Istrin). German translation (Thurn–Meier 2009) and a French project not re-verified in this session
candidates.value: Covers mythography, Troy (after Dictys), Persians, Alexander and the Seleucids, the foundation of Antioch and the Roman emperors. Central to the reception of antiquity, the Alexander tradition and Slavonic chronography, so a strong match for the editor's specialism.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High: simple Greek. Text reconstruction needs Slavonic and Excerpta parallels; Dindorf's text is outdated and Thurn's is in copyright
candidates.pilot_unit: Book VIII (Alexander, Diadochi, Seleucus, Antioch), est. 5–6k words

candidates.title: George Synkellos, Ecloga chronographica (Ἐκλογὴ χρονογραφίας; «Избранная хронография» Георгия Синкелла)
candidates.author: George Synkellos
candidates.size: Mosshammer c. 470 Teubner pp., est. 150k words
candidates.edition: Dindorf, CSHB 1829 (public domain). Mosshammer, Teubner 1984 (in copyright)
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia lists only the medieval Slavonic abridgement (ed. Totomanova 2008) and studies. No modern Russian
candidates.en_evidence: W. Adler & P. Tuffin, The Chronography of George Synkellos (OUP 2002), listed on ru.wikipedia
candidates.other_translations: None found
candidates.value: The largest storehouse of Berossus, Manetho, Africanus, Eusebius, Panodorus, Annianus and the 1 Enoch fragments. Indispensable for Near Eastern, Egyptian, Jewish and Hellenistic chronology.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High: regular learned Greek. King-lists and tables need structured handling and automated numeral checks
candidates.pilot_unit: The Egyptian dynasties (Manetho via Africanus/Eusebius) or the Alexander–Diadochi section, c. 30 Teubner pp.

candidates.title: Dexippus(?), Scythica Vindobonensia: new palimpsest fragments (Vind. hist. gr. 73); «Скифика» Дексиппа, венские фрагменты
candidates.author: P. Herennius Dexippus (attribution debated)
candidates.genre: Classicizing military history (Gothic wars of the 250s–260s)
candidates.size: Several palimpsest leaves, est. 3–5k words
candidates.edition: Martin & Grusková, GRBS 54.4 (2014): Greek text plus English, CC BY. Later leaves in other journals; Empire in Crisis (OAPEN, open access)
candidates.ru_evidence: A Russian search ('Дексипп венский палимпсест перевод') found nothing. Old fragments only in Destunis 1860 (ru.wikipedia, Дексипп (историк))
candidates.en_evidence: GRBS 2014 article includes an English translation (checked in the PDF). Other leaves are translated in scattered studies
candidates.other_translations: German and Italian scholarship (Martin; Mecella 2013 covers the old fragments)
candidates.value: One of the most important newly discovered Greek historical texts: Decius' Gothic war and the sieges of Balkan cities. Relevant to Black Sea and Gothic studies, and has no Russian at all.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium: a gappy text with editorial supplements. The AI must not fill gaps, which makes it a good showcase for visible review
candidates.pilot_unit: The GRBS 2014 fragment set, c. 2–3k words, with a CC BY source text

candidates.title: John Lydus, De ostentis (Περὶ διοσημειῶν; «О знамениях»)
candidates.author: John Lydus
candidates.size: Wachsmuth c. 190 pp., est. 30–35k words
candidates.edition: Wachsmuth, Teubner 2nd ed. 1897 (public domain)
candidates.ru_evidence: Tiny: Sinitsa translated only the introduction (chs. 1–8; Belgorod 2018) and ch. 71. Sinitsa–Bolgov (2022): «полных комментированных переводов – задача на будущее»
candidates.en_evidence: Bandy (ed.), The Works of Ioannes Lydus III: De ostentis (Edwin Mellen 2013), listed on ru.wikipedia
candidates.other_translations: An Italian edition/translation is mentioned in Sinitsa's survey; details not verified
candidates.value: Preserves Nigidius Figulus' Etruscan thunder calendar and lore from Fonteius, Labeo and Campestris. A prime source on Etruscan and Roman religion and ancient divination, for historians of religion and science.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High: clear Greek. Technical astro-meteorological terms need a glossary and comparison with the Latin sources
candidates.pilot_unit: The thunder calendar (brontoscopic calendar) chapters, est. 5k words

candidates.title: John Zonaras, Epitome historiarum, Books I–VI; «Хроника» Иоанна Зонары, кн. I–VI
candidates.author: John Zonaras
candidates.genre: Byzantine historical epitome (Jewish, Near Eastern, Persian and Macedonian history)
candidates.size: Dindorf vol. I, est. 100k words
candidates.edition: Dindorf, Teubner 1868 (public domain). Pinder, CSHB 1841 (public domain)
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia lists only a canon-law treatise in modern Russian (Bondach 2007). The chronicle exists only in medieval Slavonic
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia lists only Banchich & Lane 2009 (12.15–13.19). Loeb Dio covers parts of 7–9. Nothing found for 1–6
candidates.other_translations: Only Renaissance Latin, French and Italian
candidates.value: A learned paraphrase of Josephus, Herodotus, Xenophon, Plutarch and Arrian, valuable for source criticism and the Byzantine reception of Persian and Alexander history. Books 7–9 are covered in the Dio candidate.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High: Atticizing but regular Greek. Source parallels allow automated alignment checks
candidates.pilot_unit: The Persian–Alexander section (Book IV), est. 6–8k words; book division to be verified

candidates.title: John of Antioch, Historia chronica (fragments); «Хроника» Иоанна Антиохийского
candidates.author: John of Antioch
candidates.genre: World chronicle surviving in fragments (Excerpta Constantiniana, Salmasiana)
candidates.size: 300+ fragments, est. 60–80k words
candidates.edition: Roberto 2005 and Mariev, CFHB 47 (2008): both in copyright. Müller FHG IV–V and de Boor, Excerpta de insidiis 1905: public domain
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Иоанн Антиохийский (историк)) mentions only Mariev's English. A Russian search found no translation. Small excerpts in the Свод... are possible but unverified
candidates.en_evidence: Mariev 2008, 'recensuit anglice vertit' (ÖAW catalogue). Reviewed in BMCR 2009.12.06
candidates.other_translations: Italian (Roberto 2005), from memory
candidates.value: Lost material on the Republic and Empire (from Dio, Eutropius, Priscus) and unique 5th-century western events such as the sack of 455. The Roberto–Mariev attribution dispute suits a transparent, multi-model apparatus.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium: easy Greek, but attribution and two rival editions need care. Use public-domain texts unless permission is obtained
candidates.pilot_unit: Fragments on the 5th-century West (Valentinian III, Aetius, 455), est. 5k words

candidates.title: Sextus Julius Africanus, Chronographiae (fragments); «Хронография» Юлия Африкана
candidates.author: Sextus Julius Africanus
candidates.language: Greek (with Latin, Syriac and Armenian testimonia)
candidates.size: About 100 fragments plus testimonia, est. 20–30k words
candidates.edition: Routh, Reliquiae sacrae II (1846; public domain). Wallraff et al., GCS NF 15 (2007; in copyright)
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Секст Юлий Африкан) lists only the Russian Martyrdom of Symphorosa (vostlit). No Chronographiae
candidates.en_evidence: Wallraff (ed.), Chronographiae: The Extant Fragments, translated by W. Adler (2007), per en.wikipedia
candidates.other_translations: None found beyond the English in GCS
candidates.value: The founding text of Christian world chronography (the 5,500-year scheme, Olympiad synchronisms). Source for Eusebius, Synkellos and the Paschale; important for Jewish-Hellenistic chronology.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium-high: short fragments. The main difficulty is separating verbatim quotation from paraphrase in the citing authors
candidates.pilot_unit: The Moses–Ogyges synchronism and Olympiad-chronology fragments, est. 4k words

candidates.title: Excerpta Latina Barbari (Barbarus Scaligeri; 'Alexandrian World Chronicle')
candidates.author: Anonymous Alexandrian compiler; anonymous Frankish translator
candidates.date: Greek original 527–539 CE; Latin version 8th c.
candidates.size: 63 folios, est. 20–25k words
candidates.edition: Frick, Chronica minora I (1892; public domain). Schoene 1875 (public domain)
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Excerpta Latina Barbari) cites only Western scholarship. No Russian translation listed or found
