candidates.en_evidence: B. Garstad, Apocalypse of Pseudo-Methodius: An Alexandrian World Chronicle (DOML, HUP 2012), per en.wikipedia
candidates.other_translations: None found
candidates.value: Ptolemaic, Seleucid and Macedonian king-lists from Africanus, Alexander and Nebuchadnezzar narratives, and Alexandrian prefects. Shows how late antiquity transmitted Hellenistic history; fits the Alexander tradition.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium: the barbarous Latin needs reconstruction of the Greek behind it, which makes it a good test of multi-model review
candidates.pilot_unit: King-lists from Assyria to the Ptolemies, including the Alexander passage, est. 5k words

candidates.title: Diodorus Siculus, Bibliotheca historica, Books XXI–XL (fragments); «Историческая библиотека», кн. XXI–XL
candidates.author: Diodorus Siculus
candidates.size: Loeb vols. XI–XII, est. 100–120k words
candidates.edition: Dindorf, Teubner 1867–68 (public domain). Goukowsky, CUF (in copyright, partial)
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia: a full but amateur Russian translation (simposium.ru, 2012, «непрофессиональный») and Alekseev 1774–75 (from French). Professional Russian only as excerpts (ancientrome: 26, 34–39)
candidates.en_evidence: Loeb (Walton). attalus.org covers books 33–40 (links on ru.wikipedia)
candidates.other_translations: French: 19th-century complete translation (remacle.org) and the CUF series
candidates.value: The main continuous source for the First Punic War, the Sicilian slave wars, the Hellenistic kingdoms, the Gracchi and the Social War. Widely used by students; a critical Russian translation is still lacking.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High: standard Hellenistic Greek. The excerpt source of each fragment must be labelled
candidates.pilot_unit: Books 34/35–36 (Sicilian slave wars), est. 8–10k words

sweep:greek-historiography.ru_gap_notes:
These texts have English translations but no Russian one:
- Synkellos (Adler–Tuffin 2002)
- Julius Africanus (Adler 2007)
- John of Antioch (Mariev 2008)
- Excerpta Latina Barbari (Garstad 2012)
- Malalas I–XIII (Jeffreys 1986; Russian only XIV–XVIII)
- Cassius Dio 1–50 (Loeb; professional Russian only 51–80; 36, 37, 48 amateur from English)
- Chronicon Paschale 284–628 (Whitby; Russian has only Adam–Terah)
- Eusebius' Chronographia (English online)
- Lydus' De magistratibus III, De mensibus and De ostentis (Bandy 2013; Russian only fragments)
- Dexippus' Vienna fragments (GRBS 2014, CC BY)

Diodorus 21–40 has only an amateur Russian translation.
Russian status is unknown for Patria of Constantinople II–IV (Berger, DOML 2013) and the Parastaseis (Cameron–Herrin 1984).
Web searches ran out mid-sweep. Later statuses rest on Wikipedia/catalogue lists and should be rechecked in elibrary.

sweep:christian-late-antique.corpus_overview:
Russian coverage of this corpus is uneven. The 19th-century academies, and azbyka.ru today, hold the "great" Fathers well. Beyond them, verified Russian holdings are scraps:
- Didymus: 1 work (De Spiritu Sancto).
- Zeno: 4 short pieces out of 93 tractates.
- Hilary: 1 of his c. 58 Psalm tractates.
- Caesarius: 3–4 of 238 sermons.
- Sophronius' 70 miracles of Cyrus and John: a 2.9k-character excerpt.
- Eusebius' 15-book Praeparatio: only Book XI (2002).

Ambrosiaster appears only in Latin. Quodvultdeus, Facundus and Procopius of Gaza are absent from the azbyka author index. The Russian ACCS series gives only snippets.

English coverage is far denser. FOTC, ACW, ANF, ACT, DOML and Liturgical Press have translated:
- all of Caesarius' sermons;
- Origen's Munich Psalm homilies (2021);
- Didymus on Genesis, Zechariah, Job and Psalms;
- the Pseudo-Clementines;
- Praeparatio (1903);
- the Miracles of Thecla (2012);
- the Life of Hypatius (2024).

Untranslated in both languages: Quodvultdeus' Liber promissionum, Facundus, Didymus on Ecclesiastes, the Asterian Psalm homilies, Procopius on Genesis, Apponius and Arnobius the Younger. Some of these exist only in French, German or Italian.

Of the 14 candidates:
- Russian: 7 none, 6 tiny or partial, 1 unknown.
- English: 7 none, 2 partial, 5 full.

Method caveat: the WebSearch quota was exhausted. Status was checked by fetching pravenc.ru, azbyka.ru, Russian and English Wikipedia, Open Library and Labirint directly. Single-text translations in Russian journals (eLibrary, CyberLeninka) could not be fully ruled out.

candidates.title: Liber promissionum et praedictorum Dei (Book of God's Promises and Predictions) / «Книга обетований и предсказаний Божиих»
candidates.author: Quodvultdeus of Carthage (transmitted under Prosper's name)
candidates.genre: Typological exegesis / theology of history, apocalyptic
candidates.size: 3 parts + Dimidium temporis + Gloria sanctorum (c. 150 chapters); est. 45–55k words
candidates.edition: Braun, SC 101–102 (1964) and CCSL 60 (1976); public-domain text in PL 51 (under Prosper)
candidates.ru_evidence: Not in azbyka.ru author directory; ru.wikipedia 'Кводвультдеус' (wikitext checked) cites no translation; no Russian edition found
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia lists only Braun SC; Open Library shows French and Italian only. English exists only for his creedal sermons (Finn, ACW 2004)
candidates.other_translations: French: Braun, SC 101–102 (1964). Italian: Città Nuova (1989); Libreria Editrice Vaticana (2002)
candidates.value: Written by Augustine's deacon, the exiled bishop of Carthage. It contains eyewitness notes on the Vandal conquest, Carthage's Caelestis temple, pagan cult, portents and Roman monuments, and is a key Augustinian theology of history. Used by historians of Vandal Africa, late paganism and apocalypticism.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: plain Latin prose with dense biblical citation that is easy to verify; public-domain source. Contemporary allusions need historical notes.
candidates.pilot_unit: Part III (tempus gratiae), chs. 34–44 (incl. the Caelestis temple), plus Dimidium temporis; est. 10–12k words

candidates.title: Quaestiones Veteris et Novi Testamenti (Questions on the Old and New Testament) / «Вопросы Ветхого и Нового Завета»
candidates.author: Ambrosiaster (anonymous Roman cleric; transmitted under Augustine's name)
candidates.size: 127 questions (recension III; 150 in recension I); est. 110–130k words
candidates.edition: Souter, CSEL 50 (1908), public domain; also PL 35. Q.114–115: Bussières, SC 512 (2007)
candidates.ru_evidence: azbyka.ru/otechnik/Amvrosiast lists Latin originals only. ru.wikipedia 'Амброзиастер' cites only Pauline-commentary excerpts in the Russian ACCS series (Библейские комментарии отцов Церкви)
candidates.en_evidence: Only a self-published, non-peer-reviewed version: J. Litteral, CreateSpace 2018, 452 pp. (Open Library). No scholarly English translation found.
candidates.other_translations: French: Q.114–115 (SC 512, 2007). German: Q.115 (von Queis 1972). No complete scholarly translation found.
candidates.value: Late-4th-century Rome through a learned cleric's eyes. Q.114 'Against the pagans' (incl. Mithraic initiation) and Q.115 'On fate' (astrology); also Roman law, Jews, women, Novatianists, Manichees. A core source for the religion and society of late-antique Rome.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: plain argumentative Latin and a public-domain critical text. Challenges: differences between recensions; legal and astrological terms.
candidates.pilot_unit: Q.114 Adversus paganos + Q.115 De fato; est. 14–16k words

candidates.title: Homiliae in Psalmos, Codex Monacensis graecus 314 (Origen's 'new' Homilies on the Psalms) / «Гомилии на Псалмы» (Мюнхенский кодекс)
candidates.author: Origen of Alexandria
candidates.size: 29 homilies on Pss 15, 36, 67, 73–77, 80, 81; est. 85–100k words
candidates.edition: Perrone et al., Die neuen Psalmenhomilien, GCS NF 19 (De Gruyter 2015), under copyright. Rights clearance or an own transcription of the Munich manuscript is needed.
candidates.ru_evidence: pravenc.ru 'Ориген' notes the 2015 publication but lists no Russian translation; azbyka.ru Origen page has no Psalm homilies; Labirint catalogue: none. Journal partials not excluded.
candidates.en_evidence: J. W. Trigg, Origen: Homilies on the Psalms, Codex Monacensis Graecus 314 (FOTC 141, CUA Press 2021), per Open Library
candidates.other_translations: GCS volume has German/Italian apparatus; other modern translations not verified
candidates.value: The most important patristic textual discovery in decades: 29 largely unknown Greek homilies by antiquity's most influential Christian scholar. Rich in Hexaplaric philology, Jewish exegesis and Origen's preaching voice in mid-3rd-century Caesarea. High visibility, and nothing exists in Russian.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: homiletic Greek with simple syntax. Biblical and Hexaplaric variants must be tracked; source-text rights are the main obstacle.
candidates.pilot_unit: Homily on Ps 15 + four homilies on Ps 76; est. 18–22k words

candidates.title: Pro defensione trium capitulorum libri XII (with Contra Mocianum and Epistula fidei catholicae) / «В защиту Трёх глав»
candidates.author: Facundus of Hermiane
candidates.language: Latin (quoting Greek conciliar documents in translation)
candidates.size: All works = PL 67, cols. 527–878; est. 110–130k words
candidates.edition: Clément & Vander Plaetse, CCSL 90A (1974); SC 471, 478, 479, 484, 499 (2002–06); public-domain text in PL 67
candidates.ru_evidence: Absent from azbyka.ru author directory; ru.wikipedia 'Факунд Гермианский' mentions no translation
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia bibliography lists only PL and SC; Open Library shows only French and Italian translations
candidates.other_translations: French: Fraïsse-Bétoulières, SC (5 vols., 2002–2006). Italian: Città Nuova (2007).
candidates.value: An African bishop's defiant address to Justinian. A first-hand source for the Three Chapters crisis, imperial church policy and the Fifth Council; preserves documents that are otherwise lost. Key for 6th-century Byzantine and African history and for late-antique church–state theory.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: long, dense polemical Latin full of quotations; patristic sources must be identified. Public-domain text available.
candidates.pilot_unit: Liber contra Mocianum (est. 6–8k words), or Book XII on imperial authority (est. 8–10k)

candidates.title: Tractatus (Sermons) / «Трактаты» Зинона (Зенона) Веронского
candidates.author: Zeno of Verona
candidates.size: 93 tractates (16 long, 77 short); PL 11, cols. 253–528; est. 45–50k words
candidates.edition: Löfstedt, CCSL 22 (1971). Public domain: Giuliari (1883); Ballerini (1739) = PL 11.
candidates.ru_evidence: azbyka.ru lists only 4 short pieces (c. 14k characters) of 93; the pravenc.ru 'Зинон' bibliography (2009) gives no Russian translation
candidates.en_evidence: G. Jeanes, The Day Has Come! (Liturgical Press 1995): Easter and baptismal sermons only (Open Library)
candidates.other_translations: German: BKV (1934). Italian: Banterle (1987); Città Nuova (2008).
candidates.value: An African-born rhetor-bishop writing Apuleian artistic prose: a zodiac sermon for neophytes, attacks on pagan rites, Virgilian echoes, early Christian Verona. A prime source for Christian–classical cultural interaction and late Latin style.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: mannered, rhythmic Latin with wordplay and textual cruxes. Public-domain text exists.
candidates.pilot_unit: Dossier of c. 12 tractates on classical culture and Easter (incl. I.38 on the twelve signs); est. 8–10k words

candidates.title: Commentary on Ecclesiastes (Tura papyrus) / «Толкование на Екклесиаста»
candidates.author: Didymus the Blind
candidates.genre: Exegetical lectures (classroom notes with student questions)
candidates.size: Lacunose Tura codex; est. 70–90k words
candidates.edition: Binder, Liesenborghs, Kramer, Gronewald et al., PTA (Habelt 1965–1983), with German translation. Not public domain.
candidates.ru_evidence: azbyka.ru Didymus page lists only 'Книга о Святом Духе'; ru.wikipedia 'Дидим Слепец' cites no translations
candidates.en_evidence: Open Library shows English only for Genesis (2016), Zechariah (2006), Job (2025) and the Psalm lectures (2024); none for Ecclesiastes
candidates.other_translations: German: PTA volumes (with the edition)
candidates.value: A unique stenographic record of a 4th-century Alexandrian classroom: student questions, philosophy and pagan learning, Origenist exegesis. Valuable for historians of education and philosophy, papyrologists and Origenism studies.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: lacunae and supplements must be marked rigorously; the conversational Greek is otherwise accessible.
candidates.pilot_unit: Lectures on Eccl 1:1–2:14; est. 10–12k words

candidates.title: Thaumata: Miracles of SS Cyrus and John / «Чудеса святых Кира и Иоанна»
candidates.author: Sophronius (later Patriarch of Jerusalem)
candidates.size: Encomium + 70 miracles; est. 70–80k words
candidates.edition: Fernández Marcos, Los Thaumata de Sofronio (Madrid 1975); partial public-domain text in PG 87.3 (Mai)
candidates.ru_evidence: azbyka.ru Sophronius page: 'Чудеса святых мучеников Кира и Иоанна' is only 2.9k characters (a tiny excerpt)
candidates.en_evidence: Open Library returns only French items; no English translation found
candidates.other_translations: French: Festugière, extracts (1971); full French by Gascou (2006, not verified here)
candidates.value: Incubation cures at Menouthis near Alexandria, successor to an Isis cult. Rich on physicians, disease, social life and Chalcedonian–Miaphysite conflict on the eve of the Arab conquest, by an outstanding stylist. Valuable for historians of medicine, Egypt and religion.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: elaborate Atticizing prose and medical vocabulary; the narratives themselves are clear.
candidates.pilot_unit: Encomium + Miracles 1–10; est. 12–15k words

candidates.title: Pseudo-Clementine Homilies / «Климентины: Беседы (Гомилии)»
candidates.author: Anonymous (Syrian Jewish-Christian milieu)
candidates.size: 20 homilies + prefatory letters; est. 90k words
candidates.edition: Rehm, Irmscher, Paschke, GCS 42 (1953; 3rd ed. 1992). Public domain: Dressel (1853); Lagarde (1865).
candidates.ru_evidence: azbyka.ru 'Климент Римский' lists only the Epistles and De virginitate; ru.wikipedia 'Климентины' cites only studies, no translation
candidates.en_evidence: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 8 (1886), public domain; ru.wikipedia links English versions
candidates.other_translations: French: Écrits apocryphes chrétiens II (Pléiade 2005); not verified here
candidates.value: The only Christian 'recognition novel' of antiquity, structurally close to the Greek romances. Homilies 4–6 stage Clement against Apion on allegorical readings of myth; also Simon Magus and Jewish Christianity. Relevant to ancient-novel studies (incl. the Alexander Romance) and mythography.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: clear koine narrative and dialogue; public-domain Greek, with English available for checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Homilies 4–6 (debate with Apion on Greek myths); est. 14–16k words

candidates.title: Sermones / «Проповеди» Кесария (Цезария) Арелатского
candidates.author: Caesarius of Arles
candidates.size: 238 sermons; est. 250–300k words
candidates.edition: Morin (1937–42) = CCSL 103–104 (1953); many sermons are in public-domain PL 39 (Pseudo-Augustinian appendix)
candidates.ru_evidence: azbyka.ru lists only 'Избранные слова (12, 39, 40)' + one Nativity sermon; ru.wikipedia says only the Vita Caesarii was translated into Russian (2014/2016)
candidates.en_evidence: M. M. Mueller, Sermons I–III (FOTC 31, 47, 66; CUA Press), cited in ru.wikipedia
candidates.other_translations: French, Italian, German and Polish translations of the sermons (per ru.wikipedia)
candidates.value: Preaching to the peasants of 6th-century Gaul: Kalends festivals, augury, amulets, healing cults, drinking, rural life. The principal source for late Roman popular religion and 'pagan survivals' in the post-Roman West.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: deliberately simple 'sermo humilis' Latin.
candidates.pilot_unit: c. 12 sermons on pagan practices (e.g. 13, 33, 50–54, 192–193); est. 15k words

candidates.title: Praeparatio evangelica / «Евангельское приготовление»
candidates.author: Eusebius of Caesarea
candidates.genre: Apologetics (anthology of pagan and Jewish sources)
candidates.size: 15 books; est. 280–320k words (largely quotations)
candidates.edition: Mras, GCS 43 (1954–56; rev. 1982–83); Gifford, Oxford 1903 (Greek text + English), public domain
candidates.ru_evidence: pravenc.ru 'Евсевий' lists only Book XI (Yastrebov, ЦиВр 2002, plus fragments); azbyka.ru lists only Book XI. Demonstratio evangelica: no Russian translation listed.
candidates.en_evidence: Gifford 1903 (public domain)
candidates.other_translations: French: Sources Chrétiennes, several books (not verified here)
candidates.value: A treasure-house of lost Greek prose: Philo of Byblos, Porphyry's Philosophy from Oracles, Oenomaus of Gadara, Diogenianus, Atticus, Numenius, Aristocles. Central for historians of Greek religion, oracles and philosophy.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high for the prose; medium for embedded hexameter oracles and attributing fragments.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book V.18–VI.7: Oenomaus' 'Detection of Frauds' on oracles, with Eusebius' frame; est. 12–15k words

candidates.title: Miracula SS. Cosmae et Damiani (Greek miracle collections) / «Чудеса святых Космы и Дамиана»
candidates.author: Anonymous (shrine of the Kosmidion, Constantinople)
candidates.size: c. 38–48 miracles; est. 35–45k words
candidates.edition: Deubner, Kosmas und Damian (Teubner 1907), public domain; Rupprecht (1935)
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Косма и Дамиан' cites no translation of the Greek miracles; not found on azbyka. Needs check in 19th-century church journals.
candidates.en_evidence: Open Library: only French (Festugière 1971). DOML 'Miracle Tales from Byzantium' (2012) covers Thecla and others, not Cosmas and Damian.
candidates.other_translations: French: Festugière, Collections grecques de miracles (1971)
candidates.value: Incubation at the Kosmidion: patients, doctors, diseases, Jews and pagans healed. A key source for Byzantine medicine and Constantinopolitan social history, directly comparable to the Asclepian iamata.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: simple narrative koine; public-domain critical text.
candidates.pilot_unit: First 12 miracles; est. 8–10k words

candidates.title: Homiliae in Psalmos (31 Psalm homilies) / «Беседы на Псалмы» Астерия Софиста (Псевдо-Астерия)
candidates.author: Asterius the Sophist, or an anonymous Antiochene ('Ps.-Asterius', per Kinzig)
candidates.size: 31 homilies + fragments; est. 70–80k words
candidates.edition: M. Richard, Asterii Sophistae commentariorum in Psalmos quae supersunt (Oslo 1956). German: Kinzig, BGL 56 (Hiersemann 2002).
candidates.ru_evidence: azbyka.ru (under Asterius of Amasea, the PG 40 ascription) has 5 homilies on Ps 5 and one each on Ps 6–7; most likely from this corpus, so c. 7 of 31
candidates.en_evidence: Open Library returns only the German translation (Kinzig 2002); en.wikipedia lists no translation
candidates.other_translations: German: Kinzig (2002)
candidates.value: The earliest Greek homiletic cycle on the Psalms after Origen: vivid Easter-week preaching, catechumens, liturgy, Arian-era theology, striking rhetorical imagery. For historians of liturgy, preaching and Antioch.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium-high: rhetorical Greek with puns and antitheses; the authorship debate needs commentary.
candidates.pilot_unit: Homilies not yet in Russian (e.g. on Ps 1–4); est. 12–15k words

candidates.title: Tractatus super Psalmos / «Трактаты на Псалмы» Илария Пиктавийского
candidates.author: Hilary of Poitiers
candidates.size: Instructio + tractates on c. 58 Psalms (incl. 22 on Ps 118); est. 180–200k words
candidates.edition: Zingerle, CSEL 22 (1891), public domain; Doignon et al., CCSL 61 ff. (1997–)
candidates.ru_evidence: azbyka.ru Hilary page offers only 'Беседа на псалом 130'; ru.wikipedia 'Переводы' lists only that homily
candidates.en_evidence: NPNF II.9 (1899) gives only Pss 1, 53, 130; Open Library shows only studies (Burns 2012)
candidates.other_translations: French: Ps 118 (SC); not verified here
candidates.value: The first major Latin Psalm commentary and a Latin adaptation of Origen. Key for Latin exegesis, the Nicene controversy and the Vetus Latina text. For Latinists and historians of exegesis.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: compressed, difficult Latin; public-domain text.
candidates.pilot_unit: Instructio Psalmorum + Tractatus on Ps 2; est. 10–12k words

candidates.title: Commentary on Genesis (Eclogarum in libros historicos VT epitome, pt. 1) / «Толкование на Бытие»
candidates.author: Procopius of Gaza
candidates.size: est. 100–130k words
candidates.edition: Metzler, GCS NF 22 (2015), with German translation (2016); Exodus volume 2020. PG 87.1 has a mainly Latin version.
candidates.ru_evidence: Procopius of Gaza is absent from the azbyka.ru author directory; no Russian translation found
candidates.en_evidence: Open Library lists editions and translations in Latin, Greek, German, French and Italian only; en.wikipedia cites only Metzler (German)
candidates.other_translations: German: Metzler (2016 Genesis; 2020 Exodus)
candidates.value: The earliest Greek catena-commentary. Preserves exegetical fragments of Philo, Origen, Eusebius of Emesa, Didymus and Theodoret; central to the Gaza school, where classical rhetoric met Christian exegesis.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: compiled excerpts require identifying their sources.
candidates.pilot_unit: Gen 1:1–2:3 (Hexaemeron section); est. 15–20k words

sweep:christian-late-antique.ru_gap_notes:
Texts with English but no (or minimal) Russian translation:
- Caesarius of Arles, Sermons: all 238 in English (FOTC); 3–4 in Russian.
- Origen, Munich Psalm homilies: English by Trigg (2021).
- Eusebius, Praeparatio: English by Gifford (1903); Russian has Book XI only.
- Eusebius, Demonstratio evangelica: English by Ferrar (1920); no Russian listed by pravenc.
- Pseudo-Clementines: English in ANF 8.
- Didymus on Genesis, Zechariah, Job and Psalms: English in FOTC and others; Russian none.
- Ambrosiaster's Pauline commentary: English (IVP 2009; SBL 2017); Russian has only ACCS snippets.
- Cassiodorus, Expositio Psalmorum: English (Walsh, ACW); ru.wikipedia cites Russian only for the Institutiones.
- Life of Hypatius (English: Storin 2024) and Miracles of Thecla (English: DOML 12, 2012): Russian status unverified.

sweep:greek-rhetoric.corpus_overview:
Coverage in this corpus is very uneven. In Russian, several works are complete: Libanius' 64 orations (Shestakov 1912–16, repr. 2014) and Synesius (Sidash 2012–14). Aristides is growing through Mezheritskaya (2006, 2017, plus journal pieces). Partial: Themistius about 9 of 34 orations (1961–85; Shabaga in Aristeas, Or. 14, 18, 19), Dio about 16 of 80, Maximus 7 of 41, Himerius 7 of about 80, Choricius 2 pieces, Aeneas 9 of 25 letters, Theophylact 19 of 85 letters, Alciphron in selections. Libanius' 1,544 letters: only a few dozen in Russian. His 51 declamations: 4. Nothing was found in Russian for his progymnasmata, Procopius of Gaza's letters, Syrianus or Sopater.

English is nearly complete for Aristides (Behr), Dio (Loeb), Maximus (Trapp), Himerius (Penella), Themistius (Penella 2000, Heather–Moncur 2001, Swain 2021), the Heroicus and the progymnasmata (Kennedy, Gibson). About two-thirds of Libanius' letters exist in some modern language (BMCR 2024.01.47), but English has only selections. Choricius' 8 orations, Procopius' letters, Theophylact's letters and the Hermogenes commentaries have no scholarly English.

Key caveat: romanletters.org (2026) has published unvetted Claude-made English for 7,597 letters, including Libanius (1,054) and Procopius of Gaza (166). It is a direct precedent and competitor. Neoscholia's edge would be the critical apparatus and the visible review process.

Method note: the WebSearch quota ran out. Statuses rest on Russian and English Wikipedia bibliographies, BMCR, Myriobiblion, ΣΧΟΛΗ, Aristeas and archive.org. The Russian status of Hermogenes, Aphthonius and Menander Rhetor remains unverified.

candidates.title: Choricius of Gaza, Orations I–VIII (Laudationes Marciani I–II, Laudatio Aratii et Stephani, Laudatio Summi, Epithalamia, Epitaphioi for Maria and Procopius) / Хорикий Газский, Речи
candidates.author: Choricius of Gaza
candidates.genre: Epideictic oratory: encomia (with church ekphrasis), wedding speeches, funeral orations
candidates.size: 8 orations; estimated 30,000–35,000 words (estimate, not counted)
candidates.edition: Foerster & Richtsteig, Choricii Gazaei opera (Teubner 1929, repr. 1972); 1929 imprint is US public domain. Boissonade 1846 (public domain, partial corpus): archive.org/details/choriciigazaeio00boisgoog
candidates.ru_evidence: Russian Wikipedia 'Хорикий Газский' lists only the Apologia mimorum (Freyberg 1968) and the Brumalia speech (Bolgov 2016), and states that no work has a complete Russian translation. Orations I–VIII are absent.
candidates.en_evidence: BMCR 2010.10.02: Penella 2009 translates only the declamations and dialexeis; the eight orations are not in it. Litsas 1980 is an unpublished Chicago dissertation (scope unverified).
candidates.other_translations: Italian: Or. VII–VIII by C. Greco 2010 (BMCR 2011.12.41); Or. VIII also by Corcella in Amato (ed.) 2010. French or German for Or. I–VI: none found.
candidates.value: Main literary source for 6th-century Gaza: ekphraseis of the churches of St Sergius and St Stephen (art history, archaeology, mosaics), civic and episcopal elite, Christian sophistic under Justinian. Used by Byzantinists, art historians and historians of rhetoric. No Russian and no published English.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium-high. Atticist prose, dense allusion and ekphrastic and architectural terms. Penella's version of the declamations helps calibrate style. Architectural vocabulary needs expert review.
candidates.pilot_unit: Laudatio Marciani I (Or. I), including the St Sergius ekphrasis; estimated about 7,000 words.

candidates.title: Procopius of Gaza, Letters (Ἐπιστολαί), about 162–166 letters / Прокопий Газский, Письма
candidates.author: Procopius of Gaza
candidates.genre: Literary epistolography (friendship, patronage and school letters)
candidates.size: About 166 letters; about 25,000 Greek words (my estimate from the OCR of Hercher's text)
candidates.edition: Garzya & Loenertz 1963 (Ettal). Public domain: Hercher, Epistolographi Graeci (1873), archive.org/details/epistolographoih00hercuoft. Italian edition: Amato et al. 2010.
candidates.ru_evidence: Russian Wikipedia 'Прокопий Газский' lists works and modern editions but no Russian translation. None on Myriobiblion, the Russian Byzantine-texts library.
candidates.en_evidence: No scholarly English found (BMCR reviews mention only Italian and French work). romanletters.org (2026) has unvetted Claude-made English of all 166 letters, labelled non-authoritative.
candidates.other_translations: Italian: F. Ciccolella in E. Amato (ed.), Rose di Gaza (2010), BMCR 2011.10.10. The French Budé volume (2014) covers the rhetorical works, not the letters (BMCR 2015.03.48).
candidates.value: Core of the 'School of Gaza': a network of sophists, bishops, officials and pupils in Palestine around 500. Key for late antique education, Christian–classical paideia and prosopography. The short letters suit a bilingual, annotated scholarly edition.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Short, formulaic Atticist letters. Main risks are allusions and identifying addressees (PLRE), so the commentary needs expert prosopographical checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Letters 1–40 (Hercher numbering), about 6,000 words.

candidates.title: Libanius, Letters not yet translated in full: Foerster nos. 494–839 and 1113–1540 (the 355–365 corpus) / Либаний, Письма
candidates.author: Libanius of Antioch
candidates.size: About 770 letters in these ranges. BMCR estimates that about one-third of the 1,544 letters (about 500) are untranslated into any modern language.
candidates.edition: Foerster, Libanii opera X–XI (Teubner 1921–22), public domain; scans on archive.org.
candidates.ru_evidence: Russian Wikipedia 'Либаний': only selected letters to Julian, Modestus and Themistius (Grabar-Passek 1964). No other Russian letter translations listed.
candidates.en_evidence: Selections only: Norman (Loeb 1992), Bradbury 2004, Cribiore 2007, Bradbury & Moncur 2023 (273 letters of 388–393; BMCR 2024.01.47). romanletters.org has unvetted AI English for 1,054 letters ('thematic renderings').
candidates.other_translations: Spanish: letters 1–493 (González Gálvez, Gredos 2005). Italian: letters 840–1112 (Pellizzari 2017). Both per BMCR 2024.01.47.
candidates.value: The largest pagan letter collection of Late Antiquity and the backbone of PLRE prosopography. Key for provincial government, the curial class, Julian's reign and the Antiochene school. A complete scholarly rendering of the remaining third would be a real first.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. Terse, allusive and prosopographically dense; needs Seeck/PLRE dating and consistent naming conventions. Well suited to multi-model cross-review against the English selections.
candidates.pilot_unit: Foerster 494–600 (about 105 letters, estimated about 12,000 words), after removing letters already in English selections.

candidates.title: Theophylact Simocatta, Letters (Ἐπιστολαὶ ἠθικαί, ἀγροικικαί, ἑταιρικαί): 85 fictional letters / Феофилакт Симокатта, Письма
candidates.author: Theophylact Simocatta
candidates.size: 85 letters; about 7,500–8,000 words (my estimate from Hercher's text)
candidates.edition: Zanetto, Teubner 1985. Public domain: Hercher, Epistolographi Graeci (1873), archive.org. Copernicus' Latin version of 1509.
candidates.ru_evidence: 19 of 85 letters (I–V, XV, XIX–XXI, XXXIV, XXXVIII–XL, L, LI, LXI, LXXXIII–LXXXV) translated by T. A. Miller in Памятники византийской литературы IV–IX вв. (1968), pp. 244–249; online at myriobiblion.byzantion.ru/feofilact.htm
candidates.en_evidence: No English translation found. English Wikipedia lists only Copernicus' Latin (1509); a BMCR search shows none. The work is not on romanletters.org.
candidates.other_translations: Latin: Copernicus 1509 (reprinted Hipler 1873). Modern-language translations: none found (unverified).
candidates.value: The last flowering of the Alciphron/Aelian fictional-letter genre, bridging the Second Sophistic and Byzantium. Copernicus' only self-published book was its translation. Appeals to historians of literature and science and to general readers.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Short, self-contained, mannered prose; the mythological and proverbial allusions are easy to annotate. Can be completed and fully reviewed quickly.
candidates.pilot_unit: The whole collection (85 letters, about 8,000 words), an ideal first complete publication.

candidates.title: Dio Chrysostom, Orations 1–4 On Kingship (Περὶ βασιλείας; Or. 4 'Alexander and Diogenes') / Дион Хрисостом, Речи о царской власти
candidates.author: Dio Chrysostom (Dio of Prusa)
candidates.size: 4 orations; estimated about 25,000 words (Or. 4 about 8,000)
candidates.edition: von Arnim, Dionis Prusaensis opera I (1893), public domain. Loeb Greek–English, Dio Chrysostom vol. I (Cohoon 1932).
candidates.ru_evidence: Russian Wikipedia 'Дион Хрисостом' lists Russian translations only of Or. 6–12, 18, 21, 36, 51, 53 and 55; Or. 1–4 (and 31–34) are absent.
candidates.en_evidence: Loeb Classical Library, Dio Chrysostom I (J. W. Cohoon, 1932), covering Or. 1–11. Other modern English versions exist.
candidates.other_translations: Several full translations into Western European languages (Spanish, Italian, German); not individually re-verified.
candidates.value: Central text for Trajanic imperial ideology and Cynic-Stoic kingship theory. Or. 2 and Or. 4 stage Alexander with Philip and with Diogenes, so it is directly relevant to Alexander studies. A notable gap for Russian readers.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Clear Atticist prose with rich secondary literature for cross-checking; low lexical risk.
candidates.pilot_unit: Or. 4 (Alexander and Diogenes), about 8,000 words.

candidates.title: Philostratus, Heroicus (Ἡρωικός) / Флавий Филострат, Героик
candidates.author: Flavius Philostratus
candidates.size: Estimated about 20,000–25,000 words
candidates.edition: de Lannoy, Teubner 1977. Public domain: Kayser, Teubner 1870–71 (archive.org).
candidates.ru_evidence: Russian Wikipedia 'Флавий Филострат' lists Russian versions of the Life of Apollonius, Gymnasticus (2021, 2022), Imagines, Lives of the Sophists and Letters, but not the Heroicus.
candidates.en_evidence: Maclean & Aitken, Flavius Philostratus: Heroikos (SBL 2001); Rusten & König, Loeb (2014). Both cited from memory and not re-checked online this session.
candidates.other_translations: German, French and Italian versions exist (not re-verified).
candidates.value: A vinedresser and a Phoenician discuss the cult of Protesilaus and a 'corrected' Trojan War against Homer. Key for hero cult, Homer reception, Dictys/Dares-type revisionism and Second Sophistic Hellenism. Widely taught.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Readable dialogue prose; the many heroic-cult realia need commentary, which existing literature supports well.
candidates.pilot_unit: Opening frame and the Protesilaus section (first third), estimated about 7,000 words.

candidates.title: Aelius Aristides, Platonic orations: Or. 2 To Plato: In Defence of Oratory; Or. 3 In Defence of the Four; Or. 4 To Capito / Элий Аристид, Против Платона
candidates.author: Aelius Aristides
candidates.size: Or. 2 and Or. 3 are very long; estimated 70,000–80,000 words in total. Or. 4 is short (about 4,000).
candidates.edition: Lenz & Behr (Brill, 1976–80). Public domain: Dindorf 1829 (archive.org).
candidates.ru_evidence: Russian Wikipedia 'Элий Аристид': Mezheritskaya covers the Sacred Tales, To Rome, funeral orations and monodies, the Egyptian and Smyrnaean orations and the hymns. Aristeas adds minor pieces. Or. 2–4 are not listed.
candidates.en_evidence: Behr, Complete Works I (Brill 1986); Trapp, Loeb (2017 for Or. 1–2, 2021 for Or. 3–4). Cited from memory and not re-checked online.
candidates.other_translations: Italian and French versions of Or. 2 exist (not re-verified).
candidates.value: The fullest ancient reply to Plato's Gorgias: a defence of rhetoric and of Pericles, Miltiades, Cimon and Themistocles. Central for the rhetoric–philosophy quarrel and for Platonism in the Second Sophistic.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium-high. Long, periodic Atticist argument with many quotations from Plato. Can be cross-checked against Behr and Trapp.
candidates.pilot_unit: Or. 4 To Capito (short, self-contained), then Or. 2 §§1–100.

candidates.title: Libanius, Declamations (Μελέται), 51 pieces; unit = those absent from the Russian, English and German selections / Либаний, Декламации
candidates.author: Libanius of Antioch
candidates.size: 51 declamations in Foerster vols. V–VII (three Teubner volumes); several hundred thousand words (estimate)
candidates.edition: Foerster, Libanii opera V–VII (Teubner 1909–13), public domain; scans on archive.org.
candidates.ru_evidence: Russian Wikipedia 'Либаний': Decl. 1 (Raytsina 1997) and Decl. 26, 28, 29 (Grabar-Passek 1961/1964) only.
candidates.en_evidence: D. A. Russell, Libanius: Imaginary Speeches, a selection (1996), per German Wikipedia and BMCR 2013.02.38. No complete English found.
candidates.other_translations: German: U. Lempp, Libanios: Musterreden (2015), scope unverified. Other single pieces may exist.
candidates.value: The largest Greek declamation corpus: classical Athens, Homer and New Comedy re-performed in a 4th-century school. Key for education, reception of Demosthenes and Socrates, and the Byzantine rhetorical canon.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium-high. Long and rhetorically regular Attic prose; stasis structure helps alignment. Requires checking for overlap with Russell and Lempp first.
candidates.pilot_unit: One historical declamation not in Russell or Lempp (to be chosen after checking their contents), about 8,000–10,000 words.

candidates.title: Syrianus, Commentaries on Hermogenes' On Ideas and On Issues (In Hermogenem commentaria) / Сириан, Комментарии к Гермогену
candidates.author: Syrianus (Athenian Neoplatonist; attribution partly debated)
candidates.size: 2 Teubner volumes (Rabe); estimated about 300 pages
candidates.edition: Rabe, Syriani in Hermogenem commentaria I–II (Teubner 1892–93), public domain; raw Greek OCR on Lace.
candidates.ru_evidence: No Russian translation found: nothing in Russian Wikipedia; the ΣΧΟΛΗ article index (Neoplatonism-focused) shows none.
candidates.en_evidence: Only the introduction to On Ideas ('Syrianus'), in Baltzly & Share 2025, Ancient Commentators series (BMCR 2025.10.46). The commentaries proper: none found.
candidates.other_translations: None found.
candidates.value: A Neoplatonist scholarch (Proclus' teacher) reads school rhetoric. Evidence for the canonisation of Hermogenes, Platonic theory of style, and lost rhetoricians. Specialists in rhetoric, Neoplatonism and Byzantine education.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. Technical stasis and 'ideas' terminology needs a fixed glossary aligned with Heath, Wooten and Patillon. The repetitive lemma-and-comment structure suits AI.
candidates.pilot_unit: Commentary on On Ideas, opening section (Rabe vol. I, first about 40 pages), about 10,000 words.

candidates.title: Sopater, Division of Questions (Διαιρέσεις ζητημάτων) / Сопатр, Разделение вопросов
candidates.author: Sopater (rhetor; identity and date debated)
candidates.genre: Rhetorical handbook: invention for declamation themes
candidates.size: About 80 themes; Walz, Rhetores Graeci vol. VIII (estimated several hundred pages)
candidates.edition: Walz, Rhetores Graeci VIII (1835), public domain (Google Books / archive.org).
candidates.ru_evidence: No Russian translation found in the Russian sources checked (Russian Wikipedia, ΣΧΟΛΗ index, Aristeas listing).
candidates.en_evidence: Innes & Winterbottom, Sopatros the Rhetor (BICS Suppl. 48, 1988): textual studies with partial renderings; the extent of translation is unverified (cited in BMCR 1998.03.13).
candidates.other_translations: None found.
candidates.value: The only worked handbook showing how historical themes (Athens, Demosthenes, Sparta) were argued through stasis in schools. Underpins modern reconstructions of declamation. Specialist but unique.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. Compressed technical prose with corrupt passages; needs the Innes–Winterbottom emendations and a stasis glossary.
candidates.pilot_unit: The first 10 themes, estimated about 15,000 words.

candidates.title: Himerius, Orations (Λόγοι), about 80 speeches and fragments / Гимерий, Речи
candidates.author: Himerius
candidates.size: About 80 orations, many fragmentary or in Photian excerpts; Colonna edition about 270 pages (estimate)
candidates.edition: Colonna 1951 (in copyright). Public domain: Dübner (Didot 1849) and Wernsdorf 1790.
candidates.ru_evidence: Russian Wikipedia 'Гимерий': only Or. 1, 3, 23 (Поздняя греческая проза, 1960) and Or. 12, 17, 18, 24 plus Ecl. 17 (Памятники... 1964).
candidates.en_evidence: R. J. Penella, Man and the Word: The Orations of Himerius (University of California Press 2007), a complete translation (from memory; not re-checked online).
candidates.other_translations: Italian and German partial versions exist (unverified).
candidates.value: Athenian sophist, teacher of Basil and Gregory of Nazianzus, linked to Julian. Key for 4th-century Athenian education, student life, and prose-hymn and propemptikon forms.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium-high. Poetic, image-laden prose and fragmentary excerpts; Penella can be used for cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Ten short school orations not among the Russian-translated Or. 1, 3, 12, 17, 18, 23, 24 (about 10,000 words).

candidates.title: Maximus of Tyre, Dissertations (Διαλέξεις), 41 lectures; unit = the 34 without Russian / Максим Тирский, Речи
candidates.author: Maximus of Tyre
candidates.size: 41 lectures, about 100,000 words in total (estimate)
candidates.edition: Trapp, Teubner 1994; Koniaris 1995. Public domain: Hobein, Teubner 1910.
candidates.ru_evidence: Russian Wikipedia: Or. 2 and Or. 36 (1961) and Or. 5 (1990). ΣΧΟΛΗ abstracts: new Russian translations of Or. 8–9 and 20–21. So 7 of 41.
candidates.en_evidence: M. B. Trapp, Maximus of Tyre: The Philosophical Orations (Oxford 1997), complete (from memory; not re-checked online).
candidates.other_translations: French and Italian versions exist (unverified).
candidates.value: Accessible popular Platonism on God, prayer, daimons, love, Homer and the Cynic life. Preserves lyric fragments (Sappho). Excellent for students; a major Russian gap in the Second Sophistic.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Lucid lecture prose; well-edited text; easy to cross-check with Trapp.
candidates.pilot_unit: Or. 11 (Who is God according to Plato?), estimated about 5,000 words.

candidates.title: Libanius, Progymnasmata (model exercises) / Либаний, Прогимнасмы
candidates.author: Libanius (with some pseudepigrapha)
candidates.genre: School rhetoric: fables, narrations, chreiai, encomia, ethopoeiae, ekphraseis
candidates.size: About 96 pieces (Spanish Wikipedia count); Foerster vol. VIII (several hundred pages, including spuria)
candidates.edition: Foerster, Libanii opera VIII (Teubner 1915), public domain; archive.org.
candidates.ru_evidence: Russian Wikipedia 'Либаний' lists Russian translations of orations, letters and declamations, but none of the progymnasmata.
candidates.en_evidence: C. A. Gibson, Libanius's Progymnasmata (SBL, Writings from the Greco-Roman World 27, 2008), complete (from memory; not re-checked online).
candidates.other_translations: Not verified.
candidates.value: Model exercises from the most influential late antique school. Short myths, fables and ekphraseis teach both rhetoric and mythology; foundational for Byzantine education. Ideal for students and teaching.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Short, self-contained, formulaic pieces suited to batch translation and visible review.
candidates.pilot_unit: The narrations (διηγήματα) and fables as a block, estimated about 6,000 words.

sweep:greek-rhetoric.ru_gap_notes:
Texts with an English translation but no Russian one:
- Dio Chrysostom, Or. 1–4 (Kingship) and the civic Or. 31–51.
- Aelius Aristides, Or. 2–4 and most of Or. 5–25.
- Maximus of Tyre: 34 of 41 lectures.
- Himerius: about 70 orations.
- Philostratus' Heroicus.
- Libanius' Progymnasmata (Gibson 2008) and most of his declamations.
- Themistius' political orations: English complete with Swain 2021; Shabaga is filling the Russian gap in Aristeas.
- Aeneas of Gaza's Theophrastus with Zacharias' Ammonius: English 2012; Russian not found.
- Polemo's declamations: English Reader 1996 (not re-verified).
- Progymnasmata of Theon, Aphthonius and Nicolaus, and Hermogenes' On Issues and On Ideas: English by Kennedy, Heath and Wooten; Russian status unverified.

Already covered in Russian, so drop: Isidore of Pelusium (19th-century Russian translation, not re-checked here), Synesius (Sidash), Aristaenetus (Polyakova), Callistratus (Kondratiev 1936).

candidates.title: Res gestae Alexandri Macedonis (Latin Alexander Romance) / Deeds of Alexander of Macedon / RU: Юлий Валерий, «Деяния Александра Македонского»
candidates.author: Iulius Valerius Alexander Polemius (probably the consul of 338)
candidates.date: early to mid 4th c. CE (Wikipedia gives 270–330 or 360–380)
candidates.genre: Novelistic biography; adaptation of the Ps.-Callisthenes α recension
candidates.size: 3 books; est. 35–40k words. Kuebler's edition appends the Collatio Alexandri cum Dindimo and the Epistola ad Aristotelem
candidates.edition: Rosellini, Teubner 1993 (corr. 2004; in copyright). Public-domain Kuebler, Teubner 1888: https://archive.org/details/iulivalerialexan00vale
candidates.ru_evidence: Absent from the ancientrome.ru catalogue, the vostlit.info А–Я indexes and the simposium.ru source list. No ru.wikipedia article (404). No Russian translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia (Res gestae Alexandri Macedonis) mentions no translation. Open Library lists only French versions. No English translation found; confirm in WorldCat/BMCR.
candidates.other_translations: French: J.-P. Callu, Julius Valère, Roman d'Alexandre (Brepols 2010); F. Foubert, La geste d'Alexandre le Grand (Peeters 2014). No German, Italian or Spanish found.
candidates.value: The earliest Latin Alexander Romance and a faithful witness to the lost α recension. Through the Zacher Epitome it is the source of the medieval Western Alexander tradition. Core text for Alexander-Romance studies, late Latin and reception studies; matches the editor's own PhD field. Ideal flagship.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: narrative late Latin. The Greek α text (Kroll 1926) and the Armenian/Syriac versions allow parallel checking. Risks: Graecizing syntax, Kuebler vs Rosellini readings.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book I (Nectanebo, birth, education, Bucephalas; est. 12–14k words)

candidates.title: Q. Aurelius Symmachus, Epistulae (Letters, Books 1–10) / RU: Симмах, «Письма»
candidates.author: Q. Aurelius Symmachus (c. 345–402)
candidates.date: c. 365–402 CE; edited after his death by his son
candidates.size: c. 900 letters; est. 100k+ words. Book 2 = 91 letters to Nicomachus Flavianus
candidates.edition: Seeck, MGH AA 6.1 (1883), public domain: https://archive.org/details/qaureliisymmach00seecgoog. Callu, Budé (1972–2002)
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia lists only Relatio 3 (Ranovich 1990) and a few letters (Strelnikova, Памятники позднего античного ораторского и эпистолярного искусства, 1964, pp. 205–212). Not on vostlit or ancientrome.
candidates.en_evidence: Book 1 only: Salzman & Roberts, The Letters of Symmachus (SBL 2011; Open Library). Relationes: Barrow 1973. en.wikipedia: 'little of his work has been translated into English'.
candidates.other_translations: French complete: Callu, Budé, 4 vols. Italian commentary volumes by book: Cecconi II, Pellizzari III, Marcone IV and VI, Rivolta Tiberga V, Roda IX.
candidates.value: A central source for the pagan senatorial elite and Theodosian politics (the era of the Altar of Victory dispute), for prosopography (PLRE) and for late Latin epistolography. Books 2–9 are closed to Russian and English readers.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: short, allusive, formulaic friendship letters. Needs prosopographical and dating control; the French and Italian versions can be used for checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book 2 (91 letters to Virius Nicomachus Flavianus; est. 8–10k words; no English translation)

candidates.title: Magnus Felix Ennodius, Epistulae and Dictiones (Letters; Declamations/Speeches) / RU: Эннодий, «Письма», «Речи»
candidates.author: Magnus Felix Ennodius (473/4–521), bishop of Pavia
candidates.size: 297 letters (9 books), 28 dictiones and opuscula incl. the Panegyric to Theoderic; est. 120k+ words
candidates.edition: Vogel, MGH AA 7 (1885), public domain: https://archive.org/details/magnifelicisenn00vogegoog. Hartel, CSEL 6 (1882). Gioanni, Budé (letters)
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Эннодий) lists editions only, no Russian translation. Absent from the ancientrome, vostlit and simposium catalogues.
candidates.en_evidence: Only the Vita Epiphanii (Cook 1942) and the poems (Mulligan, Poetry of Ennodius, Routledge 2022) found. No English translation of the letters or dictiones (en.wikipedia; Open Library).
candidates.other_translations: French: letters Books I–IV (Gioanni, Budé 2006, 2010). German: Panegyric (Rohr, MGH 1995). Italian: Panegyric (2002). Later letter books: none found.
candidates.value: A key witness to Ostrogothic Italy, the Laurentian schism, rhetorical schooling and Boethius' circle. Largely inaccessible to non-Latinists.
candidates.ai_feasibility: low–medium: notoriously obscure, mannered Latin with textual cruxes. A good showcase for visible disagreement between models and arbitration by the human editor.
candidates.pilot_unit: Letters Book V, beyond the published Budé volumes (est. 8–10k words); or the Panegyric to Theoderic (est. 6k words)

candidates.title: Marcellus (Empiricus), De medicamentis liber (On Remedies) / RU: Марцелл Эмпирик, «О лекарствах»
candidates.author: Marcellus of Bordeaux, magister officiorum 394–395
candidates.size: Preface, prefatory epistles and 36 chapters arranged head to foot; 255 pp. in Niedermann; est. 90–100k words
candidates.edition: Niedermann, CML V (1916; 2nd ed. 1968). Helmreich, Teubner 1889, public domain: https://archive.org/details/marcellidemedic00unkngoog
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia lists only the German translation. Not in ancientrome, vostlit or simposium. The 1980 anthology 'Медицина в памятниках латинской литературы' may contain excerpts (unverified).
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia mentions no translation. Open Library shows only the German translation (1968) and German studies.
candidates.other_translations: German complete: Kollesch & Nickel, CML V (Akademie-Verlag 1968). No complete French or Italian found.
candidates.value: A unique view of Gallo-Roman everyday medicine, magic and Christianization. Contains Gaulish plant names and charms (important for Celtic studies), links to Ausonius' circle, and preserves earlier Latin pharmacology. Used by historians of medicine, Celticists and Latinists.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: recipes are formulaic. Plant and drug identification, measures, vulgarisms and charms need an expert lexicographic check.
candidates.pilot_unit: Preface, prefatory epistles and Chapter 8 (eye diseases, with charms); est. 12–15k words

candidates.title: Itinerarium Alexandri + Epitoma rerum gestarum Alexandri (Metz Epitome) with the Liber de morte testamentoque Alexandri / RU: «Итинерарий Александра», «Мецская эпитома»
candidates.author: Anonymous (the Itinerarium is sometimes attributed to Julius Valerius); anonymous epitomator
candidates.date: Itinerarium c. 340 (dedicated to Constantius II); Metz Epitome 4th–5th c.
candidates.genre: Historical breviary; epitome; Successor-period propaganda pamphlet (Liber de morte)
candidates.size: Itinerarium est. 8–10k words; Metz Epitome (c. 123 sections incl. the Liber de morte) est. 10–12k words
candidates.edition: Itinerarium: Tabacco (Olschki 2000); Mai 1817, public domain: https://archive.org/details/itinerariumalex00unkngoog. Metz Epitome: Thomas, Teubner 1960/66 (in copyright)
candidates.ru_evidence: Neither text appears in the ancientrome, vostlit or simposium catalogues. No Russian translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: The Liber de morte is translated in Heckel, The Last Days and Testament of Alexander the Great (1988; Open Library). An English Itinerarium (Davies, AHB 1998) is reported but unverified here.
candidates.other_translations: Itinerarium: Italian (Tabacco 2000), German (Hausmann 1970). Metz Epitome: no complete modern translation found.
candidates.value: Independent Latin Alexander historiography: the Itinerarium draws on Arrian, the Metz Epitome on the Clitarchan 'vulgate' tradition, plus a propaganda pamphlet on Alexander's death. Natural companion to Julius Valerius and within the editor's specialism.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: plain historiographic Latin. Arrian, Diodorus and Curtius allow systematic checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Liber de morte testamentoque Alexandri (Metz Epitome §§87–123; est. 4k words) or the whole Itinerarium

candidates.title: Rufius Festus Avienus, Aratea (Phaenomena) and Descriptio orbis terrae / RU: Авиен, «Явления Арата», «Описание круга земель»
candidates.author: Rufius Festus Avienus (fl. c. 350–380)
candidates.genre: Didactic poetry: astronomy (after Aratus) and geography (after Dionysius Periegetes)
candidates.size: Aratea 1,878 hexameters; Descriptio 1,393 hexameters
candidates.edition: Soubiran, Budé 1981 (Aratea); Van de Woestijne 1961 (Descriptio). Public-domain Aratea, Breysig 1882: https://archive.org/details/rufifestiavieni00aviegoog; Holder 1887
candidates.ru_evidence: Only Ora maritima (Kondratiev, ВДИ 1939 no. 2; simposium.ru/ru/node/10568) and Descriptio excerpts on Scythia and the Caucasus (ВДИ 1949; Античная география 1953). Aratea: none found.
candidates.en_evidence: English exists only for Ora maritima (Murphy, Ares; Roller 2021). Open Library shows no English Aratea or Descriptio.
candidates.other_translations: French: Aratea (Soubiran, Budé 1981); Descriptio (Despois & Saviot 1843). Spanish and Portuguese versions of Ora maritima.
candidates.value: Major 4th-c. pagan didactic poetry combining Stoic-Neoplatonic theology, astronomy and geography; reception of Aratus and Dionysius, and a model for medieval cosmography. For literary historians and historians of science.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: dense verse and star nomenclature. The Greek models (Aratus, Dionysius) and the Latin versions of Cicero and Germanicus allow line-by-line control.
candidates.pilot_unit: Descriptio orbis terrae complete (1,393 lines, est. 9k words), or the Aratea proem plus the first c. 300 lines

candidates.title: Expositio totius mundi et gentium (Description of the Whole World and Its Peoples) / RU: «Описание всего мира и народов»
candidates.author: Anonymous (Greek original, possibly by a Syrian merchant); anonymous Latin translators
candidates.date: Greek original 350–362 CE; surviving Latin versions 6th c.
candidates.size: 67 chapters; est. 6–7k words; two Latin versions
candidates.edition: Rougé, Sources Chrétiennes 124 (1966); Cioffi, Teubner (De Gruyter 2025). Public-domain Riese, Geographi Latini Minores 1878: https://archive.org/details/geographilatinim00ries
candidates.ru_evidence: No ru.wikipedia article (404). Absent from the ancientrome, vostlit and simposium catalogues. No Russian translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: Only J. Woodman's 1964 Ohio State MA thesis, available online. en.wikipedia: a widely available printed English translation 'has never been published'.
candidates.other_translations: French: Rougé 1966. No Italian or German translation found.
candidates.value: A unique mid-4th-c. panorama of the empire's trade goods, cities, shows and peoples (Antioch, Alexandria, Persia), and important for vulgar Latin. Short, self-contained, with a new 2025 critical text: an ideal pilot.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium–high: short text but vulgar, corrupt Latin. The two versions check each other; the commentary must handle commodities and place names.
candidates.pilot_unit: Entire text, both Latin versions in parallel (67 chapters, est. 6–7k words)

candidates.title: Sidonius Apollinaris, Epistulae (Letters, 9 books) / RU: Сидоний Аполлинарий, «Письма» (RU-gap)
candidates.author: C. Sollius Modestus Apollinaris Sidonius (c. 430–c. 485), bishop of Clermont
candidates.size: 147 letters in 9 books; est. 65–70k words (plus 24 poems)
candidates.edition: Luetjohann, MGH AA 8 (1887), public domain: https://archive.org/details/gaisoliiapollin00ltgoog. Loyen, Budé
candidates.ru_evidence: Excerpts only: Trukhina, История Древнего Рима. Тексты и документы (2004), pp. 393–400; poems in Поздняя латинская поэзия (1982) and a 1998 anthology (per ru.wikipedia).
candidates.en_evidence: Anderson, Loeb (2 vols, 1936/1965); Dalton 1915, online (per en.wikipedia).
candidates.other_translations: French complete (Loyen, Budé). Many recent English and Italian commentaries on individual books.
candidates.value: Indispensable for the end of Roman Gaul: the Visigoths (portrait of Theoderic II), Euric, the siege of Clermont, the Gallo-Roman aristocracy. A first-rank gap in Russian.
candidates.ai_feasibility: low–medium: deliberately precious, allusive style. The English and French versions may be used for checking only, never as a base.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book 1 (11 letters, incl. 1.2 on Theoderic II; est. 7–8k words)

candidates.title: Cassiodorus, Variae, Books III–XII / RU: Кассиодор, «Варии» (кн. III–XII) (RU-gap)
candidates.author: Magnus Aurelius Cassiodorus Senator (c. 485–c. 580)
candidates.genre: Chancery letters, edicts and model letters for appointments (formulae)
candidates.size: 468 documents in 12 books; Books III–XII c. 380 documents, est. 90–100k words
candidates.edition: Mommsen, MGH AA 12 (1894), public domain: https://archive.org/details/cassiodorisenato00cass. Fridh, CCSL 96 (1973)
candidates.ru_evidence: Only Books I–II (V. G. Izosin) on ancientrome.ru/antlitr/cassiodorus. ru.wikipedia lists no Russian translation of the Variae.
candidates.en_evidence: Bjornlie, The Variae (University of California Press 2019, complete); Barnish, TTH 1992 (selection); Hodgkin 1886 (abridged). Cited from memory; not re-checked online here.
candidates.other_translations: Italian complete with commentary (Giardina et al., L'Erma, 2014–2017; from memory, not verified here).
candidates.value: The primary documentary source for Ostrogothic Italy: administration, diplomacy (Clovis, Alaric II), economy, urban life and late Roman ideology of rule.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: inflated but formulaic chancery rhetoric; the English and Italian versions are available for verification.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book III (53 letters, incl. Theoderic's diplomatic letters of 507; est. 10–12k words)

candidates.title: Servius (and 'Servius Danielis'), Commentarii in Vergilii Aeneidos libros, Books 2–12 / RU: Сервий, «Комментарии к Энеиде»
candidates.author: Maurus Servius Honoratus (fl. c. 400), plus a later expanded layer (Servius Danielis)
candidates.date: c. 400–420 CE; the expanded layer compiled 7th–8th c.
candidates.size: Aeneid commentary est. 300k+ words; Aen. 6 alone est. 25–30k words
candidates.edition: Thilo–Hagen (1878–1902), public domain: https://archive.org/details/serviigrammatic03thilgoog. Harvard Servius (Aen. 1–5)
candidates.ru_evidence: Book 1 only: N. A. Fedorov, in Вергилий. Энеида. С комментариями Сервия (Лабиринт 2001); see ancientrome.ru/antlitr/servius and ru.wikipedia.
candidates.en_evidence: Isolated books only, e.g. Aen. 4 (McDonough, Prior & Stansbury 2004; cited from memory, not re-checked). en.wikipedia lists no complete translation.
candidates.other_translations: No complete modern translation found.
candidates.value: The most influential ancient commentary on Latin poetry: grammar, religion, antiquarian lore and fragments of lost authors. The very model of 'scholia' for a platform called Neoscholia.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: plain didactic Latin. Difficulties: lemma layout and separating the Servian and expanded layers.
candidates.pilot_unit: Commentary on Aeneid 6 (underworld, religion and philosophy; est. 25–30k words), or Aen. 2 (est. 15–20k words)

candidates.title: Pelagonius, Ars veterinaria (Veterinary Medicine) / RU: Пелагоний, «Ветеринарное искусство»
candidates.author: Pelagonius, writing to named horse-owners
candidates.genre: Veterinary manual on horses, in letter form
candidates.size: c. 470 sections; est. 25–30k words
candidates.edition: Fischer, Teubner 1980 (in copyright). Ihm 1892, public domain: https://archive.org/details/pelagoniiartiav00pelagoog
candidates.ru_evidence: Not in the ancientrome, vostlit or simposium catalogues. No Russian translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia lists only the Fischer edition. Open Library shows Italian (2014) and French (2019) versions only; Adams 1995 is a linguistic study.
candidates.other_translations: Italian: Arte veterinaria (Società Dante Alighieri 2014). French: Recueil de médecine vétérinaire (Budé 2019). Italian translation of 1826.
candidates.value: The best-preserved Latin veterinary treatise. Evidence for aristocratic and circus horse culture, close parallels to the Greek hippiatric corpus, letters naming real addressees; a key source for the Latin technical vocabulary (Adams 1995).
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: formulaic recipes. Disease and drug terms need checking against the Greek hippiatric texts and Adams' lexicon.
candidates.pilot_unit: Preface and opening chapters on fever and head ailments (est. 5–6k words)

candidates.title: Iulius Firmicus Maternus, Mathesis (8 books) / RU: Фирмик Матерн, «Матесис» (RU-gap)
candidates.author: Iulius Firmicus Maternus, Sicilian senator
candidates.genre: Astrological handbook with a philosophical-apologetic frame
candidates.size: 8 books; Teubner 2 vols; est. 150k words
candidates.edition: Kroll–Skutsch–Ziegler, Teubner 1897–1913, public domain: https://archive.org/details/matheseoslibrivi02firmuoft. Monat, Budé 1992–97
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Юлий Фирмик Матерн) lists no translation. Absent from the ancientrome, vostlit and simposium catalogues.
candidates.en_evidence: Bram, Ancient Astrology (1975); Holden 2011; Dykes, Mathesis (Cazimi Press 2023; Open Library).
candidates.other_translations: French (Monat, Budé); German (Stiehle 2008); Italian Book 1 (Colombi 1996).
candidates.value: The largest Latin astrological work. Evidence for religion and society under Constantine (professions, slavery, sexuality) and for astrological doctrine; written before the author's Christian polemic. For historians of religion and science.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: clear prose with systematic terminology; the existing translations allow cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book 1 (the defence of astrology, incl. the account of Plotinus' death; est. 10k words)

candidates.title: Post-Theodosian Novels (Novellae of Theodosius II, Valentinian III, Marcian, Majorian, Severus, Anthemius) / RU: «Новеллы» после Кодекса Феодосия (RU-gap)
candidates.author: Imperial chanceries
candidates.size: c. 85 laws; est. 35–40k words; Majorian's Novels c. 12 laws
candidates.edition: Mommsen & Meyer, Theodosiani libri XVI, vol. II (1905), public domain: https://archive.org/details/theodosianilibri00codeuoft
candidates.ru_evidence: Only selections: Novels of Theodosius II translated by E. V. Silvestrova (История Древнего Рима. Тексты и документы, 2005, pp. 231–232). A full annotated translation of the Codex Theodosianus remains unpublished (ru.wikipedia).
candidates.en_evidence: Pharr, The Theodosian Code and Novels and the Sirmondian Constitutions (1952; Open Library).
candidates.other_translations: None confirmed for the Novels.
candidates.value: The last legislation of the Western Empire: taxation, city councillors (curiales), barbarian settlement, urban decline, Majorian's reforms. Essential for 5th-c. social and economic history.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: formulaic legal Latin; Pharr allows verification. The institutional commentary is the demanding part.
candidates.pilot_unit: Novellae Maioriani (458–460; c. 12 laws; est. 8k words)

candidates.title: Notitia Dignitatum (Eastern and Western parts) / List of Offices / RU: «Notitia dignitatum» (Перечень должностей)
candidates.author: Anonymous (office of the primicerius notariorum)
candidates.genre: Register of administrative and military posts, with illustrations
candidates.size: East 43 chapters, West 45 chapters; est. 15–20k words, mostly lists
candidates.edition: Seeck 1876, public domain: https://archive.org/details/notitiadignitat00seecgoog. Neira Faleiro, Madrid 2005
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia (Notitia dignitatum) lists editions and studies but no translation. Absent from the vostlit, ancientrome and simposium catalogues.
candidates.en_evidence: Fairley, Notitia Dignitatum or Register of Dignitaries (University of Pennsylvania 1899; Open Library). Dated and without commentary.
candidates.other_translations: None confirmed.
candidates.value: Fundamental for late Roman army units, the civil administration, state arms factories (fabricae) and frontier commands; a standard reference for military historians and archaeologists of the frontier (limes). A Russian version with commentary on the units would be widely used.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high for the text (lists); medium for the commentary (identifying units, insignia, archaeology).
candidates.pilot_unit: East, chs. I–IX (prefects and magistri militum with their unit lists; est. 4–5k words)

sweep:latin-late-antique.ru_gap_notes:
Texts available in English but missing in Russian, or present only in snippets:
- Sidonius' Letters (Loeb; Dalton 1915)
- Cassiodorus' Variae III–XII (Bjornlie 2019)
- Firmicus' Mathesis (Bram 1975; Holden 2011; Dykes 2023)
- Theodosian Code and Novels (Pharr 1952; Russian has only selections)
- Corpus agrimensorum (Campbell 2000; Russian excerpts 2004)
- Notitia Dignitatum (Fairley 1899)
- Liber Pontificalis (Davis, TTH)
- Symmachus' Relationes (Barrow 1973; Russian has only Relatio 3)
- Ennodius' poems (Mulligan 2022)
- Optatian (Hall 2024)
- Caelius Aurelianus (Drabkin 1950)
- Palladius' Opus agriculturae (Fitch 2013)
- Vegetius' Mulomedicina (1748)
- Anthimus (Grant)

The Russian status of the last five rests only on their absence from the ancientrome, vostlit and simposium catalogues; journals (cyberleninka, elibrary) were not searched.

candidates.title: Mesopotamian cuneiform commentaries (mukallimtu/ṣâtu) – 'Babylonian scholia'; unit: commentaries on literary works (Enūma eliš VII, Ludlul, Theodicy, Lugale) / Месопотамские клинописные комментарии
candidates.author: Anonymous Assyrian and Babylonian scholars (ummânū)
candidates.size: 882 catalogue entries (CCP); pilot c. 10–15 tablets, est. under 1,000 lines
candidates.edition: CCP online editions (Frahm, Jiménez et al.) under CC BY-SA 4.0 (ccp.yale.edu/citation-guidelines); Frahm, Babylonian and Assyrian Text Commentaries (2011). Photos copyright of the museums.
candidates.ru_evidence: No Russian translation found. CyberLeninka 'клинописные комментарии' returns only studies; no ru.wikipedia article on the genre.
candidates.en_evidence: CCP gives annotated English translations for part of the 882 catalogue entries (ccp.yale.edu/catalogue); many remain unedited.
candidates.other_translations: Scattered German/French in articles; no full corpus translation found.
candidates.value: Earliest systematic commentary tradition, parallel to Greek scholia and Alexandrian philology. Key for hermeneutics, the milieu of Berossus and the history of science. A programmatic match for the 'Neoscholia' name.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: transliterations exist, but etymological wordplay, polyvalent signs and Sumerian equations need expert control. An ideal showcase for visible multi-model review.
candidates.pilot_unit: CCP literary section: commentaries on Enūma eliš VII (names of Marduk), Ludlul, Theodicy; c. 10–15 tablets

candidates.title: Babylonian Astronomical Diaries (historical sections) + Hellenistic chronicles BCHP 1–20, 333–61 BCE / Астрономические дневники и эллинистические хроники Вавилона
candidates.author: Anonymous Esagila astronomers, Babylon
candidates.size: 20 chronicles + historical notes from dozens of diaries; est. 15–25k words
candidates.edition: Sachs & Hunger, Astronomical Diaries I–III (1988–96); Finkel, van der Spek, Pirngruber, BCHP (SBL WAW; livius.org). Both copyrighted.
candidates.ru_evidence: No corpus translation found. ru.wikipedia links 'Вавилонские астрономические дневники' only to the English article; passages are used in Russian studies (Сивкина–Кривощекова 2023, CyberLeninka).
candidates.en_evidence: Sachs–Hunger translations of the Hellenistic diaries (attalus.org/docs/diaries.html); BCHP 1–20 in English on livius.org.
candidates.other_translations: Italian selection (Del Monte 1997), not re-verified.
candidates.value: The only contemporary Babylonian view of Alexander (Gaugamela, entry into Babylon, death), the Diadochi, Seleucids and Parthians. An essential control for Arrian, Diodorus and Curtius, and directly within the editor's Alexander expertise.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high-medium: formulaic dating and astronomy, transliterations available. Fragmentary lines need disciplined non-restoration. Existing English used only for cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Alexander years 333–322 BCE: diaries −330 (Gaugamela), −324, −322 + BCHP 1–4; c. 300–400 lines

candidates.title: Akkadian literary predictive texts ('prophecies'): Dynastic Prophecy (BM 40623), Uruk, Marduk, Šulgi Prophecies, Text A / Аккадские «пророчества», «Династическое пророчество»
candidates.author: Anonymous
candidates.date: 12th c. BCE (Marduk) to early Hellenistic (Dynastic Prophecy, after 331 BCE)
candidates.size: 5 texts, est. 400–600 lines, partly fragmentary
candidates.edition: Grayson, Babylonian Historical-Literary Texts (1975); Neujahr, Predicting the Past (2012). Both copyrighted.
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia full-text search for 'Династическое пророчество' gives 1 hit (a mention in 'Набонид'); CyberLeninka shows no translation.
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia lists the Dynastic and Uruk Prophecies among Akkadian literature; standard English editions are Grayson 1975 and Neujahr 2012 (not re-verified online).
candidates.other_translations: German (Borger; TUAT), not re-verified.
candidates.value: Babylonian ex eventu view of the fall of Darius III and of Alexander. Background for Daniel, the Oracle of the Potter, the Demotic Chronicle and prophecy motifs in the Alexander Romance. Small and high-impact.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: short and heavily studied. The contested restorations (Alexander/Darius passage) are an ideal showcase for visible disagreement between models.
candidates.pilot_unit: Dynastic Prophecy complete (one 4-column tablet) + Uruk Prophecy

candidates.title: Enūma Anu Enlil, Tablets 1–6 (lunar visibility omens) / «Энума Ану Энлиль», таблицы 1–6
candidates.author: Babylonian/Assyrian celestial diviners (canonical series)
candidates.date: Compiled late 2nd–early 1st mill. BCE; Nineveh manuscripts 7th c. BCE
candidates.size: 6 tablets, est. several hundred omens (~1,000 lines)
candidates.edition: Verderame, Le tavole I–VI della serie astrologica Enūma Anu Enlil (2002, Italian); Virolleaud, L'Astrologie chaldéenne (1905–12, public-domain copies).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Энума Ану Энлиль' cites no translation (only a pop-science book); none found elsewhere.
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia: Tablets 1–6 are edited only in Italian (Verderame 2002); 'less than half of the series' is in English.
candidates.other_translations: Italian full (Verderame 2002).
candidates.value: Foundation of Babylonian celestial divination and the root of Hellenistic astrology (Greek lunar omens, Hephaestion, John Lydus). Key for classicists studying 'Chaldaean' science.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: rigidly formulaic protasis/apodosis with conventional logograms. Technical terms and broken entries need expert verification.
candidates.pilot_unit: Tablets 1–2

candidates.title: Hellenistic temple rituals of Babylon and Uruk (Babylon Akītu ritual; Uruk rituals, TU 38–44) / Ритуалы Вавилона и Урука селевкидского времени
candidates.author: Anonymous priests (Seleucid-era copies)
candidates.size: c. 10 tablets, est. c. 1,000 lines
candidates.edition: Thureau-Dangin, Rituels accadiens (1921; public domain, archive.org); Linssen, The Cults of Uruk and Babylon (2004).
candidates.ru_evidence: CyberLeninka ('акиту ритуал перевод', 'Урук эллинистический ритуал') finds no translation; possible excerpts in В.В. Емельянов's ritual studies (unverified).
candidates.en_evidence: Linssen 2004 (not re-verified online); partial in ANET (Sachs).
candidates.other_translations: French full (Thureau-Dangin 1921, public domain).
candidates.value: Cult in Seleucid Babylonia, including the king's ritual humiliation at the Akītu. Crucial for Hellenistic kingship, Antiochus I, Berossus and Greek–Babylonian interaction.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium-high: prose instructions; the public-domain French edition gives transliteration. Sumerian incantation passages are harder.
candidates.pilot_unit: Babylon Akītu ritual (DT 15, DT 109, MNB 1848), est. c. 450 lines

candidates.title: Demotic Chronicle (P. Paris BN 215 recto) / «Демотическая хроника»
candidates.author: Anonymous Egyptian priest(s)
candidates.size: c. 6 papyrus columns (estimate)
candidates.edition: Spiegelberg, Die sogenannte demotische Chronik (1914; public domain, archive.org); Felber 2002 (German); Quack 2015 (study).
candidates.ru_evidence: No Russian translation found: ru.wikipedia mentions it only in a navbox; CyberLeninka hits are studies (Ладынин) citing it.
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia points to an annotated English course translation (yorku.ca/pswarney/2110/dem-chron); no standard published English found.
candidates.other_translations: German (Spiegelberg 1914; Felber 2002); Italian (Bresciani 1969).
candidates.value: Egyptian verdict on Persian rule, Teos, Nectanebo I–II and the Greeks. An oracle with commentary, i.e. Egyptian 'scholia'. Vital for Ptolemaic ideology and the Nectanebo legend of the Alexander Romance.
candidates.ai_feasibility: low-medium: LLMs are weak in Demotic. Work from Spiegelberg's public-domain transcription; cryptic oracle phrasing needs an Egyptologist reviewer.
candidates.pilot_unit: Entire text (c. 6 columns)

candidates.title: Letters from Assyrian and Babylonian Scholars (SAA 10), incl. substitute-king dossier / Письма ассирийских и вавилонских учёных
candidates.author: Court scholars of Esarhaddon and Assurbanipal
candidates.size: SAA 10: 389 letters; also SAA 8 astrological reports
candidates.edition: Parpola, SAA 10 (1993); Hunger, SAA 8 (1992); online at SAAo/ORACC (licence to verify).
candidates.ru_evidence: CyberLeninka ('заместительный царь ассирийские письма', 'ассирийские астрологи письма перевод') finds no translation; none found.
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia State Archives of Assyria: SAA 8 (Hunger 1992) and SAA 10 (Parpola 1993) with English translations.
candidates.other_translations: None found.
candidates.value: An inside view of 'Chaldaean' scholarship, eclipse anxiety and the substitute-king ritual. Illuminates Arrian 7.24 (a pseudo-king on Alexander's throne) and Greek images of the Chaldaeans.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: open transliterations and epistolary formulae. The English edition is used only for cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Substitute-king (šar pūḫi) letters, c. 30 letters

candidates.title: Myth of the Sun's Eye (P. Leiden I 384) with Greek version (P. Lond. Lit. 192) / «Миф о Солнечном Оке»
candidates.author: Anonymous
candidates.date: Demotic manuscript 2nd c. CE; Greek version 3rd c. CE
candidates.size: c. 22 Demotic columns (estimate) + Greek fragments
candidates.edition: Spiegelberg, Der ägyptische Mythus vom Sonnenauge (1917; public domain, archive.org); de Cenival 1988 (French).
candidates.ru_evidence: Only three inserted fables, in a popular version: И.С. Кацнельсон, «Фараон Хуфу и чародеи» (1958), contents checked on archive.org.
candidates.en_evidence: de.wikipedia lists only German and French editions; no complete English translation found.
candidates.other_translations: German (Spiegelberg 1917); French (de Cenival 1988).
candidates.value: A rare Egyptian–Greek bilingual literary work containing Aesopic fables (Lion and Mouse). Central to Greco-Egyptian literary exchange and fable studies.
candidates.ai_feasibility: low-medium: the Demotic is hard, helped by Spiegelberg's public-domain transcription and German. The Greek version is easy.
candidates.pilot_unit: Greek version + corresponding Demotic columns (est. 3–5 columns)

candidates.title: Sakikkû (SA.GIG), Babylonian Diagnostic Handbook of Esagil-kīn-apli / Вавилонский диагностический справочник «Сакикку»
candidates.author: Esagil-kīn-apli (redactor)
candidates.date: Redacted 11th c. BCE; manuscripts 7th–3rd c. BCE
candidates.size: 40 tablets, 3,000+ entries
candidates.edition: Labat, Traité akkadien de diagnostics et pronostics médicaux (1951); later Heeßel (2000) and Scurlock (2014), not re-verified.
candidates.ru_evidence: CyberLeninka 'Сакикку': 0 results; no ru.wikipedia article or translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: Scurlock 2014 (not re-verified online); en.wikipedia confirms the structure but gives no bibliography.
candidates.other_translations: French full (Labat 1951); German partial (Heeßel 2000).
candidates.value: The first systematic diagnostic manual. Comparanda for the Hippocratic Prognostic and Epidemics; central to history of medicine and Greco-Babylonian contacts.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high-medium: formulaic entries, but disease identifications are contested, which suits structured debate between models.
candidates.pilot_unit: Tablets 1–2 (signs met on the way to the patient)

candidates.title: Persepolis Fortification Tablets (Elamite), Hallock PF 1–2087 / Персепольские таблички крепостной стены
candidates.author: Achaemenid administrators under Darius I
candidates.size: Over 15,000 records, c. 5% published; Hallock: 2,087 texts
candidates.edition: Hallock, OIP 92 (1969; free PDF, archive.org/details/oip92); OCHRE database.
candidates.ru_evidence: CyberLeninka 'Персеполь таблички эламские' gives only studies; no Russian translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: Hallock translated the 2,087 published texts; about 95% of the archive is unpublished (en.wikipedia).
candidates.other_translations: Selections in French/German studies (not verified).
candidates.value: Primary evidence for the Persian court, roads, rations and Greeks (Yaunā) in Persian service. Indispensable control for Herodotus, Xenophon and Ctesias.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: highly formulaic with a small vocabulary, but LLMs know little Elamite, so rely on Hallock's glossary. Unpublished tablets are not accessible.
candidates.pilot_unit: One Hallock category, e.g. Q texts (travel rations), a few hundred short texts

candidates.title: Murašû archive, Nippur / Архив дома Мурашу
candidates.author: Scribes of the Murašû firm
candidates.size: 650–879 tablets
candidates.edition: Hilprecht & Clay BE 9 (1898), Clay BE 10 (1904), PBS 2/1 (1912), all public domain on archive.org; Cardascia 1951; Stolper 1985.
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia has no article (red link 'Мурашу[англ.]' in several articles); no Russian translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: Clay's volumes translate selected texts; Stolper 1985 edits a subset (en.wikipedia 'Murashu family').
candidates.other_translations: French selection (Cardascia 1951).
candidates.value: Achaemenid land-for-service system and Persian nobles known from Ctesias (Menostanes, Artoxares, Arbarius). Economic history of Persia during the Peloponnesian War.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: formulaic contracts with public-domain copies and transliterations; prosopography needs checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Texts naming Ctesian nobles, or BE 10 (Darius II); c. 100 texts

candidates.title: Aramaic Documents from Ancient Bactria (Khalili Collection) / Арамейские документы из Бактрии
candidates.author: Achaemenid satrapal chancery of Bactria
candidates.size: 48 documents: 30 leather, 18 wooden tallies
candidates.edition: Naveh & Shaked, Aramaic Documents from Ancient Bactria (2012); copyrighted.
candidates.ru_evidence: CyberLeninka 'Бактрия арамейские документы Халили': 0 hits; no Russian translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: Naveh & Shaked 2012 edition with English translation (en.wikipedia 'Khalili Collection of Aramaic Documents').
candidates.other_translations: None found.
candidates.value: Bactrian administration on the eve of and under Alexander: Bessus as king, and a text dated 'year 7 of Alexander'. A unique documentary counterpart to Arrian and Curtius.
