candidates.ai_feasibility: high: Imperial Aramaic is well within LLM competence and the corpus is small. Copyright of the edition means permission is needed to republish the source.
candidates.pilot_unit: The 18 leather letters + the Alexander-dated document

candidates.title: Demotic Magical Papyrus of London and Leiden (PDM xiv) / Лондонско-Лейденский демотический магический папирус
candidates.author: Anonymous (Theban magical library)
candidates.language: Demotic, with Old Coptic glosses and Greek
candidates.size: c. 30 columns (estimate)
candidates.edition: Griffith & Thompson (1904–09; public domain, archive.org: facsimile, transliteration, English); Betz, Greek Magical Papyri in Translation (1986).
candidates.ru_evidence: CyberLeninka ('Лейденский магический папирус демотический') finds no translation; none found.
candidates.en_evidence: Griffith & Thompson 1904 (archive.org); Betz 1986.
candidates.other_translations: None found.
candidates.value: A bridge between Egyptian ritual and the Greek Magical Papyri (same Theban library). Vital for religion in Roman Egypt, Old Coptic and Greek–Egyptian bilingualism.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: a public-domain transliteration exists, so the source can be published freely; voces magicae and Old Coptic glosses are tricky.
candidates.pilot_unit: Lamp and vessel divination spells (first c. 5 columns)

candidates.title: Ptolemaic temple inscriptions of Edfu, Chassinat Edfou I–V / Надписи храма Гора в Эдфу
candidates.author: Priests of the Edfu temple
candidates.genre: Ritual, theological and geographical temple texts
candidates.size: Chassinat, 14 volumes in all; Edfou I–V several thousand text columns (estimate)
candidates.edition: Chassinat, Le temple d'Edfou (IFAO, 1892–1934; likely public domain); German translations by Kurth (Edfou VIII 1998, VII 2004, VI 2014).
candidates.ru_evidence: CyberLeninka 'Эдфу надпись перевод' finds no translations; none found.
candidates.en_evidence: Only selected texts in English; Kurth's 2004 English guide (de.wikipedia 'Edfu-Projekt').
candidates.other_translations: German: Edfou VI–VIII complete (Edfu-Projekt); Edfou I–V largely untranslated in any language.
candidates.value: The largest coherent body of Ptolemaic theology, ritual and sacred geography, and the self-image of priests under Greek kings. Core volumes have no translation in any language.
candidates.ai_feasibility: low: Ptolemaic sign values and no open transliteration; the source is image-based. Needs an Egyptologist in the loop; a long-term project.
candidates.pilot_unit: Ritual scenes of one chapel in Edfou I (est. 30–50 pp.)

sweep:ane-egypt.ru_gap_notes:
Texts available in English but not in Russian:
- Astronomical Diaries and BCHP (Sachs–Hunger; Finkel–van der Spek–Pirngruber).
- SAA scholarly letters and reports (Parpola, Hunger; SAAo).
- Akkadian prophecies (Grayson, Neujahr).
- Sakikkû (Scurlock; French: Labat).
- Persepolis Fortification texts (Hallock, 2,087 texts).
- Murašû archive (Clay, Stolper).
- Bactrian Aramaic documents (Naveh–Shaked).
- Coffin Texts (Faulkner). Russian Wikipedia says no Russian translation exists; only single spells appear in studies (e.g. Богданов 2022, CT 1027).
- Demotic Magical Papyrus (Griffith–Thompson; Betz).
- Demotic Book of Thoth (Jasnow–Zauzich 2005).
- Most of ETCSL's roughly 400 Sumerian compositions.
- Hittite Ahhiyawa texts (Beckman–Bryce–Cline). Russian has only fragments in studies (unverified).

Russian coverage is already good for epic, myth, wisdom and laws. Elephantine is partly translated (Волков 1915), and so are some Demotic tales (Кацнельсон 1958).

sweep:greek-poetry.corpus_overview: Russian coverage of this corpus is wider than usually assumed, so many items on the starting list drop out. T. L. Aleksandrova has translated six late-antique poems into Russian: Eudocia's Homeric cento (Vestnik PSTGU 2018), Paul the Silentiary (VDI 2019), John of Gaza (2020), Triphiodorus (2021), the Orphic Argonautica (2023) and the Orphic Lithica (2024). Other Russian translations: Lycophron (Surikov), Dionysius Periegetes (Ilyushechkina, VDI 2005-06), Nonnus' Paraphrase (2002), the Sibylline Oracles (Vitkovskie 1996), Colluthus (Miller 1849), and AP Books I-III and VIII (Sinitsa & Bolgov 2014). Greek Anthology: about 3,700 epigrams in AP plus about 390 in the Planudean appendix. English has a complete version (Paton's Loeb). Russian has only selections, the largest being Gasparov & Shul'ts 1999 (728 pp.). Its share of the whole could not be quantified; by estimate, Books IX, XI, XIV and XVI are the least covered. The real Russian gaps fall into three groups. (1) Hellenistic and imperial didactic and technical poetry: Nicander 1,588 lines, Oppian about 3,500, Ps.-Oppian about 2,150, Ps.-Manetho about 3,300, Maximus about 600, Ps.-Scymnus about 1,000. (2) Fragmentary Hellenistic poetry: Callimachus' Iambi and Hecale, the Milan Posidippus. (3) Learned verse of the 7th-14th centuries that carries ancient material: George of Pisidia about 5,000 lines, Tzetzes about 14,350, Manasses 6,733, Philes, and the Byzantine Alexander Poem about 6,100. In group 3, English is also missing or exists only as volunteer work. Method caveat: the session's web-search budget was used up. Statuses were checked through ru.wikipedia, ancientrome.ru, Crossref and archive.org, and claims marked 'unverified' still need checking.

candidates.title: Ἱστορίαι / Chiliades (Book of Histories); «Хилиады» («Книга историй»)
candidates.author: John Tzetzes
candidates.genre: Antiquarian-didactic poem in political verse; self-commentary on his letters
candidates.size: 12,674 political verses, about 660 'histories', 13 chiliads
candidates.edition: Kiessling 1826, public domain (https://books.google.com/books?id=dG0GAAAAQAAJ); Leone 1968, 2nd ed. 2007. The volunteer English translation is based on Kiessling.
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Иоанн Цец': only excerpts, in Памятники византийской литературы IX–XIV вв. (1969), pp. 252–259. No fuller Russian translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: Volunteer translation (Untila, Berkowitz, Ramiotis, Dogani et al.; mitologia.pt), made from Kiessling 1826. It calls itself a 'tentative first edition' with minimal notes; last edit 2024. https://archive.org/details/TzetzesCHILIADES; also on theoi.com.
candidates.other_translations: No complete French, German, Italian or Spanish translation found (search not exhaustive).
candidates.value: Preserves fragments and testimonia of over 200 ancient authors. A key text for source criticism and for Byzantine teaching of the classics, and it contains Alexander anecdotes. No annotated scholarly translation exists in any language. A source-tracing commentary is exactly the apparatus Neoscholia offers.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Political verse reads almost like prose. The main work is identifying sources, which AI does well but every case needs checking against TLG and the fragment editions.
candidates.pilot_unit: Chiliad I (about 1,000 verses, opening with Croesus), or a thematic dossier of the Alexander histories

candidates.title: Expeditio Persica, Bellum Avaricum, Heraclias (+ Hexaemeron); «Ираклиада», «На нашествие варваров» и др.
candidates.author: George of Pisidia
candidates.genre: Panegyrical epic in iambic trimeter; didactic-theological poem (Hexaemeron)
candidates.size: About 5,000 verses in total. Expeditio Persica 1,088; Bellum Avaricum about 540; Heraclias about 470; Hexaemeron about 1,900 (approximate).
candidates.edition: Pertusi 1959; Tartaglia 1998 (UTET, complete); Gonnelli 1998 (Hexaemeron). Public-domain texts: Bekker, CSHB 1836; Querci 1777 = PG 92 (scans; URLs not checked).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Георгий Писида' lists only Russian 'отрывки' (excerpts) of Expeditio Persica, Bellum Avaricum, Heraclias and others. Hexaemeron is not listed.
candidates.en_evidence: No complete English translation found on English Wikipedia or Crossref; only studies (Whitby, Howard-Johnston, Leppin).
candidates.other_translations: Italian, complete: Pertusi 1959; Tartaglia 1998; Gonnelli 1998 (Hexaemeron).
candidates.value: Eyewitness court poetry on Heraclius' Persian war, the Avar-Persian siege of Constantinople (626) and the True Cross. Used as a source by Theophanes. The last classicizing panegyric of Late Antiquity, at the 7th-century cutoff. Hexaemeron is a key text on late-antique science and Platonism.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium-high. The trimeters are dense and allusive, with rare vocabulary. Italian translations allow cross-checking, and historical commentary can draw on Howard-Johnston.
candidates.pilot_unit: Bellum Avaricum (about 540 lines, the 626 siege), then Expeditio Persica

candidates.title: Byzantine Alexander Poem (Διήγησις Ἀλεξάνδρου, cod. Marc. gr. 408); «Византийская поэма об Александре»
candidates.author: Anonymous
candidates.language: Late Byzantine Greek, learned and vernacular mixed
candidates.genre: Verse romance in political verse, retelling the Pseudo-Callisthenes Alexander tradition
candidates.size: About 6,120 political verses in 3 books
candidates.edition: Reichmann 1963; Aerts 2014 (De Gruyter, Byzantinisches Archiv): text, synopsis and commentary. No open digital text found.
candidates.ru_evidence: No Russian translation found (ru.wikipedia, Crossref).
candidates.en_evidence: Contents of Aerts 2014 (doi 10.1515/9781614513070): Books I–III text, synopsis, commentary, indices. No translation.
candidates.other_translations: None found (Modern Greek: unknown)
candidates.value: A key link between the Pseudo-Callisthenes recensions and the later Phyllada and Rimada. This is directly the editor's specialism, so commentary can tie each episode to the recensions and give a flagship showcase of human-AI expertise.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. Late vernacular morphology and Aerts' commentary are aids; the narrative is predictable. Expert oversight is essential.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book I opening (Nectanebo and Alexander's birth), about 600–800 verses

candidates.title: Περίοδος πρὸς Νικομήδην βασιλέα, Periodos to Nicomedes ('Pseudo-Scymnus'); «Землеописание» Псевдо-Скимна
candidates.author: Anonymous ('Pseudo-Scymnus')
candidates.genre: Didactic geographical poem in iambic trimeter
candidates.size: About 1,000 trimeters preserved, plus prose-paraphrase fragments of the lost end
candidates.edition: Müller, GGM I (1855), public domain (archive.org scans); Marcotte 2000 (CUF).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Псевдо-Скимн' lists no Russian translation. Black Sea excerpts are probably in Latyshev's Scythica et Caucasica (1893; VDI 1947 reprint): unverified.
candidates.en_evidence: Roller 2021, Three Ancient Geographical Treatises in Translation (doi 10.4324/9781003030379-3); Shipley et al. 2024, Geographers of the Ancient Greek World (doi 10.1017/9781009194211.022).
candidates.other_translations: French: Marcotte 2000 (CUF). German: Korenjak 2003 (unverified).
candidates.value: Gives foundation dates for Greek colonies, especially on the Black Sea, drawing on Ephorus, Eratosthenes and Demetrius of Callatis. Essential for Black Sea and Bosporan archaeology, which has a large Russian-language readership. Also an important Hellenistic statement on didactic poetry and patronage.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Plain, catalogue-like trimeters. The commentary on toponyms and archaeology is demanding but well documented.
candidates.pilot_unit: Prologue (about 140 lines) plus the Pontic section; the whole poem (about 1,000 lines) is pilot-sized

candidates.title: Θηριακά, Ἀλεξιφάρμακα, Theriaca and Alexipharmaca; «Териака», «Противоядия»
candidates.author: Nicander of Colophon
candidates.genre: Didactic hexameter poems on venomous animals and poisons
candidates.size: 958 + 630 = 1,588 hexameters, plus extensive scholia
candidates.edition: O. Schneider 1856, with scholia, public domain (https://archive.org/details/theriacaetalexi00schngoog); Gow–Scholfield 1953; Jacques, CUF 2002/2007.
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Никандр Колофонский': only Scythia/Caucasus excerpts, VDI 1947 no. 3, pp. 302–303. No full Russian translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: Gow & Scholfield 1953, CUP (review doi 10.1017/s0009840x00180710); Overduin 2015, Brill (Theriaca, doi 10.1163/9789004283602).
candidates.other_translations: French: Jacques, CUF (2002 Theriaca; Alexipharmaca vol. III).
candidates.value: The earliest surviving Greek works on venomous animals and poisons. A core source for ancient pharmacology, zoology and Hellenistic glossographic poetics, with rich scholia. Used by historians of medicine and Hellenistic poetry.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. The vocabulary is notoriously obscure and full of glosses, and identifying plants and animals needs specialist checks. A good showcase for visible model disagreement.
candidates.pilot_unit: Alexipharmaca (630 hexameters) with selected scholia

candidates.title: Ἴαμβοι and Ἑκάλη, Iambi and Hecale (fragments, with the Diegeseis); «Ямбы», «Гекала»
candidates.author: Callimachus of Cyrene
candidates.size: Iambi: 13 poems, originally about 1,000 lines, now fragmentary. Hecale: about 180 fragments. Roughly 600–800 legible lines in all (estimate).
candidates.edition: Pfeiffer 1949–53; Hollis 2009 (Hecale); Kerkhecker 1999. No open digital text of the fragments verified.
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Каллимах из Кирены': Hecale only in Эллинские поэты (1999), pp. 210–211; Iambi pp. 300–303 (Smyka, Yarkho). Tiny selections.
candidates.en_evidence: Trypanis, Loeb 1958; Hollis 2009 (Hecale with translation); Acosta-Hughes 2002; Kerkhecker 1999 (listed on ru.wikipedia).
candidates.other_translations: Italian: Lelli 2005 (Iambi 14–17); D'Alessio 1996 (BUR, unverified). German: Asper 2004 (unverified).
candidates.value: Programmatic core of Hellenistic poetics and the model for Catullus, Horace's Epodes and Ovid. Russian readers have the Hymns and Aetia selections but practically none of the Iambi or Hecale. High value for teaching.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium-low. Papyrus lacunae make hallucinated restorations a real risk. Review agents must check brackets and supplements against the editions.
candidates.pilot_unit: Iambi 1–13 with the Diegeseis (about 400–500 legible lines; estimate)

candidates.title: Ἁλιευτικά, Halieutica (On Fishing); «Галиевтика» («О рыбной ловле»)
candidates.author: Oppian of Anazarbus
candidates.genre: Didactic hexameter poem on marine life and fishing
candidates.size: 5 books, about 3,500 hexameters
candidates.edition: Mair, Loeb 1928 (US public domain; https://archive.org/details/oppiancolluthust00oppiuoft); Fajen 1999 (Teubner).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Оппиан': only excerpts by Grabar'-Passek in Памятники поздней античной поэзии и прозы (1964), pp. 34–39.
candidates.en_evidence: Mair, Loeb 1928 (doi 10.5962/bhl.title.30404); archive.org scan.
candidates.other_translations: Spanish: Calvo Delcán, Gredos 134 (1990).
candidates.value: The largest ancient poem on marine life. A source for ancient ichthyology, fishing technology and imperial court didactic poetry (dedicated to Marcus Aurelius and Commodus). Heavily read and annotated in Byzantium. Appeals to both specialists and general readers.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Clear epic diction. Fish-name identifications (Thompson's glossary) need checking. Mair's English allows cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book 1 (about 800 hexameters)

candidates.title: Περὶ καταρχῶν, On Initiatives (Katarchai); «О начинаниях»
candidates.author: 'Maximus' (astrological poet; identity disputed)
candidates.size: About 600 hexameters (approx.), plus a Byzantine prose paraphrase
candidates.edition: Ludwich 1877 (Teubner, public domain; archive.org scans); Zito 2016 (CUF 521).
candidates.ru_evidence: No Russian translation found (no ru.wikipedia article; nothing on Crossref).
candidates.en_evidence: No English translation found (Crossref); the only modern translation is French.
candidates.other_translations: French: Zito, CUF 2016 (review doi 10.3917/phil.901.0225c).
candidates.value: The only substantial Greek verse manual of catarchic astrology: choosing moments for travel, marriage, farming and so on. Valuable for the history of science and religion and for daily-life mentalities. It meets the 'no English translation' ideal.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium-high. Formulaic technical content. Needs a controlled astrological glossary (a dedicated glossary agent) and cross-checking with Zito's French.
candidates.pilot_unit: The entire poem (about 600 lines), a complete small pilot

candidates.title: Ἰλιακά: Antehomerica, Homerica, Posthomerica (Carmina Iliaca)
candidates.author: John Tzetzes
candidates.genre: Hexameter epitome of the Trojan War, with the author's scholia
candidates.size: 1,676 hexameters (407 + 489 + 780), plus Tzetzes' scholia
candidates.edition: Leone 1995 (Catania); Jacobs 1793 and Bekker 1816 (public domain; URLs not checked).
candidates.ru_evidence: No Russian translation found. ru.wikipedia lists only 1969 excerpts of Tzetzes' works in general.
candidates.en_evidence: Volunteer 'first English translation' (mitologia.pt, 2014), not peer-reviewed: https://archive.org/details/TzetzesANTEHOMERICA, .../TzetzesHOMERICA, .../TzetzesPOSTHOMERICA
candidates.other_translations: Italian: unverified (Leone's 1995 edition)
candidates.value: A Byzantine school epic and reception of the epic cycle. Preserves otherwise lost material, e.g. a Cassius Dio passage on Archimedes (Rance, CQ 2023). The scholia show classroom method. Pairs naturally with the Chiliades.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Straightforward hexameters; Tzetzes' own scholia guide the commentary.
candidates.pilot_unit: Antehomerica (407 hexameters)

candidates.title: Ἀποτελεσματικά, Apotelesmatica (Pseudo-Manetho); «Апотелесматика»
candidates.author: Pseudo-Manetho (composite)
candidates.date: c. 1st/2nd–4th c. CE (books of different dates)
candidates.size: 6 books, about 3,300 lines (approx.)
candidates.edition: Koechly 1858 (public domain); Lightfoot, OUP 2020/2023.
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Манефон' names the 6-book work but lists no translation; none found.
candidates.en_evidence: Lightfoot, OUP 2020 (Books 2, 3, 6; doi 10.1093/actrade/9780198858782.book.1) and 2023 (Books 4, 1, 5; doi 10.1093/actrade/9780192868473.book.1).
candidates.other_translations: None verified
candidates.value: The largest surviving Greek astrological poem. A source for the social history of Roman Egypt (professions, slaves, marriage, deviance) and for imperial verse technique. Used by historians of science and of Roman society.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. Technical but repetitive. Lightfoot's English gives cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book 4 (about 600 lines; approx.)

candidates.title: Κυνηγετικά, Cynegetica (On Hunting); «Охота» («Кинегетика»)
candidates.author: Pseudo-Oppian (of Apamea)
candidates.genre: Didactic hexameter poem on hunting and land animals
candidates.size: 4 books, about 2,150 hexameters
candidates.edition: Boudreaux 1908; Mair 1928 (US public domain, archive.org); Papathomopoulos 2003 (Teubner).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Оппиан': only excerpts in Памятники поздней античной поэзии и прозы (1964), pp. 34–39. It does not say which poem.
candidates.en_evidence: Mair, Loeb 1928: https://archive.org/details/oppiancolluthust00oppiuoft
candidates.other_translations: Spanish: Calvo Delcán, Gredos 134 (1990).
candidates.value: Ancient zoology of land animals, Syrian local lore and Severan court culture. Linked to the famous illustrated manuscript Venice Marc. gr. 479. Pairs with the Halieutica for a didactic 'animal poetry' strand.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Clear diction. Animal identifications need checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: One book (about 500–600 hexameters), e.g. Book 2

candidates.title: Epigrams of the Milan papyrus (P.Mil.Vogl. VIII 309, 'New Posidippus'); «Миланский папирус» Посидиппа
candidates.author: Posidippus of Pella (attribution of all poems debated)
candidates.genre: Epigram book in sections (Lithika, Oionoskopika, Hippika, etc.)
candidates.size: 112 epigrams, about 600 lines, many damaged
candidates.edition: Bastianini–Gallazzi 2001; Austin–Bastianini 2002. Modern texts under rights; reuse needs checking.
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Посидипп' lists no Russian translation of the papyrus, only a 2019 study. Russian work so far is analytical (Kazanskaya, Philologia Classica 2016; Hyperboreus 2019).
candidates.en_evidence: Austin–Bastianini 2002; Nisetich in Gutzwiller (ed.), The New Posidippus 2005; Fain 2019 chapter (doi 10.1525/9780520947764-006).
candidates.other_translations: Italian: Bastianini–Gallazzi 2001
candidates.value: The only surviving Hellenistic poetry book transmitted on papyrus. It reshaped our picture of Hellenistic epigram and Ptolemaic court ideology (gems, omens, chariot victories). Essential for Hellenistic studies.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. Damaged papyrus and supplements need careful marking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Lithika (AB 1–20, about 120 lines)

candidates.title: Στίχοι περὶ ζῴων ἰδιότητος, De animalium proprietate (On the Properties of Animals)
candidates.author: Manuel Philes
candidates.date: early 14th c. CE (dedicated to Michael IX Palaiologos)
candidates.size: About 2,000 verses
candidates.edition: Lehrs & Dübner, Poetae bucolici et didactici (Didot 1851/1862; Greek with Latin), public domain.
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Мануил Фил' lists no translations; none found.
candidates.en_evidence: No English translation found (English Wikipedia, Crossref).
candidates.other_translations: None modern found (only the 19th-c. Latin version)
candidates.value: A Byzantine verse reworking of Aelian and Oppian: a case study in how ancient natural history was passed on. Completes a 'zoological poetry' series with Oppian and Nicander. Truly untranslated.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Simple dodecasyllables, and aligning with the Aelian sources can be automated.
candidates.pilot_unit: Opening about 500 verses, aligned with Aelian

candidates.title: Σύνοψις χρονική, Synopsis Chronike; «Хроника» Константина Манассии
candidates.author: Constantine Manasses
candidates.genre: Verse world chronicle in political verse
candidates.size: 6,733 verses
candidates.edition: Lampsidis 1996 (CFHB 36); Bekker 1837 (CSHB, public domain; URL not checked).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Константин Манассия': Russian only of excerpts from the Middle Bulgarian Slavonic version (Polyvyannyi 1990, vostlit.info). Kantemir's 18th-c. translation survives in manuscript (doi 10.31860/2712-7591-2020-1-176-180). No modern Russian from the Greek.
candidates.en_evidence: Yuretich 2018, The Chronicle of Constantine Manasses (Liverpool UP; doi 10.2307/jj.38238666).
candidates.other_translations: Modern Bulgarian: Buyukliev 1992
candidates.value: A formative text for Slavic and Russian chronography, yet Russian readers know it only through Slavonic. Its sections on antiquity (Troy, Persia, Alexander, Rome) show Byzantine retelling of ancient history.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Ornate but regular verse; the English translation is available for cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Sections on antiquity (Troy, Alexander), about 700 verses (to be delimited)

sweep:greek-poetry.ru_gap_notes: These texts have English translations but no Russian ones. Hellenistic and imperial: Nicander (Gow–Scholfield 1953; Overduin 2015), Oppian's Halieutica and Ps.-Oppian's Cynegetica (Mair 1928, now US public domain), Ps.-Manetho (Lightfoot 2020–23), Ps.-Scymnus (Roller 2021; Shipley 2024), Callimachus' Iambi and Hecale (Trypanis 1958; Hollis 2009), the Milan Posidippus (Austin–Bastianini 2002), and Euphorion (Lightfoot Loeb 2009; Russian has only Tsybenko's selected fragments). Byzantine: Manasses (Yuretich 2018), Tzetzes' Allegories of the Iliad and Odyssey (DOML 2015, 2019), and Tzetzes' Chiliades and Carmina Iliaca (volunteer English online only). The Greek Anthology also falls here: Paton's complete English against Russian selections only.

sweep:greek-technical.corpus_overview: Greek technical literature is the largest under-translated block of Greek prose. Galen alone runs to c. 2.6 million words (122 works in Kühn). A heuristic count of Fichtner's Galen bibliography (BBAW, 2023/12) finds an English version for at least 54 of 108 TLG-numbered genuine works (c. 50–60%), yet the largest pharmacological works (Simple Drugs, 11 books; Compound Drugs by Places, 10; by Kinds, 7 books, c. 102k words; Antidotes) have no English and mostly no translation at all. Russian Galen: De usu partium (1971), Balalykin et al., Сочинения I–V (2014–18, c. 3,200 pp.) and c. 8 journal pieces, est. 10–20% of works. Hippocratic corpus: Rudnev/Karpov, 3 vols (1936–44); treatise-level gaps unverified. The late-antique encyclopedists (Oribasius, Aetius, Alexander of Tralles, Paul) have no Russian at all; English is complete only for Paul. Elementary mathematics/astronomy is well covered in Russian by Shchetnikov and ΣΧΟΛΗ (Nicomachus 2008, Theon of Smyrna 2009, Cleomedes 2010, Geminus 2011, Ptolemy's Harmonics 2012, Euclid's Optics 2019, Autolycus), but advanced works (Hipparchus, Proclus' Hypotyposis, Theon's and Pappus' Almagest commentaries, Eutocius) lack Russian and mostly English. Military texts are fairly covered (Aelian RU 2022; poliorcetics RU 1996; Loeb/Whitehead EN). Minor geographers have rough English on ToposText, Russian mostly Latyshev excerpts; Stephanus' 3,655 entries exist complete only in German. Alchemy is complete only in French (1888); Hippiatrica and CCAG (12 vols) remain essentially untranslated. Литературные памятники contains no Greek technical author. Benchmark: Zainaldin et al. 2026 scored LLMs 95/100 on translated Galen vs 80/100 on untranslated pharmacology.
sweep:greek-technical.ru_gap_notes: English but no Russian found: Aretaeus (Adams 1856), Dioscorides (Beck 2005/2017), Paul of Aegina (Adams 1844–47; surgical Book VI especially valuable), Theophrastus' De causis plantarum (Loeb 1976–90; Russian has only Historia plantarum), Geoponika (Dalby 2011), Oribasius Books 1 and 4 (Grant 1997), Porphyry's Commentary on Ptolemy's Harmonics (Barker 2015; not in ΣΧΟΛΗ), Manetho's Apotelesmatica (Lightfoot 2020), Rhetorius (Holden 2009), Onasander (Loeb 1923; ru.wikipedia lists no RU), Ps.-Aristotle Problemata (Loeb; RU only Books 15, 19 and Mechanics), and the minor geographers (ToposText EN; RU Latyshev excerpts). Vettius Valens (EN Riley) has unknown Russian status. Best RU-gap targets: Aretaeus, Dioscorides, Paul VI, Theophrastus CP.

candidates.title: Τῶν Ἀράτου καὶ Εὐδόξου φαινομένων ἐξήγησις — Commentary on the Phaenomena of Aratus and Eudoxus; RU: «Комментарий к „Явлениям“ Арата и Евдокса»
candidates.author: Hipparchus of Nicaea
candidates.genre: Astronomy; critical commentary on didactic poetry
candidates.size: 3 books; est. c. 30,000 words (Manitius 1894: 376 pp. including facing German and notes)
candidates.edition: Manitius, Teubner 1894, Greek with German, public domain: https://archive.org/details/McGillLibrary-hssl_hipparchou-ton-aratou_QB41H561894-18575
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia «Гиппарх» (Издания и переводы) lists only Manitius 1894 and Almagest RU; ΣΧΟΛΗ translation index (Shchetnikov's astronomy series: Geminus, Cleomedes, Autolycus) has no Hipparchus.
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia «Hipparchus», Translations: only German (1894) and Italian (2013/2022). Vanin–Cusinato, arXiv 2206.08243: first modern-language translation since Manitius 1894.
candidates.other_translations: German: Manitius 1894. Italian: Cusinato & Vanin 2013, 3rd ed. 2022 (open, arXiv 2206.08243).
candidates.value: Only surviving work of antiquity's greatest observational astronomer; chief evidence for Eudoxus' lost Phaenomena, the scholarly reception of Aratus and pre-Ptolemaic star positions (renewed by the 2022 Sinai palimpsest find of his catalogue). Used by historians of astronomy, Hellenistic poetry and science.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium-high: plain technical Koine; risk lies in numbers (degrees, risings and settings). Agents must check figures against planetarium computation and against Manitius and Vanin.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book 1 (critique of Aratus and Eudoxus, reply to Attalus), est. 10–12k words

candidates.title: Θεραπευτικά (12 books), Περὶ πυρετῶν, Περὶ ἑλμίνθων — Therapeutics, On Fevers, Letter on Intestinal Worms; RU: Александр Траллийский, «Терапевтика»
candidates.author: Alexander of Tralles
candidates.size: 12 books plus two short works; est. 120–150k words (Puschmann, 2 vols, c. 1,200 pp. with facing German)
candidates.edition: Puschmann, Alexander von Tralles, 2 vols, Wien 1878–79 (Greek and German; repr. 1963), public domain; Nachträge 1886. Scans via BSB digital collections.
candidates.ru_evidence: No ru.wikipedia article; absent from ΣΧΟΛΗ index and from Balalykin's Galen series; no Russian version found anywhere.
candidates.en_evidence: en, de and fr Wikipedia list only Puschmann (German) and Brunet (French); Langslow 2006 studies the Latin version. No English translation found.
candidates.other_translations: German: Puschmann 1878–79. French: Brunet, 4 vols, 1933–37. German excerpts of iatromagic: Grimm-Stadelmann 2020.
candidates.value: Last great original clinician of Late Antiquity (brother of Anthemius, architect of Hagia Sophia): case observations, open critique of Galen, amulets and iatromagical remedies. Heavily used in Latin, Arabic and Hebrew medicine. For historians of medicine, magic, Byzantium.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high for prose (clear didactic Koine); medium for drug names; Puschmann and Brunet allow cross-checking. Amulet formulas need specialist review.
candidates.pilot_unit: Letter on Intestinal Worms (est. c. 4k words) plus Therapeutics I chapters on melancholy and epilepsy (est. c. 8k)

candidates.title: Ἐθνικά (epitome) — Ethnica; RU: Стефан Византийский, «Этника». Proposed unit: entries on Alexander's and the Diadochi's foundations
candidates.author: Stephanus of Byzantium
candidates.size: 3,655 entries in the epitome (Billerbeck count); est. 120–150k words (Meineke 1849, c. 700 pp.)
candidates.edition: Billerbeck et al., CFHB 43, 5 vols, 2006–17 (critical, with German; copyright). Meineke 1849 is public domain (Google Books; Greek on ToposText).
candidates.ru_evidence: Only excerpts: part of letter Ε translated by M. M. Kholod, Клио 2(21), 2003 (vostlit.info); Pontic and Caucasian entries in Latyshev's excerpts. No complete Russian.
candidates.en_evidence: ToposText work 241: 'a few entries … translated by Brady Kiesling'. en.wikipedia lists only Latin versions; no published English translation found.
candidates.other_translations: German: Billerbeck et al. 2006–17 (complete, with commentary). Latin: Pinedo 1678, Berkel 1688.
candidates.value: Standard reference for Greek toponyms and ethnics; nearly every entry cites an ancient authority, many of them lost (Hecataeus, Theopompus, Artemidorus, Alexander Polyhistor). Indispensable to historians, epigraphists, archaeologists. The Alexandreia entry lists 18 cities, a natural bridge to Alexander studies.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: formulaic Greek is easy; the risks are the grammar of ethnic forms, corrupt fragments and place identifications. Check against Billerbeck and Pleiades IDs.
candidates.pilot_unit: c. 60–80 entries on cities named after Alexander and the Diadochi (Alexandreia, Antiocheia, Seleukeia, Apameia, Laodikeia etc.), est. 8–10k words

candidates.title: Περὶ κράσεως καὶ δυνάμεως τῶν ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων — De simplicium medicamentorum temperamentis ac facultatibus (Simple Drugs); RU: Гален, «О смешении и силе простых лекарств»
candidates.author: Galen of Pergamon
candidates.size: 11 books, Kühn XI 379–892 and XII 1–377 (c. 890 pp. with Latin); est. 130–150k Greek words
candidates.edition: Only Kühn 1826 (Greek and Latin, public domain). Fichtner: CMG edition of Book IX in preparation (Martelli). Petit 2010: editio princeps of I.1–3.
candidates.ru_evidence: Not in the ru.wikipedia Galen translation list (1971; Balalykin I–V, 2014–18; journal pieces). The contents of vols II–V were not checked in detail.
candidates.en_evidence: Fichtner Galen bibliography (BBAW 2023/12, no. 78) lists only Garofalo's 1985 sample and Petit's annotated French of I.1–3. No English.
candidates.other_translations: French: Petit 2010 (I.1–3 only). German: Haars 2018 translates Oribasius' Collections XV, an excerpt of this work's drug catalogue.
candidates.value: Galen's foundational theory of drug action (qualities and degrees) and antiquity's fullest critical pharmacopoeia. Book X (animal substances) includes his polemic against using human body parts as drugs. Core source for history of pharmacy, Arabic and Latin reception, material culture.
candidates.ai_feasibility: theory books high; catalogue books medium-low. Zainaldin et al. 2026: LLM failures track rare pharmacological terms (r = −.97). Requires term-frequency flagging and multi-model review.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book X (animal substances, incl. the polemic on human parts), est. 12–15k words. Avoids Book IX, now under CMG edition.

candidates.title: Ἱππιατρικά — Hippiatrica (Corpus Hippiatricorum Graecorum); RU: «Гиппиатрика». Proposed unit: Apsyrtus' excerpts
candidates.author: Compilation: Apsyrtus, Hierocles, Theomnestus, Eumelus, Pelagonius (in Greek), Anatolius and others
candidates.date: Sources 3rd–5th c. CE; late-antique compilation, recensions down to 10th c.
candidates.size: Oder–Hoppe CHG I–II, c. 800 Teubner pp.; est. 200k+ words across recensions
candidates.edition: Oder & Hoppe, Corpus Hippiatricorum Graecorum I–II, Leipzig 1924–27 (public domain in the US by date; EU status depends on the editors' death dates).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia «Гиппиатрика» (derived from the English article) cites no translation; none found in the checked Russian catalogues.
candidates.en_evidence: No complete translation. McCabe, A Byzantine Encyclopaedia of Horse Medicine (OUP 2007) translates excerpts only; en.wikipedia lists no translation.
candidates.other_translations: No complete modern translation found in any language.
candidates.value: Unique ancient veterinary corpus. Apsyrtus served with the army on the Danube; his letters to named soldiers and landowners illuminate army logistics, horse-breeding and rural society. Also charms, verse and proverbs. For historians of medicine, the Roman army, agriculture and compilation.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: practical prose and letters; risks are hippological and drug terms and parallel recensions. A good showcase for visible agent debate over variants.
candidates.pilot_unit: Apsyrtus' prefaces and letters plus the opening fever chapters of the Berlin recension (CHG I), est. 8–10k words

candidates.title: Ὑποτύπωσις τῶν ἀστρονομικῶν ὑποθέσεων — Hypotyposis astronomicarum positionum (Outline of Astronomical Hypotheses); RU: Прокл, «Очерк астрономических гипотез»
candidates.author: Proclus Diadochus
candidates.size: Proem and 7 chapters; est. 25–30k words (Manitius 1909, c. 300 pp. with facing German)
candidates.edition: Manitius, Teubner 1909 (Greek and German; repr. 1974), public domain: https://www.wilbourhall.org/pdfs/proclus/ProclusHypotosis.pdf
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia «Прокл» gives no translation; absent from the ΣΧΟΛΗ translation index (2007–2026); no Russian version found.
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia «Proclus» links only the Greek text (astrologicon.org); de.wikipedia lists only Manitius' German. No English found.
candidates.other_translations: German: Manitius 1909 (the only one found).
candidates.value: Considered antiquity's best introduction to the Almagest (de.wikipedia); Proclus treats epicycles and eccentrics as calculating devices, not physical truths, a key text for 'saving the phenomena', Neoplatonism and Byzantine teaching (a textbook from the 13th c.). For philosophers and historians of science.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high-medium: lucid prose; diagrams and parameters must be verified against the Almagest; Manitius' German allows cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Proem, ch. 1 and ch. 7 (critique of the hypotheses), est. 6–8k words

candidates.title: Περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων / Θεραπευτικὸν ὀξέων καὶ χρονίων παθῶν — On the Causes and Signs, and the Therapy, of Acute and Chronic Diseases; RU: Аретей, «О причинах и признаках острых и хронических болезней»
candidates.author: Aretaeus of Cappadocia
candidates.size: 8 books (4 + 4); est. 55–60k words (Hude, CMG II)
candidates.edition: Hude, CMG II, 1923 (2nd ed. 1958), free online: http://cmg.bbaw.de/epubl/online/cmg_02.html. Adams 1856 Greek text is public domain.
candidates.ru_evidence: The detailed ru.wikipedia «Аретей из Каппадокии» tabulates 12 editions and translations (Latin, German, English, French), none Russian.
candidates.en_evidence: Adams, London 1856 (Sydenham Society), complete, public domain.
candidates.other_translations: German: Dewez 1790–1803, Mann 1858. French: Laennec/Grmek 2000 (Causes and Signs).
candidates.value: A literary masterpiece of Greek medicine with classic descriptions of diabetes, coeliac disease, asthma, migraine, tetanus, and mania and melancholy. Ideal for students and historians of medicine and psychiatry; Russian readers have no version at all.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: coherent descriptive prose; Ionic forms are manageable; Adams and Hude's apparatus serve for cross-checking, not as a base.
candidates.pilot_unit: Causes and Signs of Chronic Diseases, Book I (mania, melancholy, epilepsy) and II.2 (diabetes), est. 10–12k words

candidates.title: Κυρανίδες — Cyranides (Kyranides); RU: «Кираниды»
candidates.author: Anonymous (attributed to Hermes Trismegistus and Harpocration)
candidates.genre: Magical-medical natural history (stones, plants, birds, fish)
candidates.size: 4 books (plus 2 appended in Kaimakis); est. 40–50k words
candidates.edition: Kaimakis 1976 (critical; copyright). Ruelle and de Mély, Les lapidaires grecs, 1898 (partial Greek with French; public domain). Latin: Delatte 1942.
candidates.ru_evidence: No ru.wikipedia article; no Russian translation found in the checked catalogues (ΣΧΟΛΗ, Литпамятники).
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia lists only a 1685 English version (from Latin) and Waegeman 1987 (selected Book 1 passages). No modern complete English.
candidates.other_translations: French: de Mély 1898 (partial text). German: Arabic Book 1, Toral-Niehoff 2004.
candidates.value: Key Hermetic handbook of amulets, love-magic, lapidary and bestiary lore, influential in Latin, Arabic and Old French. Its prologue (Harpocration's stele) matters for Hermetism. For historians of magic, religion, science and medieval reception.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium-low: an unstable 'living text' with corrupt passages and rare names of stones, fish and plants. Uncertainty flags are mandatory; the editor checks against Kaimakis and the Latin.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book 1 prologue plus the first four letter-chapters (Α–Δ), est. 5–6k words

candidates.title: Zosimus' Greek alchemical works (Authentic Memoirs; On the Letter Omega; Final Quittance); RU: Зосима Панополитанский, «Подлинные записки», «О букве омега»
candidates.author: Zosimus of Panopolis
candidates.size: c. 28 fragmentary works; est. 25–35k words
candidates.edition: Berthelot & Ruelle, Collection des anciens alchimistes grecs, 1887–88 (Greek and French; public domain). Mertens, Budé 1995 (Mémoires authentiques; critical).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia «Зосима Панополитанский» cites only histories of chemistry, no translation; none found elsewhere.
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia: 'English translations remain elusive'; only excerpts (Mead's Omega excerpt; the Visions). Abt's English versions translate Arabic works.
candidates.other_translations: French: Berthelot–Ruelle 1888 (everything known at the time); Mertens 1995 (Budé).
candidates.value: The first named alchemist, foundational for the history of chemistry, Gnosticism, Hermetism and Egyptian temple technology; his dream-visions are major religious-literary texts. Broad humanities appeal.
candidates.ai_feasibility: low-medium: allegorical, corrupt, symbolic-technical vocabulary. Needs conservative literal translation, explicit uncertainty markers and reviewer debate.
candidates.pilot_unit: On the Letter Omega (Mertens, Mém. I) plus Final Quittance, est. 4–5k words

candidates.title: Περὶ ὕλης ἰατρικῆς — De materia medica; RU: Диоскорид, «О лекарственных веществах» (RU-gap)
candidates.author: Pedanius Dioscorides
candidates.size: 5 books, c. 800+ chapters; est. 130–160k words (Wellmann, 3 vols)
candidates.edition: Wellmann, 3 vols, Berlin 1906–14, public domain (archive.org).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia «Диоскорид» lists only the Greek and Latin 1549 edition and an English translation; nothing in ΣΧΟΛΗ or Литературные памятники.
candidates.en_evidence: Beck 2005 (3rd ed. 2017), complete; Osbaldeston 2000; Goodyer 1655 (en.wikipedia De materia medica).
candidates.other_translations: Spanish: García Valdés (Gredos 1998); many Renaissance vernacular versions (Italian, German, French, Spanish).
candidates.value: The most influential pharmacological work ever written (c. 600 plants plus animal and mineral drugs), the basis of European and Arabic materia medica until the 18th c. Essential to historians of medicine, botany, trade and lexicography; no Russian version.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: formulaic descriptions translate easily; plant identifications and synonyms need specialist control; use Beck only for cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Preface plus Book V (vine, wines, minerals), est. c. 15k words

candidates.title: Ἰατρικαὶ συναγωγαί — Collectiones medicae (Medical Collections); RU: Орибасий, «Врачебные собрания»
candidates.author: Oribasius of Pergamon
candidates.size: Originally 70 books, c. 25 survive (1–15, 21–22, 24–25, 43–51, fragments); est. 300k+ words (Raeder, CMG VI, 4 vols)
candidates.edition: Raeder, CMG VI 1–2 (1928–33), online at cmg.bbaw.de. Bussemaker–Daremberg 1851–76 (Greek and French), public domain.
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia «Орибасий» lists no translation; none found in ΣΧΟΛΗ or the Balalykin publications.
candidates.en_evidence: Grant, Dieting for an Emperor (Brill 1997): Books 1 and 4 only (en.wikipedia Oribasius).
candidates.other_translations: French: Bussemaker–Daremberg 1851–76 (surviving books). German: Haars 2018 (Book XV).
candidates.value: Preserves verbatim excerpts of lost physicians (Antyllus, Rufus, Athenaeus of Attaleia, Dieuches, Mnesitheus) alongside Galen. Prime source on ancient diet, exercise, baths and surgery. For historians of medicine, daily life and sport.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high-medium: expository excerpted prose; the layering of source attributions suits AI commentary that tracks Galenic and other parallels.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book VI (exercise, voice training, sleep; rich in Antyllus), est. 15–20k words

candidates.title: Περὶ συνθέσεως φαρμάκων τῶν κατὰ γένη — De compositione medicamentorum per genera (Composition of Drugs according to Kinds); RU: Гален, «О составлении лекарств по родам»
candidates.author: Galen of Pergamon
candidates.size: 7 books, Kühn XIII 362–1058; c. 102,000 words (Zainaldin et al. 2026)
candidates.edition: Only Kühn 1827 (Greek and Latin, public domain); no modern critical edition (Zainaldin et al. 2026; Fichtner no. 82).
candidates.ru_evidence: Not in the ru.wikipedia Galen translation list; the Balalykin series focuses on philosophical and anatomical works (vols II–V contents not fully verified).
candidates.en_evidence: Zainaldin et al. 2026: Comp. gen. 'has never been translated into English'. Fichtner bibliography (no. 82) lists no translation in any language.
candidates.other_translations: None found (Fichtner 2023/12).
candidates.value: Recipe book quoting many Hellenistic and early imperial pharmacologists: evidence for drug trade, pharmaceutical practice and lost authors. A methodological showcase, since a published LLM benchmark on this very text exists.
candidates.ai_feasibility: low-medium: Zainaldin et al. report mean 79.9/100, bimodal, with catastrophic failures on dense recipes but c. 95 on expository passages. Needs a term lexicon and pharmacological review.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book I (theory plus the first plaster groups), est. c. 15k words; the benchmark's 10 passages serve as a test set

candidates.title: Ὑπόμνημα εἰς τὴν Πτολεμαίου μαθηματικὴν σύνταξιν — Commentary on Ptolemy's Almagest; RU: Теон Александрийский, «Комментарий к „Альмагесту“»
candidates.author: Theon of Alexandria
candidates.size: Multi-book commentary; Rome's edition covers I–IV, the rest only Basel 1538; est. 150k+ words in total
candidates.edition: Rome, Studi e Testi 72 and 106 (1936–43; copyright). Basel 1538 editio princeps and Halma 1821–22 (I–II with French), public domain.
candidates.ru_evidence: Not in the ΣΧΟΛΗ translation index or ru.wikipedia; no Russian version found.
candidates.en_evidence: en.wikipedia «Theon of Alexandria» lists only Rome's and Tihon's French-language editions; no English translation found.
candidates.other_translations: French: Halma 1821–22 (Books I–II). Tihon's French translations cover Theon's Handy Tables commentaries, not the Almagest.
candidates.value: The principal late-antique guide to Ptolemy: sexagesimal arithmetic in Book I; the Book III heading credits Hypatia's edition, central to Hypatia and Alexandrian scholarship. Basis of Byzantine and Arabic Almagest teaching.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: formulaic mathematical prose; code agents must recompute every calculation; Halma serves for cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book I, est. 15–20k words (incl. sexagesimal division)

sweep:philosophy.corpus_overview:
Russian coverage here is uneven, and wider than often assumed. Fully or largely available in Russian: Porphyry (Sidash, Труды I–III, 2017–22; In Ptol. Harm., Tsypin 2013); all of Iamblichus (Sidash et al., 4 vols, 2020); Plutarch's Platonic and anti-Stoic treatises (Sidash 2008); Proclus' Elements, Platonic Theology and In Parm. (2006); Damascius' De principiis and In Parm.; Numenius, Nicomachus, Theon, Cleomedes and Timaeus Locrus (ΣΧΟΛΗ 2009–13); Ezekiel's Exagoge (2019). Ongoing: Proclus In Tim. (Mesyats, Book II, 2025), Philo De aeternitate (Afonasin 2025–26), Galen (Balalykin, Сочинения vols 1–5).
Gaps: of about 12 surviving Neoplatonic Plato commentaries, Hermias and Olympiodorus' three (In Alc., In Gorg., In Phaed.) have no Russian version at all, and neither do Damascius' In Phaed. and In Phileb. Proclus' In Remp., In Alc. and In Crat. exist only as excerpts. The Commentaria in Aristotelem Graeca (about 15,000 pages) have only a handful of Russian extracts, against more than 100 English volumes from the Ancient Commentators project (about 130 planned). Philo: about 14 of roughly 50 treatises are in Russian, but all are in English (Loeb, 12 vols). Philodemus: 3 works in Russian. Stobaeus: no complete translation into any modern language. Hellenistic Jewish historians: complete in English (Holladay), nothing in Russian.
Texts also missing in English: Philoponus' De opificio (German only), the Anonymous Theaetetus commentary (unpublished English draft only), Pseudo-Pythagorean ethical treatises (Italian only), and Stobaeus' chapters. Conclusion: Neoscholia can lead in Russian across the whole commentary tradition, but genuine world-first opportunities are few and valuable.

candidates.title: Περὶ κοσμοποιίας / De opificio mundi — John Philoponus, On the Creation of the World (RU «О сотворении мира»); pilot Book III
candidates.author: John Philoponus (Ioannes Grammaticus)
candidates.date: c. 546–560 CE (dedicated to Sergius of Antioch)
candidates.size: 7 books; Reichardt Teubner c. 300 pp.; est. 85–95k words (estimate)
candidates.edition: Reichardt, Teubner 1897, public domain: https://archive.org/details/joannisphiliponi00philuoft. Scholten, Fontes Christiani 23 (1997), Greek–German, copyrighted.
candidates.ru_evidence: Excerpts only: Benevich, Антология восточно-христианской богословской мысли II (2009), pp. 55–62 (ruwiki Иоанн Филопон). Ogovitsin, commentary on IV.4, ΣΧΟΛΗ 20.2 (2026). No full translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: The enwiki article on Philoponus' De opificio lists only Reichardt and Scholten's German. An Open Library search returns only Teubner and Herder editions. No English translation found.
candidates.other_translations: German: C. Scholten, Über die Erschaffung der Welt (Herder 1997, 3 vols). Other languages: none found.
candidates.value: Philoponus' late Christian synthesis of Alexandrian science. It applies impetus dynamics to the heavens and to light and cosmography, and attacks Theodore of Mopsuestia's (and Cosmas') cosmos. A key text for history of science and theology, Byzantine exegesis and the reception of Basil's Hexaemeron.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Clear technical prose, a public-domain Greek text, and abundant parallels (CAG, Basil). Risks: dense scientific terminology and the Antiochene polemical context. The German version can serve for cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book III (firmament, Gen 1:6–8; critique of the tabernacle-shaped cosmos), about 12–15k words (estimate). Alternative: prooemium plus Book I.

candidates.title: Anonymous Commentary on Plato's Theaetetus (P.Berol. inv. 9782); RU «Анонимный комментарий к „Теэтету“»
candidates.author: Anonymous Middle Platonist
candidates.date: Composed between the 1st c. BCE and mid-2nd c. CE; papyrus 2nd c. CE
candidates.size: 78 columns covering Tht. 142a–158a; est. 9–11k words
candidates.edition: Diels and Schubart, BKT II (1905), public domain: https://archive.org/details/anonymerkommenta00diel. Standard: Bastianini and Sedley, CPF III (1995), copyrighted.
candidates.ru_evidence: CyberLeninka searches ('Анонимный комментарий к Теэтету') return only studies. Absent from the translation sections of ΣΧΟΛΗ issues 2007–2026. No Russian version found.
candidates.en_evidence: The enwiki article lists only G. Boys-Stones' unpublished draft English translation (academia.edu, 2019). No published complete English translation found.
candidates.other_translations: Italian: Bastianini and Sedley, CPF III (1995). German: B. Hene, Leuven dissertation 2018 (per enwiki).
candidates.value: The earliest surviving commentary on any Platonic dialogue. Unique evidence for pre-Plotinian Platonism: an anti-Stoic critique of oikeiosis, the debate with sceptical Academics, and Theodorus' irrationals. Essential for historians of Platonism, epistemology and the commentary genre.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. Compact argumentative Greek, but the papyrus has lacunae and depends on supplements. It needs a papyrologist's check, and the readings should follow CPF.
candidates.pilot_unit: Whole text (about 10k words); first stage cols. I–XI (prologue plus the oikeiosis digression), about 1.5k words.

candidates.title: Εἰς τὸν Πλάτωνος Φαῖδρον σχόλια — Hermias, Commentary on Plato's Phaedrus (RU «Схолии к „Федру“»)
candidates.author: Hermias of Alexandria (recording Syrianus' lectures)
candidates.size: 3 books; Couvreur 266 pp.; est. 85–95k words (estimate)
candidates.edition: Couvreur 1901, public domain: https://archive.org/details/hermiaealexandr00couvgoog. Lucarini and Moreschini, Teubner 2012 (standard, copyrighted).
candidates.ru_evidence: ruwiki Гермий Александрийский lists no translation. CyberLeninka ('Гермий Федр перевод') and ΣΧΟΛΗ issues show only studies.
candidates.en_evidence: Baltzly and Share, Hermias: On Plato Phaedrus 227A–245E (Bloomsbury 2018), 245E–257C, and 257C–279C (2025), per Open Library.
candidates.other_translations: German: Bernard (1997), not verified in this sweep. French and Italian: unknown.
candidates.value: The only complete surviving Neoplatonic commentary on the Phaedrus, from Syrianus' school. Central for Neoplatonic theories of eros, divine madness, the soul-chariot, rhetoric and inspiration, and for the Renaissance reception (Ficino).
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Lemma-based scholastic prose with repetitive terminology, and the English version for cross-checking. Care is needed with Neoplatonic divine hierarchies.
candidates.pilot_unit: Commentary on the palinode myth, Phdr. 246a–249d, about 15k words (estimate).

candidates.title: Fragments of the Hellenistic Jewish historians (Demetrius, Eupolemus, Pseudo-Eupolemus, Artapanus, Cleodemus, Aristeas, Theodotus, Philo the Epic poet) plus Aristobulus; RU «Иудейско-эллинистические историки»
candidates.author: Various, mostly via Alexander Polyhistor in Eusebius, Praeparatio Evangelica IX and Clement
candidates.size: est. 12–15k words in total; Artapanus about 2.5k
candidates.edition: Gifford, Praeparatio Evangelica, 1903, public domain: https://archive.org/details/evangelicaepraep02euse. Freudenthal 1875, public domain. Mras GCS 1954–56 and Holladay (copyrighted).
candidates.ru_evidence: CyberLeninka (Артапан, Эвполем, Александр Полигистор) returns studies only. Only Ezekiel's Exagoge is translated (Религия. Церковь. Общество, 2019). No Russian Praeparatio Evangelica found.
candidates.en_evidence: C. R. Holladay, Fragments from Hellenistic Jewish Authors I–IV (SBL 1983–96; Aristobulus in vol. III, 1995), per Open Library.
candidates.other_translations: German: N. Walter, JSHRZ (1970s–80s), not verified in this sweep.
candidates.value: The earliest Jewish historiography in Greek: Moses as culture-hero (Artapanus), the Solomon–Hiram letters (Eupolemus), biblical chronography. Key for Jewish-Greek identity, Hellenistic legend and romance (parallels to Sesonchosis and Nectanebo), and New Testament backgrounds.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Short Koine excerpts, much of it reported speech. Risks: variants in Eusebius' manuscripts and chronological arithmetic. Holladay for cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Artapanus frs. 1–3 plus Demetrius frs. 1–6 (PE IX 18, 21, 23, 27, 29), about 5k words.

candidates.title: Ἐξήγησις εἰς τὸ Ἐπικτήτου Ἐγχειρίδιον — Simplicius, Commentary on Epictetus' Handbook (RU «Комментарий к „Энхиридию“ Эпиктета»)
candidates.author: Simplicius of Cilicia
candidates.size: Commentary on 53 chapters; est. 60–70k words (uncertain)
candidates.edition: Schweighäuser 1800 and Dübner 1840, public domain: https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_72SHc8S-I5sC. I. Hadot, critical edition (Brill 1996; Budé), copyrighted.
candidates.ru_evidence: ruwiki Симпликий lists Russian extracts only from In Phys. I.1 (1998) and In De caelo II (2005). CyberLeninka search for an Encheiridion commentary translation returns nothing.
candidates.en_evidence: Brennan and Brittain, Simplicius: On Epictetus Handbook 1–26 and 27–53 (Duckworth 2002; Bloomsbury reissue), per enwiki and Open Library.
candidates.other_translations: French: I. Hadot, Budé (vol. I, chs. 1–29). English: Stanhope 1694.
candidates.value: A Neoplatonist reading of the most popular Stoic manual: what is 'up to us', moral education, and a theodicy against the Manichaeans (ch. 35). Epictetus has a large Russian readership; the text links Stoicism with late Platonism.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Expository, homiletic prose. The Epictetus lemmata already exist in Russian, and the English version allows cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Prologue plus chapter 1 ('up to us'), about 8k words; or chapter 35 (anti-Manichaean theodicy), about 6k words (estimates).

candidates.title: Ἠθικὴ στοιχείωσις — Hierocles, Elements of Ethics (P.Berol. 9780) with the Stobaean excerpts On Duties; RU «Основы этики»
candidates.author: Hierocles the Stoic
candidates.size: About 11 papyrus columns plus about 15 Stobaean excerpts; est. 9–10k words
candidates.edition: von Arnim, BKT IV (1906), public domain: https://archive.org/details/coo.31924022696045. Bastianini and Long, CPF (1992), copyrighted.
candidates.ru_evidence: ruwiki Гиерокл (стоик) lists no translation. CyberLeninka ('Гиерокл Элементы этики', 'ойкейосис') finds none, and neither do the ΣΧΟΛΗ issues.
candidates.en_evidence: I. Ramelli (trans. D. Konstan), Hierocles the Stoic: Elements of Ethics, Fragments and Excerpts (SBL/Brill 2009), per Open Library.
candidates.other_translations: Italian in CPF I.1** (Bastianini and Long 1992), not verified in this sweep.
candidates.value: The main Imperial-age Stoic source on oikeiosis and self-perception. Contains the famous 'concentric circles' of concern and household ethics (marriage, parents, kin). Widely taught in courses on Stoicism and cosmopolitanism.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High for the Stobaeus excerpts; medium for the papyrus, which has lacunae and supplements. Small and manageable.
candidates.pilot_unit: Entire corpus, about 10k words. Mini-pilot: the 'circles' excerpt (Stobaeus IV.27.23), under 1k words.

candidates.title: Περὶ τῶν ἀρεσκόντων τοῖς φιλοσόφοις — [Plutarch], Placita philosophorum (Aëtius epitome); RU «О мнениях философов»
candidates.author: Aëtius, in the Pseudo-Plutarch epitome
candidates.date: Aëtius 1st c. CE; epitome c. 150 CE
candidates.size: 5 books; est. 25k words
candidates.edition: Diels, Doxographi Graeci (1879), public domain: https://archive.org/details/doxographigraec00dielgoog. Mansfeld and Runia, Aëtiana V (2020), copyrighted.
candidates.ru_evidence: No complete Russian version found (CyberLeninka: 'Плациты', 'Аэций доксограф'; archive.org). Individual testimonia appear in Presocratic collections (Lebedev, ФРГФ 1989).
candidates.en_evidence: Mansfeld and Runia, Aëtiana V: edition, translation and commentary of the reconstructed Placita (Brill 2020), per Open Library.
candidates.other_translations: French: Lachenaud, Budé (1993), not verified in this sweep. Others: unknown.
candidates.value: The backbone of ancient doxography: a systematic survey of physical opinions from Thales to the Stoics, and the source of many DK A-testimonia. Essential for teaching and research on early Greek philosophy and science; the Russian Presocratic-studies community is strong.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Terse, formulaic sentences. Care needed with attributions and the Stobaean parallel tradition. Public-domain Diels text.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book II (cosmos, heavens, sun, moon), about 6k words (estimate).

candidates.title: Pseudo-Pythagorean ethical and political treatises (Thesleff corpus): Pseudo-Archytas, Pseudo-Metopus, Pseudo-Theages, Pseudo-Euryphamus, Pseudo-Hippodamus, Callicratidas; RU «Псевдопифагорейские трактаты»
candidates.author: Pseudonymous 'Pythagoreans'
candidates.size: Thesleff 1965 about 250 pp.; ethical-political prose est. 25–30k words
candidates.edition: Thesleff 1965 (copyrighted). Public domain: Stobaeus, ed. Wachsmuth–Hense (archive.org adw8682) and Mullach, FPG (archive.org).
candidates.ru_evidence: Russian exists only for Timaeus Locrus (ΣΧΟΛΗ 2013), the Pythagorean women's letters (ΣΧΟΛΗ 2018) and the Stobaeus IV.7 kingship texts (2018). The ethical treatises: none found.
candidates.en_evidence: Thesleff gives the Greek only. No complete modern English found (Open Library). Old Taylor versions are reportedly in Guthrie's Pythagorean Sourcebook (not verified here).
candidates.other_translations: Italian: B. Centrone, Pseudopythagorica ethica (Bibliopolis 1990), per Open Library.
candidates.value: Hellenistic pseudepigrapha that shaped Middle Platonism, Philo and Neoplatonism: virtue, happiness, law, the household. Little known even to specialists; important for historians of ethics, political thought and the Pythagorean tradition.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. Artificial Doric and textual corruption; the units are short. Centrone's Italian helps with checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Centrone set: Pseudo-Archytas On the Good and Happy Man, Pseudo-Metopus and Pseudo-Theages On Virtue, Pseudo-Euryphamus, Pseudo-Hippodamus On Happiness; about 8k words (estimate).

candidates.title: Εἰς τὴν Πολιτείαν — Proclus, Commentary on the Republic, Essay 16 'On the Myth of Er' (RU «Комментарий к „Государству“»)
candidates.author: Proclus Diadochus
candidates.size: 17 essays, Kroll 2 vols (about 700 pp.). Essay 16 fills most of vol. II: about 250 pp., est. 70–80k words (estimate)
candidates.edition: W. Kroll, Teubner 1899–1901, public domain: https://archive.org/details/inplatonisrempu00krolgoog.
candidates.ru_evidence: ruwiki Прокл Диадох lists only Petrov's partial Essay 6 ('О способе создания божественных мифов', 1997) and selections (Феномен теургии, 2003, pp. 292–314; content not verified). No Russian Essay 16 found.
candidates.en_evidence: Baltzly, Finamore and Miles, Proclus: Commentary on Plato's Republic, 3 vols (CUP 2018, 2020, 2022). Lamberton, Essays 5–6 (SBL 2012). Per Open Library.
candidates.other_translations: French: Festugière, 3 vols (1970), per ruwiki.
candidates.value: The fullest ancient exegesis of Plato's eschatological myth: the geography of the afterlife, the choice of lives, the spindle of Necessity, astronomy. Preserves earlier interpreters (Numenius, Porphyry). Key for Neoplatonic eschatology and theory of myth.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Scholastic prose, with the English version for cross-checking. The astronomical and harmonic passages need specialist review.
candidates.pilot_unit: Opening of Essay 16 (purpose of the myth, Er's 'twelve days'), about 12k words (estimate).

candidates.title: Περὶ εἱμαρμένης — Alexander of Aphrodisias, On Fate (De fato); RU «О судьбе»
candidates.author: Alexander of Aphrodisias
candidates.date: c. 198–209 CE (dedicated to Severus and Caracalla)
candidates.size: Bruns pp. 164–212; est. 13–15k words
candidates.edition: Bruns, Supplementum Aristotelicum II.2 (1892), public domain: https://archive.org/details/alexandriaphrodi00alex.
candidates.ru_evidence: ruwiki Александр Афродисийский lists only Russian 'О смешении и росте' (Solopova 2002). CyberLeninka ('Александр Афродисийский О судьбе перевод') returns studies only.
candidates.en_evidence: R. W. Sharples, Alexander of Aphrodisias on Fate (Duckworth 1983; reprinted), per Open Library.
candidates.other_translations: French: Thillet, Budé (1984), not verified in this sweep. Others: unknown.
candidates.value: The classic Peripatetic refutation of Stoic fate. Central for the history of free will, responsibility and compatibilism; short and widely taught in philosophy curricula.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Clear argumentative prose with established terminology; short.
candidates.pilot_unit: The whole treatise, about 14k words.

candidates.title: Σχόλια εἰς τὸν Γοργίαν — Olympiodorus, Commentary on Plato's Gorgias (RU «Комментарий к „Горгию“»)
candidates.author: Olympiodorus the Younger
candidates.size: 50 lectures; Westerink Teubner 1970 about 270 pp.; est. 70–80k words (estimate)
candidates.edition: Norvin, Teubner 1936 (copyright status to check); Westerink, Teubner 1970 (standard, copyrighted).
candidates.ru_evidence: ruwiki Олимпиодор Младший lists Russian only for the Life of Plato (Gasparov 1979). CyberLeninka ('Олимпиодор … перевод') returns studies only.
candidates.en_evidence: Jackson, Lycos and Tarrant, Olympiodorus: Commentary on Plato's Gorgias (Brill 1998), per enwiki and Open Library.
candidates.other_translations: None found in this sweep.
candidates.value: The only extant ancient Gorgias commentary: political virtue, rhetoric versus philosophy, pagan teaching in Christian Alexandria, and allegory of the final myth. Useful for Plato reception, rhetoric and late antique education.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Lecture-note style and simple syntax. The myth section needs care.
candidates.pilot_unit: Lectures 46–50 on the final myth (Gorg. 523a–527e), about 8k words (estimate).

candidates.title: Περὶ παρρησίας — Philodemus, On Frank Criticism (PHerc. 1471); RU «О свободе речи»
candidates.author: Philodemus of Gadara (from Zeno of Sidon's lectures)
candidates.size: About 94 fragments plus 24 columns; est. 8–10k words (lacunose)
candidates.edition: Olivieri, Teubner 1914, public domain: https://archive.org/details/philodemiperipar00philuoft. Konstan et al. 1998 (improved text).
candidates.ru_evidence: ruwiki Филодем из Гадары lists Russian only for Oeconomicus (1969), On Poems V (1979) and the epigrams. Index Academicorum appeared in Respublica Literaria (2020–21). No Peri parrhesias found.
candidates.en_evidence: Konstan, Clay, Glad et al., Philodemus: On Frank Criticism (SBL 1998), per Open Library.
candidates.other_translations: Unknown, not checked in this sweep.
candidates.value: Unique evidence for therapeutic pedagogy in Epicurean communities (correction, confession). Central for parrhesia studies after Foucault, Pauline community ethics and Hellenistic psychology.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Low to medium. Fragmentary papyrus with heavy supplements; the public-domain Olivieri text is outdated. A papyrologist must check the readings.
candidates.pilot_unit: The continuous final columns Ia–XXIVb, about 3k words (estimate).

candidates.title: Ἀνθολόγιον IV.22–24 (on marriage, marital precepts, children) — John Stobaeus, Anthology; RU «Антология: о браке»
candidates.author: John Stobaeus (compiler)
candidates.date: Early 5th c. CE; excerpts from the 8th c. BCE to the 4th c. CE
candidates.size: About 200 excerpts; est. 15–20k words (estimate)
candidates.edition: Wachsmuth and Hense, 5 vols (1884–1912), public domain; vol. IV: https://archive.org/details/adw8682.0004.001.umich.edu.
candidates.ru_evidence: ruwiki Стобей: only Anth. IV.7 is in Russian (Исторический вестник 26, 2018), and it notes the anthology is untranslated as a whole. CyberLeninka shows no IV.22–24.
candidates.en_evidence: enwiki Stobaeus: 'entire work has not been translated into any modern language'. Only individual authors (Musonius, Hierocles, Antipater, Pseudo-Pythagoreans) exist in separate translations.
candidates.other_translations: No complete translation in any language (en/ru Wikipedia). Chapter-level translations: unknown.
candidates.value: A ready-made ancient dossier on marriage, from Homer and Menander to Antipater, Musonius, Hierocles and the Pythagorean women. Gender and household ideology across a millennium, with some otherwise lost texts. For social history, gender studies and classics.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High for the prose; medium for verse excerpts (comic and tragic fragments need identification against TrGF/PCG and attention to metre).
candidates.pilot_unit: IV.22a (philosophical prose excerpts on marriage), about 5k words (estimate).

candidates.title: Περὶ τοῦ βίου Μωυσέως — Philo, On the Life of Moses I–II (RU «О жизни Моисея»)
candidates.author: Philo of Alexandria
candidates.size: 2 books; est. 33k words (estimate)
candidates.edition: L. Cohn, Philonis Alexandrini opera IV (1902), public domain: https://archive.org/details/philonisalexandr0004leop.
candidates.ru_evidence: Absent from the ruwiki list of about 14 Russian Philo translations and from CyberLeninka and Yearbook listings (Matusova; Afonasin's De aeternitate, 2025–26). Not verified in the RSL catalogue.
candidates.en_evidence: F. H. Colson, Philo VI (Loeb 1935), per the ruwiki Loeb list. Also Yonge's 19th-c. translation.
candidates.other_translations: French (Œuvres de Philon) and German (Die Werke Philos) series exist; not individually verified here.
candidates.value: Moses portrayed as philosopher-king, lawgiver, priest and prophet. Key for Jewish-Greek political thought, Hellenistic ideal-ruler literature (cf. the Alexander tradition) and early Christian Moses typology.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High. Fluent Atticizing prose with rich parallels; Loeb for cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book I (Moses' birth to Balaam), about 18k words; mini-pilot Mos. II 1–65.

sweep:philosophy.ru_gap_notes: Available in English but not in Russian: Hermias In Phdr. (Baltzly–Share 2018–25); Olympiodorus In Alc., In Gorg. and In Phaed.; Damascius In Phaed. and In Phileb. (Westerink); Simplicius In Ench. (2002) and almost all of the roughly 130 Ancient Commentators on Aristotle volumes (Alexander, Simplicius, Philoponus, Ammonius, Themistius); Alexander De fato (Sharples 1983); Proclus In Remp. (CUP 2018–22, Russian has Essay 6 excerpts only) and In Alc. (Russian fragments only); Aëtius' Placita (2020); Hierocles the Stoic (2009); Philodemus On Anger, On Frank Criticism, On Piety and On Death; Aristocles of Messene (Chiesara 2001); the Hellenistic Jewish historians and Aristobulus (Holladay); Philo's Exposition of the Law and the Armenian Quaestiones (Loeb). Galen's PHP (De Lacy): Russian status unclear, check Balalykin's Сочинения.

sweep:christian-orient-graecoarabic.corpus_overview: I looked at about 40 texts from the Syriac, Coptic, Armenian, Georgian, Ge'ez, Middle Persian and Graeco-Arabic traditions. The session's web-search quota ran out, so I checked Russian status in other ways. I used the ru, en and hy Wikipedia APIs, the full vostlit.info alphabetical index (28 pages) and ancientrome.ru. I also used Solopova's Russian bibliographies (2017–2018) of Greek works preserved in Syriac, Armenian and Arabic, plus OpenAlex, archive.org and the CMG site. Russian coverage is already dense in several areas, so I dropped these texts. In Syriac historiography: the Edessa Chronicle (1959, 2000), Joshua the Stylite (1940), Ps.-Zachariah and John of Ephesus. The Chronicle of 1234 is partly translated (1946, 1964), and so are Michael the Syrian (Гусейнов) and Shenoute (Еланская 2001). Others: Mara bar Serapion, Bundahishn (1997) and Hippolytus' Georgian works (Marr). Kebra Nagast has only an amateur Russian version made from English, and the text is late. Solopova's bibliographies list almost no Russian translations of the Arabic-only Greek works: Galen, Themistius, Bryson, Mubashshir, Hunayn, Alexander of Aphrodisias. The same holds for the Armenian Philo, Eusebius' Chronicle and the Alexander Romance. These are the largest Russian gaps. Of the 14 shortlisted texts, 12 have no Russian translation; the Syriac Alexander Legend and Eusebius' Chronicle exist in Russian only in part. English: 10 have a full English translation, often an old one (1889–1990), 2 have a partial one, and 2 have none. Texts untranslated into any modern language are rare in this corpus; the Grabar Alexander Romance has not even been put into modern Armenian. Specialist reviewers are needed: Arabic for 7 texts, Armenian for 3, Syriac for 3, Ge'ez for 1. The editor's Greek gives direct control wherever Greek parallels survive.

candidates.title: Patmutʿiwn Aghekʿsandri Makedonacʿwoy (Armenian Alexander Romance, 'History of Alexander of Macedon'); RU: «История Александра Македонского» (армянская версия)
candidates.author: Anonymous (5th-c. Armenian translation of Ps.-Callisthenes, α-recension; sometimes ascribed to Movses Khorenatsi)
candidates.date: Greek α 3rd c. CE; Armenian 5th c.
candidates.size: Three books; c. 45–50k words (estimate; Wolohojian's English c. 160 pp.)
candidates.edition: Venice 1842 Mekhitarist edition (public domain); critical edition by H. Simonyan, Yerevan 1989 (copyrighted). Greek α (Kroll 1926, public domain) can be used for alignment.
candidates.ru_evidence: Not mentioned in ru.wiki «История Александра Великого», the vostlit index or Solopova 2017 (Graeco-Armeniaca). hy.wiki says the Grabar text has not even been put into modern Armenian. Simonyan 1979 (Ист.-филол. журнал) is a study, not a translation.
candidates.en_evidence: Wolohojian, The Romance of Alexander the Great by Pseudo-Callisthenes (Columbia UP 1969); PDF at attalus.org/armenian/Tales_Alexander_Wolohojian_trans.pdf
candidates.other_translations: No other modern translation found (only studies).
candidates.value: With Julius Valerius and the Syriac, this is the closest witness to the lost α-recension and preserves passages missing from Greek MS A. It has some 30 parallels with Movses Khorenatsi. It sits squarely in the editor's PhD field and would give Russian readers their first access to it.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. Current LLMs are weak in Classical Armenian, but the surviving Greek α and Julius Valerius allow control line by line. Needs an Armenian-literate reviewer.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book I chs. 1–14 (Nectanebo and Alexander's birth), c. 6k words, aligned with Greek MS A.

candidates.title: Tašʿitā d-Aleksandros (Syriac Alexander Romance / Syriac Pseudo-Callisthenes); RU: «Сирийская версия романа об Александре»
candidates.author: Anonymous translator (from Greek, perhaps via a lost Middle Persian version, as Nöldeke argued)
candidates.size: 3 books, 85 chapters; c. 40k words (estimate; Budge's English pp. 1–143)
candidates.edition: Budge 1889, Syriac text with English (public domain; archive.org/details/BudgeSyriacAlexander). No modern critical edition.
candidates.ru_evidence: No Russian translation in the vostlit index or ru.wiki. Solopova 2017 (Graeco-Syriaca) lists only Pigulevskaya 1958, which is on the Legend, not the Romance.
candidates.en_evidence: Budge 1889 is the only English translation (en.wiki); it is outdated and based on late manuscripts.
candidates.other_translations: No other modern translation found; there are studies (Nöldeke 1890; Ciancaglini, Le Muséon 2001).
candidates.value: An α-recension witness and the source of the Arabic, Ethiopic and Persian Alexander traditions. Central to Dhu l-Qarnayn and Quran-context debates. A new annotated translation with Greek collation would replace Budge for both Russian and English readers.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium-high. Syriac prose is handled reasonably well, and Budge's English and the Greek α serve as controls. A Syriac reviewer is needed for vocalisation and Persian loans.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book III (India, Letter to Aristotle, Candace, death), c. 12k words; alternatively Book I chs. 1–14.

candidates.title: Neṣḥānā d-Aleksandros (Syriac Alexander Legend) + Memra on Alexander ('Song of Alexander', Ps.-Jacob of Serugh); RU: «Сирийская легенда об Александре», «Песнь об Александре»
candidates.author: Anonymous (the Song is wrongly attributed to Jacob of Serugh)
candidates.size: Legend: Budge pp. 144–158. Song: Budge pp. 163–200, three recensions. Together c. 12k words (estimate).
candidates.edition: Budge 1889 (public domain). Song: critical edition by Reinink, CSCO 454–455 (1983; copyrighted).
candidates.ru_evidence: Legend: Пигулевская, «Сирийская легенда об Александре Македонском», Палестинский сборник 3 (66), 1958, pp. 75–97 (found via Solopova 2017; whether it contains a full translation is unverified). Song: no Russian translation found.
candidates.en_evidence: Budge 1889 (both texts; en.wiki). Reinink 1983 gives a German translation of the Song.
candidates.other_translations: German: Reinink 1983 (Song).
candidates.value: Earliest Alexander's Gate / Gog–Magog apocalyptic; Heraclian propaganda; key background to Quran 18:83–102. A hot debate (Tesei 2023). The Song is not available in Russian at all.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High for the prose Legend; medium for the Song (verse, three recensions).
candidates.pilot_unit: Song of Alexander, Reinink recension I (c. 3–4k words, estimate), with the Legend's Gate episode for comparison.

candidates.title: Ādāb al-falāsifa ('Sayings of the Philosophers'): Alexander section (philosophers' sayings at Alexander's coffin, his consolation letter to his mother); RU: «Изречения философов»
candidates.author: Ḥunayn ibn Isḥāq (survives in al-Anṣārī's abridgment)
candidates.date: 9th c. CE; compiles late-antique Greek gnomologia
candidates.size: Whole text unknown (c. 40k words?); Alexander unit c. 5k words (estimate)
candidates.edition: Badawi, Kuwait 1985 (copyrighted); Bandak 2007, Arabic–Castilian edition (copyrighted). No public-domain text found.
candidates.ru_evidence: Solopova 2018 (Graeco-Arabic bibliography) lists only Zakeri 2008, a study, and no Russian translation. The ru.wiki search found nothing.
candidates.en_evidence: No English translation found through OpenAlex or Wikipedia; only studies (Zakeri 2008). Excerpts in anthologies were not checked.
candidates.other_translations: Medieval Castilian Libro de los buenos proverbios (Bandak 2007; Walsh 1976 study); medieval Hebrew. No modern full translation found.
candidates.value: It carries lost Greek gnomic material and the Alexander-death tradition (funeral sayings) also known in Syriac and Ps.-Callisthenes reception. It is the missing link from Greek to Arabic to Castilian. Untranslated in both Russian and English.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High (Arabic). An Arabist is needed for the textual issues; Syriac and Greek parallels can be used to check.
candidates.pilot_unit: Alexander section (coffin sayings + letter to Olympias), c. 5k words (estimate).

candidates.title: Mukhtār al-ḥikam wa-maḥāsin al-kalim ('Choicest Maxims'): chapters on Alexander and Aristotle; RU: «Избранные изречения и лучшие речения»
candidates.author: al-Mubashshir ibn Fātik
candidates.date: 1048–49 CE; draws on Greek late-antique sources
candidates.genre: Lives and sayings of 21 (mainly Greek) sages
candidates.size: Alexander chapter c. 8–10k words (estimate); whole book c. 120k words (estimate)
candidates.edition: Badawi, Madrid 1958 (copyrighted). The Lives of Alexander and Aristotle were published separately in the 19th c. (en.wiki), probably public domain.
candidates.ru_evidence: Solopova 2018 lists only Rosenthal 1960–61 (prolegomena), no Russian translation. ru.wiki mentions him only in passing («Княжеские зерцала»).
candidates.en_evidence: No modern English translation. English exists only as medieval versions (Scrope 1450; Woodville/Caxton 1477, the 'Dictes and Sayings') via Latin and French (en.wiki).
candidates.other_translations: Medieval: Castilian Bocados de oro, Latin Liber philosophorum moralium antiquorum, French Dits moraulx. No modern full translation found.
candidates.value: An Arabic life of Alexander that fuses the Romance with Graeco-Arabic wisdom literature. Source of the Dictes (the first dated book printed in England). Bridges the Alexander Romance and gnomic tradition.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High (Arabic). Bocados de oro and the Middle English can serve as cross-checks.
candidates.pilot_unit: Alexander chapter, c. 8k words (estimate).

candidates.title: Risālat Arisṭūṭālīs ilā l-Iskandar fī siyāsat al-mudun ('Letter of Aristotle to Alexander on the Policy towards Cities'), with Sālim Abū l-ʿAlāʾ's Aristotle–Alexander letter cycle as an extension; RU: «Письмо Аристотеля Александру о политике в отношении городов»
candidates.author: Ps.-Aristotle (Greek original lost; Plezia argued for a Hellenistic or authentic core)
candidates.date: Greek original Hellenistic(?); Arabic translation 8th c. (Umayyad chancery)
candidates.size: c. 5k words (estimate)
candidates.edition: Bielawski & Plezia, Lettre d'Aristote à Alexandre sur la politique envers les cités (Wrocław 1970): Arabic text + French + Latin (copyrighted).
candidates.ru_evidence: Solopova 2018 mentions the Aristotle–Alexander correspondence but lists no Russian translation. The ru.wiki search found nothing.
candidates.en_evidence: Swain 2013, 'Appendix: Letter of Aristotle to Alexander', in Themistius, Julian, and Greek Political Theory (CUP), per its OpenAlex record; how complete it is was not verified.
candidates.other_translations: French and Latin (Bielawski–Plezia 1970). Sālim's letter cycle: French in Grignaschi (Muséon 1967), per Gutas 2009.
candidates.value: Hellenistic theory of world rule, Greeks and Persians under Alexander; the earliest Arabic political translation. Directly relevant to Alexander historiography and the epistolary layer of the Romance.
