candidates.ai_feasibility: High (Arabic). French and Latin translations allow cross-checking; an Arabist is needed for the 8th-c. chancery style.
candidates.pilot_unit: The whole Letter on Cities, c. 5k words (estimate).

candidates.title: Chronicon, Book I (Chronographia), Armenian version; RU: «Хроника» Евсевия, кн. I
candidates.author: Eusebius of Caesarea
candidates.language: Classical Armenian (Greek lost apart from fragments)
candidates.genre: Chronography with excerpts from lost historians
candidates.size: Schoene–Petermann pp. 1–295; c. 70–80k words (estimate)
candidates.edition: Aucher 1818 (Armenian + Latin + Greek, public domain, archive.org); Schoene–Petermann 1875 (public domain); Karst 1911 (GCS, German, public domain).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wiki «Хроника Евсевия»: only partial Russian translations (the Roman part, via Jerome, Kiev 1910). ancientrome.ru has only a list of Ptolemies (translated from English) and the Berossus fragments.
candidates.en_evidence: Andrew Smith, attalus.org/translate/eusebius.html (from the Schoene Latin), covering all of Book I.
candidates.other_translations: German: Karst 1911. Latin: Aucher 1818, Petermann 1875.
candidates.value: Preserves excerpts from Berossus, Abydenus, Alexander Polyhistor and Manetho, and Porphyry's lists of the Macedonian, Thessalian, Ptolemaic and Seleucid kings, plus the Olympic victor list. Indispensable for Hellenistic chronology; no Russian apparatus exists.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium (Armenian). Strong controls exist: Greek fragments (Syncellus), Latin and German translations.
candidates.pilot_unit: Macedonian, Thessalian and Asian/Syrian kings (Porphyry excerpts), c. 6–8k words: the history after Alexander.

candidates.title: De providentia I–II (Armenian), with De animalibus ('Alexander') as a companion piece; RU: Филон Александрийский, «О провидении»
candidates.author: Philo of Alexandria
candidates.date: c. 40 CE; Armenian translation c. 6th c.
candidates.language: Classical Armenian (Greek lost apart from Book II fragments in Eusebius, Praeparatio Evangelica 7–8)
candidates.genre: Philosophical dialogue (Philo vs. Ti. Julius Alexander)
candidates.size: Books I–II c. 25–30k words (estimate)
candidates.edition: Aucher 1822, Armenian + Latin (public domain; archive.org/details/philonisjudaeis00judgoog).
candidates.ru_evidence: Solopova 2017 (Graeco-Armeniaca) lists no Russian translation of the Armenian Philo; Russian work on it is only philological (Zeltchenko 2026 on De animalibus 31).
candidates.en_evidence: Only the Greek fragments of Book II (Loeb Philo IX, from standard reference, not re-verified). De animalibus: English by Terian 1981 (verified via reviews).
candidates.other_translations: Latin: Aucher 1822. French: Hadas-Lebel 1973 (Œuvres de Philon 35; not re-verified).
candidates.value: Philo's only debate on providence and theodicy, setting out Stoic, Epicurean and Academic arguments. Throws light on the Alexandrian elite (the future prefect Tiberius Alexander). The Greek overlap in Book II allows a controlled translation.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium. The 'Hellenizing' Armenian closely calques Greek, and the Latin plus the Greek fragments serve as checks.
candidates.pilot_unit: Book II, c. 12k words (estimate), starting with the sections that overlap Eusebius' Greek.

candidates.title: Risāla ilā Yūliyānūs fī l-siyāsa ('Letter/Oration to the Emperor on Government'); RU: Фемистий, «Послание к Юлиану об управлении государством»
candidates.author: Themistius
candidates.date: 4th c. CE (addressee debated); Arabic translation 9th–10th c.
candidates.size: c. 8–10k words (estimate)
candidates.edition: Arabic text with Latin by I. Shahîd in Themistii Orationes III (Teubner 1974; not re-verified); Swain 2013. No public-domain Arabic text.
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wiki «Фемистий» lists Russian translations only of Orations 3, 12, 30 (Егунов 1961) and 25, 27 (Грабарь-Пассек 1964). Solopova 2018 lists no Russian translation of the Arabic Themistius.
candidates.en_evidence: Swain, Themistius, Julian, and Greek Political Theory under Rome: Texts, Translations and Studies of Four Key Works (CUP 2013).
candidates.other_translations: Latin: Shahîd 1974.
candidates.value: A Greek theory of kingship lost in Greek. Key for Late Antique imperial ideology (Julian–Themistius) and for early Arabic political thought.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High (Arabic). Swain's and Shahîd's versions are available for cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: The whole Risāla, c. 8–10k words (estimate).

candidates.title: De optimo medico cognoscendo (Arabic Fī miḥnat afḍal al-aṭibbāʾ, 'On Examining the Physician'); RU: Гален, «Об испытании (распознавании) лучшего врача»
candidates.author: Galen
candidates.date: Late 2nd c. CE; Arabic translation from Hunayn's circle, 9th c.
candidates.size: c. 25k words (estimate)
candidates.edition: Iskandar, CMG Suppl. Or. IV (Berlin 1988), Arabic + English; free online at cmg.bbaw.de (copyrighted).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wiki «Гален» lists all Russian translations (Терновский 1971, Балалыкин/Щеглов 2014, Пролыгина, Афонасин); none is of an Arabic-only work. Solopova 2018 lists none.
candidates.en_evidence: Iskandar 1988 (CMG Suppl. Or. IV), confirmed on the CMG online list.
candidates.other_translations: None found.
candidates.value: Galen on charlatans, public demonstrations and how to test physicians in Rome; strongly autobiographical. A core source for the social history of Roman medicine.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High (Arabic). Iskandar's English is available for cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: The Rome anecdotes and test chapters, c. 6k words (estimate).

candidates.title: Galen's ethical and Platonic works in Arabic: Peri ēthōn (De moribus, Arabic epitome) and Compendium Timaei Platonis; RU: «О нравах»; «Краткое изложение „Тимея“»
candidates.author: Galen
candidates.size: De moribus c. 12k words; Compendium c. 8k words (estimates)
candidates.edition: Compendium: Kraus & Walzer, Plato Arabus I (1951), Arabic + Latin. De moribus: Kraus 1937 epitome (not re-verified). Both copyrighted.
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wiki «Гален» Russian list: absent. Solopova 2018 lists only Western editions and studies.
candidates.en_evidence: De moribus: Mattock 1972 (listed in Solopova 2018). Compendium: no English translation located; Latin 1951 only; Das 2021 is a study.
candidates.other_translations: Latin: Kraus–Walzer 1951. French: Festugière & Tonneau 1952 (study and translation).
candidates.value: Galen's lost moral psychology and his Middle Platonist reading of the Timaeus. Valuable for historians of philosophy and of Plato's reception.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Medium-high (Arabic); the Latin version helps.
candidates.pilot_unit: Compendium Timaei, all extant fragments, c. 8k words (estimate).

candidates.title: Oikonomikos (Arabic Tadbīr al-manzil, 'Management of the Estate'); RU: Брисон, «Ойкономикос»
candidates.author: Bryson (Neopythagorean)
candidates.language: Arabic (Greek lost; Hebrew and Latin versions derive from it)
candidates.size: c. 7–8k words (estimate)
candidates.edition: Plessner 1928, Arabic + German (archive.org); Swain 2013 critical edition.
candidates.ru_evidence: No ru.wiki hits; Solopova 2018 lists no Russian translation.
candidates.en_evidence: Swain, Economy, Family, and Society from Rome to Islam (CUP 2013), per reviews indexed in OpenAlex.
candidates.other_translations: German: Plessner 1928.
candidates.value: The only imperial-age Greek oikonomikos (household-management treatise) surviving in full. Covers slaves, wives, children and wealth; it shaped Miskawayh and Tusi. Useful to economic and social historians.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High (Arabic, short); the German and English translations are available for cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: The whole text, c. 7k words (estimate).

candidates.title: Chronicle of John of Nikiu (Ge'ez version); RU: «Хроника» Иоанна Никиусского
candidates.author: John, bishop of Nikiu
candidates.date: c. 690s CE; Ge'ez translation 1602 from a lost Arabic version
candidates.size: 122 chapters; c. 70k words (estimate; Charles c. 200 pp.)
candidates.edition: Zotenberg 1883, Ge'ez + French (public domain, Gallica).
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wiki «Иоанн Никиусский» lists only Charles's English; absent from the vostlit index. Russian studies only quote passages (Мингазов 2012 on Kubrat; Холод 2023–24).
candidates.en_evidence: Charles 1916 (tertullian.org/fathers/nikiu2_chronicle.htm).
candidates.other_translations: French: Zotenberg 1883.
candidates.value: The only Egyptian narrative of the Arab conquest of Egypt (chs. 111–121). Also has unusual traditions on Cambyses, the Argead kings, Alexander and the Ptolemies.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Low-medium. Ge'ez is weak in LLMs; Zotenberg and Charles are the controls, and an Ethiopist reviewer is required.
candidates.pilot_unit: Chs. 111–121 (Arab conquest), c. 12k words; or the Cambyses-to-Ptolemies chapters, c. 5k words.

candidates.title: Julian Romance (Syriac narrative of Julian the Apostate and Jovian); RU: «Сирийский роман о Юлиане Отступнике»
candidates.author: Anonymous (perhaps Edessene)
candidates.date: Between 363 and the 6th c. (oldest manuscript 6th c.)
candidates.size: c. 80k words (estimate; Hoffmann 1880 edition)
candidates.edition: Hoffmann 1880, Syriac text (public domain); BL Add. 14641.
candidates.ru_evidence: ru.wiki «Сирийская литература» names the romance but gives no translation; absent from the vostlit index.
candidates.en_evidence: Gollancz 1928; Sokoloff 2017 (Gorgias), per en.wiki.
candidates.other_translations: French: Richer 1978 (abridged). German: Nöldeke 1874 (second Romance).
candidates.value: A major Syriac narrative and the Christian counter-image of Julian's Persian campaign; used by Tabari. Brockelmann's Lexicon cites it 1,117 times. Matters to Late Antique historians.
candidates.ai_feasibility: High (Syriac prose); good English versions are available for cross-checking.
candidates.pilot_unit: Part III (Persian expedition, Jovian), c. 20k words (estimate).

sweep:christian-orient-graecoarabic.ru_gap_notes: These texts exist in English but not in Russian. Armenian Alexander Romance (Wolohojian 1969). Syriac Alexander Romance (Budge 1889). Eusebius' Chronicle Book I (attalus.org). Themistius' Risāla and Bryson (Swain 2013). Galen, On Examining the Physician (Iskandar 1988). Galen, De moribus (Mattock 1972). Apollonius, Conics V–VII (Toomer 1990; Russian has only Books I–IV, 2019). John of Nikiu (Charles 1916). Julian Romance (Gollancz 1928; Sokoloff 2017). Coptic Cambyses Romance (Jansen 1950). Philo, De animalibus (Terian 1981). Not re-verified and taken from standard references: Galen, On Medical Experience (Walzer 1944); Nicolaus of Damascus, On Plants; Alexander of Aphrodisias, On the Cosmos (Genequand 2001); Syriac Sentences of Menander.

sweep:epigraphy-papyri.corpus_overview: Epigraphy and papyrology are much less translated than literary texts. Papyri: I computed figures from the papyri.info data (GitHub idp.data, Oct 2026). There are 68,022 HGV documentary records. Translations hosted on papyri.info exist for 6,689 (about 10%). HGV lists translations published outside the editio princeps for 4,540 (6.7%): EN 2,433, DE 1,335, FR 871, IT 449, ES 70, Russian 0. Translations printed inside editions (P.Oxy., P.Mich.) are not counted. Example: P.Cair.Zen. has 822 texts and only 146 with any listed translation. DCLP holds 14,845 literary and subliterary papyri. Inscriptions: hundreds of thousands of Greek and Latin texts, translated only selectively. AIO covers Attica in English (ongoing), CGRN covers ritual norms (EN+FR) and IOSPE³ the Black Sea (EN+RU). Large uniform dossiers are still untranslated: Delphic manumissions (1,341 acts; Mulliez's CID V translates only some, into French), Dodona oracle tablets (4,200+; c. 150 in English in Eidinow 2007), Kaibel's c. 1,150 verse inscriptions, and the c. 2,300 CLE poems (204 in English in Courtney 1995). Russian coverage centres on Black Sea epigraphy, single set pieces (Gortyn code: Kazamanova, Myakin 2005; Parian Marble on ancientrome.ru) and scattered translations in articles. I found no Russian corpus translation for any dossier proposed here. Old public-domain editions (SGDI, Kaibel, Bücheler, Wünsch, Audollent, Edgar, Hiller, CIL) allow the source text to be published openly next to the translation. Caveat: web search was unavailable, so checks used catalogues (CyberLeninka, BMCR, archive.org, papyri.info data).

candidates.title: Delphic manumission acts (sale-to-Apollo); RU «Дельфийские акты об отпуске рабов»; pilot: earliest c. 100 acts
candidates.author: Anonymous (Delphic sanctuary/civic records)
candidates.size: 1,341 acts (Mulliez vol. 1: 722 + vol. 2: 619); est. 100–150k words
candidates.edition: SGDI II (Baunack 1892–99; public domain, archive.org sammlungdergriec0201colluoft/0202); FD III; standard: Mulliez, CID V (EFA 2020, 2023; copyrighted)
candidates.ru_evidence: CyberLeninka searches ('манумиссия Дельфы', 'дельфийские надписи об отпуске рабов') found studies only. The ancientrome.ru Delphi section has only Zelinsky's literary oracles.
candidates.en_evidence: No English corpus translation found. BMCR 2024.02.43 on Mulliez mentions no English. Only isolated sourcebook examples (from memory).
candidates.other_translations: French, selective: Mulliez, CID V vol. 1 (2020), 'not in every case', list on p. 655 (BMCR 2024.02.43)
candidates.value: The largest Greek dossier on slavery and manumission: slaves' names, origins, prices, paramonē (continued-service) obligations, women, families, guarantors. Central for social, legal and economic history, prosopography and onomastics; used by historians of slavery and of Delphi.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: very formulaic, clear structure. Risks: dating by archons and priesthoods, legal terms (paramonē, bebaiōtēr), lacunae.
candidates.pilot_unit: Acts of the first priesthoods (c. 201–170 BC): c. 100 acts from SGDI (public domain), c. 10–12k words

candidates.title: Zenon archive: P.Cair.Zen. I–V (Edgar, Zenon Papyri, 1925–31); RU «Архив Зенона»
candidates.author: Zenon of Kaunos, Apollonios the dioiketes and their correspondents
candidates.size: P.Cair.Zen.: 822 HGV records. Related sets: P.Lond. VII 261, P.Mich. I 111, PSI IV–VI 376 records
candidates.edition: C. C. Edgar, Catalogue général du Caire (1925–31): Greek text with English summaries and notes but no translations (OCR check of vol. II). Public-domain scans on archive.org; digital text on papyri.info (CC).
candidates.ru_evidence: CyberLeninka finds studies only (e.g., on Ptolemaic officials, 2019). HGV metadata records zero Russian translations across 68,022 papyri.
candidates.en_evidence: My HGV computation: 146 of 822 P.Cair.Zen. texts list any translation, 14 hosted on papyri.info. By contrast P.Mich. I (Edgar 1931) is fully translated (111/111).
candidates.other_translations: Scattered DE/FR/IT items among the 146 (HGV); no systematic translation
candidates.value: The richest archive of early Ptolemaic Egypt: the Philadelphia gift estate, Greek settlers, agriculture, taxation, trade with Syria-Palestine, everyday letters. A staple of Hellenistic history teaching, yet about 80% of the Cairo texts have no translation in any language.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium-high: koine prose with machine-readable text, and Edgar's summaries help. Risks: abbreviations, accounts, fragmentary letters, technical vocabulary.
candidates.pilot_unit: P.Cair.Zen. II (nos. 59140–59297; 158 numbers, 1926), est. 15–20k Greek words

candidates.title: Kaibel, Epigrammata Graeca ex lapidibus conlecta (1878); RU «Греческие стихотворные надписи»; pilot: Attic sepulchral epigrams nos. 1–178
candidates.author: Anonymous verse inscriptions (ed. G. Kaibel)
candidates.size: c. 1,150 numbered poems (index runs past 1130); est. 6–9k lines
candidates.edition: Kaibel 1878 (public domain, archive.org epigrammatagraec00kaibuoft). For collation: CEG (Hansen), Peek GVI (1955), SGO (Merkelbach–Stauber 1998–2004), all copyrighted.
candidates.ru_evidence: No corpus translation found. CyberLeninka ('греческие стихотворные эпитафии перевод') returned nothing relevant. Only scattered items, e.g. in Black Sea corpora.
candidates.en_evidence: No English corpus translation found. Selections only in anthologies and studies (memory; not itemised).
candidates.other_translations: German: SGO (East Greek, with translations); Peek, Griechische Grabgedichte (1960), a selection
candidates.value: Inscribed epigram is the 'people's poetry' of Greece: grief, family, gender, status and afterlife beliefs. It is the indispensable counterpart to the Anthologia Palatina for the history of the genre. Russian readers have no corpus; strong appeal for students and the general public.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high: metrical, formulaic, well edited. Kaibel's 1878 supplements must be checked against CEG/IG; the commentary should flag restorations.
candidates.pilot_unit: Kaibel 1–178 (section 'Sepulcralia: Attica'; no. 179 begins 'Insularum et Asiae'), est. c. 1,000 lines

candidates.title: Dodona oracular lead tablets (questions to Zeus Naios and Dione); RU «Вопросы к оракулу Додоны»
candidates.author: Anonymous consultants (private individuals and cities)
candidates.size: 4,200+ tablets, mostly 5–40 words
candidates.edition: Dakaris–Vokotopoulou–Christidis 2013 (2 vols, Athens; copyrighted); Lhôte 2006 (Droz); early public-domain: Carapanos, Dodone et ses ruines (1878, archive.org)
candidates.ru_evidence: CyberLeninka ('Додона', 'оракульные таблички Додоны') shows only studies (2019 sanctuary article; 2026 article on divination); no translation collection found.
candidates.en_evidence: Eidinow, Oracles, Curses and Risk (2007): catalogue of 'upwards of 150' questions with translations (BMCR 2008.01.14). Wikipedia: 4,200+ tablets.
candidates.other_translations: French: Lhôte 2006, Les lamelles oraculaires de Dodone (selection)
candidates.value: A unique set of first-person questions from ordinary Greeks about marriage, children, health, travel, slaves and business, plus city consultations. Important for religion, mentalities and dialectology. Very attractive for students and general readers; ideal showcase.
candidates.ai_feasibility: medium: short texts, but dialects, local alphabets, palimpsests and heavy restoration. The AI should translate the editors' readings and mark uncertainty. Copyright: cite the 2013 readings with attribution.
candidates.pilot_unit: 200 best-preserved questions (Lhôte's set cross-checked against 2013 corpus), c. 4–5k words

candidates.title: Carmina Latina Epigraphica (Bücheler 1895–97; Lommatzsch 1926); RU «Латинские эпиграфические стихотворения»; pilot: verse epitaphs
candidates.author: Anonymous Latin verse inscriptions
candidates.size: c. 2,300 numbered poems; est. 15k+ lines
candidates.edition: Bücheler, Anthologia Latina II.1–2 (Teubner 1895–97, public domain, archive.org); Engström 1912 supplement (public domain); Lommatzsch 1926
candidates.ru_evidence: Only single poems in articles, e.g. «Метрическая эпитафия Луция Калидия Эротика» (ИЯКФ 2014, CyberLeninka). No collection found.
candidates.en_evidence: Courtney, Musa Lapidaria (1995): 204 poems with facing English translation (BMCR 1998.03.12), i.e. under 10% of CLE.
candidates.other_translations: Regional CLE corpora with Spanish/Italian translations exist (extent not checked)
candidates.value: The largest body of non-literary Latin poetry: family feeling, social values, reception of Virgil and Ovid, Vulgar Latin and metrics. Excellent for Latin teaching; Russian readers have no anthology.
candidates.ai_feasibility: high for sense. Medium for metre, Vulgar spellings and Bücheler's supplements; check against CIL/EDCS.
candidates.pilot_unit: 150 verse epitaphs from Rome (CLE sepulcralia), est. 1,200 lines; alternative: the Pompeian carmina

candidates.title: Defixionum Tabellae Atticae (Wünsch 1897) with Audollent, Defixionum Tabellae (1904); RU «Аттические таблички с проклятиями»
candidates.author: Anonymous (curse-tablet writers)
candidates.size: DTA c. 220 tablets; DT c. 305; mostly short

sweep:epigraphy-papyri.ru_gap_notes: Translated into English but not, as a collection, into Russian: Welles's 75 Hellenistic royal letters (1934, Greek and English); Betz's Greek Magical Papyri (1986, full English; no scholarly Russian found); Diogenes of Oenoanda (Smith 1993/2003/2014 English; Russian only an amateur online version); Courtney's 204 Latin verse inscriptions (1995); CGRN ritual norms (English and French online); Attic Inscriptions Online (thousands of Attic texts in English); P.Mich. I Zenon papyri (111 of 111 English on papyri.info). HGV metadata records 2,433 papyri with published English translations and none with Russian. Any curated Russian anthology of documentary papyri (Select Papyri type) would therefore be new.

missing_areas: Method note: the session's WebSearch quota (200/200) was already used up when this critique started. Every status below was therefore checked by fetching specific sources directly: ru.wikipedia raw articles (their 'Переводы' sections), ancientrome.ru, CyberLeninka, and O. V. Smyka's published PDFs. Where I could not check a claim, it is marked 'memory' or 'unknown'.

Fragments of the Hellenistic and Alexander historians as a corpus (FGrH/BNJ 117–160: Callisthenes, Chares, Onesicritus, Nearchus, Aristobulus, Cleitarchus, the Ephemerides, Hieronymus of Cardia, Duris, Phylarchus; Arrian's Ta meta Alexandron with its palimpsests; the Heidelberg Epitome). Only Dexippus and the Jewish historians are on the list, yet this is the corpus closest to the editor's own Alexander expertise.

Ancient Greek music theory: Aristides Quintilianus, Cleonides, Bacchius, the Anonymi Bellermann, Bryennius, and the musical papyri/DAGM. None of it is on the list. Russian coverage is thin: Aristides has only II.1–5. Ptolemy's Harmonics with Porphyry's commentary is already done in Russian (Tsypin 2013), so that one should be excluded.

Roman and early Byzantine legal literature beyond the Novels: Theophilus' Paraphrasis Institutionum, Fragmenta Vaticana, Pauli Sententiae, the Collatio, the Syro-Roman Lawbook, and the Basilica scholia (which preserve the commentaries of the 6th-c. law teachers). The Digest exists in Russian; the Greek juristic commentary tradition is almost untouched.
Roman land surveyors (Corpus agrimensorum Romanorum). This is a technical, legal and administrative genre. Russian has only excerpts.

Greek mathematics and mechanics: Pappus' Collection, Eutocius, Hero (Metrica, Dioptra), Serenus, Anthemius, and the Arabic-only Philo of Byzantium and Hero's Mechanics. Only Theon on the Almagest and Proclus' Hypotyposis are on the list.

Greek astrology beyond verse astrology: Vettius Valens, Hephaestion of Thebes, Rhetorius, Dorotheus (Arabic), and the CCAG excerpts. This is a huge body of late antique technical prose with almost no Russian.
Paradoxography (mirabilia): Antigonus of Carystus' Historiarum mirabilium collectio, Apollonius, Phlegon, Ps.-Aristotle's Mirabilia, Isigonus. A distinct Hellenistic genre that is entirely absent.

Late Latin secular and Christian poetry: Merobaudes, Claudian's minor poems, the Anthologia Latina's Vandal poets (Luxorius, Codex Salmasianus), Avitus, Arator, Sedulius, Paulinus of Pella, Proba. Absent. Note that Dracontius and Corippus already exist in Russian (checked).

Greek Christian poetry and centos: Eudocia's Homerocentones and Martyrdom of Cyprian, Dioscorus of Aphrodito, the Romanos kontakia not yet in Russian. Nonnus' Paraphrase already has a full Russian translation (2002), so it should be excluded.
Manichaean and Gnostic sources: the Cologne Mani Codex (Greek), the Coptic Kephalaia, the Psalm-Book and Homilies of Medinet Madi, and Mandaean literature. Entirely missing.

Late-antique Jewish literature beyond Philo and the Hellenistic historians: midrash (Genesis Rabbah, Mekhilta), Targumim, Hekhalot texts, early piyyut (Yannai), and Jewish inscriptions and papyri (CPJ, JIGRE). Russian coverage is patchy and the material is directly relevant to the Graeco-Roman world.
Samaritan literature (Memar Marqe, the Samaritan chronicles): roots in antiquity, essentially no Russian.

The Iranian and Indian Hellenistic East: Bactrian documents, the Sogdian Ancient Letters, the Greek and Aramaic Ashoka edicts (Kandahar), the Yavanajātaka and the Yuga Purāṇa, Gandhari texts, and Middle Persian books with late antique layers (Dēnkard, Bundahišn). These are essential context for Alexander and the Seleucids; the Near East sweep stopped at Mesopotamia and Egypt.
Anatolian and Levantine epigraphy outside cuneiform: Luwian hieroglyphic, Lycian, Lydian and Phoenician/Punic inscriptions, and the Aramaic of Palmyra and Hatra. Absent.
Coptic literature beyond magic: Shenoute, Besa, Coptic martyr acts, the Pachomian dossier. Shenoute is largely untranslated into Russian.
Greek biblical catenae and the exegetical fragments they preserve (Origen, Didymus, Apollinaris, Theodore of Mopsuestia, Severus). Only Procopius' Genesis epitome is listed.

Greek grammatical scholia and Byzantine grammar: the scholia on Dionysius Thrax, Choeroboscus, the Herodian fragments, Theodosius' Canons, the Epimerismi Homerici. This is literally 'scholia', yet it is missing from a project called Neoscholia.

Other major scholia corpora not listed: Sophocles, Aeschylus, Theocritus, Hesiod's Theogony, Lucian (Arethas), Plato (Greene), Thucydides, Demosthenes and Aeschines, Nicander and Oppian. On the Latin side: Servius on the Eclogues and Georgics, Ps.-Acro on Horace, the Scholia Bernensia on Vergil.

Late Latin lexicography and teaching texts: Nonius Marcellus, the Placidus glossary, the bilingual Hermeneumata Pseudodositheana colloquia, and Latin grammarians beyond Terentianus (Diomedes, Charisius, Priscian's Institutiones). Martianus Capella is already in Russian (Shakhov 2019), so it should be excluded.
Agronomy: the Geoponica and its late antique sources (Cassianus Bassus, Anatolius). Only the veterinary Hippiatrica and Pelagonius are listed.

Minor geographers and itineraries: Marcian of Heraclea, the Stadiasmus maris magni, Agathemerus, Ptolemy's Geography catalogues (books 2–7), Latin itineraria (Antonine, Bordeaux), the Ravenna Cosmography.
Byzantine antiquarian texts on late antique Constantinople and its ancient statuary: the Parastaseis syntomoi chronikai, Hesychius Illustrius' Patria, the Patria Konstantinoupoleos.
Native historians writing in Greek (Berossus, Manetho) as a paired dossier. They are relevant to the listed Babylonian and Egyptian material but appear only indirectly.

duplicates: Stephanus of Byzantium, Ethnica appears twice: in the lexicography sweep (unit: Hellenistic city foundations) and in the technical/geography sweep (unit: Alexander's and the Diadochi's foundations). Same work, nearly the same unit; merge.

Stobaeus, Anthology IV appears twice: IV.22–25 in the lexicography sweep (RU:partial) and IV.22–24 in the philosophy sweep (RU:none). The RU statuses conflict. It also overlaps Hierocles' Stobaean excerpts 'On Duties' (inside the Hierocles entry) and the Ps.-Pythagorean household treatises transmitted in Stobaeus IV.28. Merge into one 'Stobaeus on marriage and household' dossier.
Tzetzes, Historiai (Chiliades) appears in the scholia sweep (P3) and the poetry sweep (P5). Different priorities for the same work.
Servius (with Servius Danielis) on the Aeneid appears in the Latin scholia sweep (Aen. 6) and the Latin secular sweep (Aen. 2–12).
Julius Valerius, Res gestae Alexandri Macedonis appears in the Alexander sweep (EN:partial) and the Latin secular sweep (EN:none).

Itinerarium Alexandri and the Metz Epitome with the Liber de morte appear as two separate entries in the Alexander sweep and as one combined entry in the Latin secular sweep, with conflicting EN statuses.
Byzantine Alexander Poem (1388, cod. Marc. gr. 408) appears in the Alexander sweep (EN:unknown) and the poetry sweep (EN:none).
Ps.-Clementine Homilies appear in the fiction sweep (RU:unknown) and the Christian literature sweep (RU:none).
Eusebius, Chronicon Book I appears in the historiography sweep (RU:none) and the Oriental sweep (Armenian version, RU:partial). It is one textual unit: the Greek fragments plus the Armenian.
Pelagonius appears in the Latin sweep (Ars veterinaria) and is also partly inside the technical sweep's Hippiatrica, which includes Pelagonius in Greek. Partial overlap.
The Hellenistic Jewish historians (philosophy sweep) are transmitted almost entirely in Eusebius' Praeparatio Evangelica IX, which the Christian sweep lists separately. Their text overlaps.

The chronographic entries overlap heavily: Hippolytus' Chronicon/Diamerismos is reused in the Chronicon Paschale, the Excerpta Latina Barbari and Synkellos, and most of Africanus' fragments survive in Synkellos. Five entries draw on shared material; plan them as a cluster to avoid duplicate translation.

Not duplicates, but co-dependent clusters to plan together: (a) the Aratus dossier: Scholia in Aratum, Hipparchus' Commentary, Avienus' Aratea; (b) the α-recension family: Greek AR α, Julius Valerius, Armenian AR; (c) Aelian's De natura animalium and Manuel Philes' verse paraphrase of it; (c2) the Alexander papyri entry (P.Oxy. 1798 = FGrH 148) and the proposed Alexander historians corpus; (d) Choricius, Procopius of Gaza's Letters and Procopius of Gaza's Genesis commentary (Gaza school).
